Foxconn (Hon Hai Technology Group, TWSE: 2317) was established in Taiwan in 1974; it is headquartered at No. 2, Ziyou St., Tucheng District, New Taipei City, and operates more than 230 campuses in 24 countries.

faq.q: What liquid cooling does Foxconn offer for AI racks?
faq.a: Through subsidiary Ingrasys: customized rack-level liquid cooling and immersion cooling solutions for data centers, and NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 racks integrated with an in-row CDU solution. This profile repeats only what Ingrasys’ live overview page and Foxconn’s own releases state.

faq.q: What rack capacities does Ingrasys cite for liquid cooling?
faq.a: Ingrasys states that a traditional air-cooled server rack can handle up to 25 kW of heat, whereas a liquid-cooled system can push the limits beyond 100 kW, supporting the increasing component densities of modern data centers.

faq.q: Which NVIDIA platforms does Foxconn integrate with liquid cooling?
faq.a: At OCP Global Summit 2025 (October 14, 2025), Ingrasys showcased the NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 platform integrated with an in-row CDU solution, plus the NVIDIA HGX B300 platform and new MGX servers for enterprise AI.

faq.q: What is Foxconn's legal identity and headquarters?
faq.a: Foxconn is Hon Hai Technology Group, listed on the Taiwan Stock Exchange as TWSE: 2317, established in Taiwan in 1974 and headquartered in Tucheng District, New Taipei City.

profiles.name: Fujitsu
profiles.tagline: Japanese ICT group whose data-center liquid cooling spans FSAS Technologies' Cool-Safe single-phase direct-to-chip systems for PRIMERGY servers (CDU up to 80 kW), the PRIMERGY liquid immersion cooling system, and Fujitsu monitoring/control software for liquid-cooled servers and CDUs developed with Supermicro and Nidec.

productLines.name: Cool-Safe Liquid Cooling
productLines.note: FSAS Technologies' single-phase, closed-loop direct-to-chip cold-plate cooling for AI/HPC: CDU with up to 80 kW cooling capacity, coolant distribution manifolds supporting up to 72 servers per rack, purpose-built PRIMECENTER Rack M2 42U LC, and liquid cooling modules attached directly to CPUs.

productLines.name: PRIMERGY Liquid Immersion Cooling System
productLines.note: Servers fully submerged in a non-conductive, electrically insulating dielectric fluid; a CDU circulates the fluid and transfers heat to coolant water. Fujitsu cites about 40% lower total server-system power versus air cooling and a measured PUE of 1.07; available in Japan since end of November 2018, priced from JPY 20 million excluding ICT hardware.

productLines.name: Liquid cooling monitoring and control software
productLines.note: Fujitsu software for real-time monitoring of liquid-cooled servers and cooling equipment including CDUs; offered as a subscription data-center service starting in Japan in Q1 fiscal 2025, with verification at the Tatebayashi Data Center using Supermicro GPU servers and Nidec CDUs, targeting up to 40% efficiency improvement versus air cooling.

facts.text: April 17, 2025: Fujitsu, Supermicro and Nidec announced a collaboration combining Fujitsu's liquid-cooling monitoring/control software, Supermicro GPU servers and Nidec CDUs (cumulative shipments of 5,000 units as of November 2024), to be tested at Fujitsu's Tatebayashi Data Center, with a subscription datacenter offering starting in Japan in Q1 fiscal 2025.

April 1, 2024: FSAS Technologies Inc. launched under Fujitsu Limited, consolidating Fujitsu's Japanese hardware business, including development, manufacturing, sales and maintenance of PRIMERGY, PRIMEQUEST and ETERNUS servers and storage, with about 7,500 employees.

September 6, 2018: Fujitsu announced the PRIMERGY Liquid Immersion Cooling System, available in Japan from end of November 2018, citing roughly 40% reduction in total server-system power consumption versus air cooling and a measured PUE of 1.07.

faq.q: What is Cool-Safe Liquid Cooling?
faq.a: FSAS Technologies' single-phase, closed-loop direct-to-chip cold-plate system for PRIMERGY servers: a CDU with up to 80 kW cooling capacity, coolant distribution manifolds supporting up to 72 servers per rack, the PRIMECENTER Rack M2 42U LC, and liquid cooling modules attached directly to CPUs.

faq.q: Does Fujitsu offer immersion cooling?
faq.a: Yes. The PRIMERGY Liquid Immersion Cooling System, available in Japan since November 2018, fully submerges servers in a non-conductive dielectric fluid circulated by a CDU; Fujitsu cites about 40% lower server-system power than air cooling and a measured PUE of 1.07.

faq.q: How does Fujitsu manage liquid-cooled infrastructure?
faq.a: Fujitsu's monitoring/control software provides real-time monitoring of liquid-cooled servers and equipment including CDUs. Since April 17, 2025 it is being verified with Supermicro GPU servers and Nidec CDUs at the Tatebayashi Data Center, with a subscription datacenter offering starting in Japan in Q1 fiscal 2025.

faq.q: What is FSAS Technologies' relationship to Fujitsu?
faq.a: FSAS Technologies Inc. launched on April 1, 2024 under Fujitsu Limited, taking over Fujitsu's Japanese server and storage hardware business, including PRIMERGY, PRIMEQUEST and ETERNUS. Fujitsu Limited is listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange as TSE: 6702.

profiles.name: GS Caltex
profiles.tagline: Korean oil refiner and lubricants maker (Kixx brand, GS Tower, Gangnam-gu, Seoul) selling data-center cooling fluids: POE-based Kixx Immersion Fluid S (launched 2023, expanded 2024) and Kixx DLC Fluid PG25 for direct-to-chip cooling, launched October 14, 2025.

productLines.name: Kixx DLC Fluid PG25
productLines.note: Direct liquid cooling fluid made with propylene glycol and organic acid technology (OAT) corrosion-inhibiting additives; circulates through cooling plates to manage CPU and GPU heat in data center servers. Announced October 14, 2025.

productLines.name: Kixx Immersion Fluid S
productLines.note: POE-based immersion cooling fluid for data center servers launched in 2023; lineup expanded in 2024 with S 5 and S 30 (both NSF certified, S 30 with 250 degrees C flash point), S E (biodegradable, 250 degrees C flash point) and S BIO (bio-based).

facts.text: October 14, 2025: GS Caltex launched Kixx DLC Fluid PG25, a propylene glycol direct liquid cooling fluid with OAT corrosion inhibitors. The release also notes immersion fluid supplied to Samsung SDS (2024) and LG Uplus Pyeongchon data center (2025), an immersion cooling system built with Supermicro at its Daejeon R&D Center, and an MOU with GS E&C and SDT on cooling technology.

The Kixx Immersion Fluid S lineup was expanded with variants S 5 and S 30 (both NSF certified; S 30 with a 250 degrees C flash point), S E (biodegradable, 250 degrees C flash point) and S BIO (bio-based).
GS Caltex launched Kixx Immersion Fluid S, a POE-based immersion cooling fluid for data center servers, entering the data-center cooling fluids market.

faq.q: What cooling fluids does GS Caltex offer for data centers?
faq.a: Two lines: Kixx Immersion Fluid S, a POE-based immersion cooling fluid launched in 2023 and expanded in 2024 with NSF-certified, biodegradable and bio-based variants, and Kixx DLC Fluid PG25, a propylene glycol direct liquid cooling fluid with OAT corrosion inhibitors announced October 14, 2025.

faq.q: Where have GS Caltex cooling fluids been demonstrated or supplied?
faq.a: Per the company announcement of October 14, 2025, its immersion cooling fluid was supplied to Samsung SDS data centers in 2024 and to LG Uplus Pyeongchon data center in 2025, and an immersion cooling system was built with Supermicro at GS Caltex Daejeon R&D Center.

faq.q: What is Kixx DLC Fluid PG25 made of?
faq.a: It is a propylene glycol-based fluid with organic acid technology (OAT) corrosion-inhibiting additives, designed to circulate through cooling plates that manage heat from CPUs and GPUs in data center servers.

faq.q: Where is GS Caltex headquartered and is it listed?
faq.a: GS Caltex is headquartered at GS Tower, 508 Nonhyeon-ro, Gangnam-gu, Seoul, South Korea. No stock listing for GS Caltex itself and no confirmed ownership structure were found on the pages opened for this profile (NOT_FOUND).

profiles.name: Kaori
profiles.tagline: Taiwanese brazed plate heat exchanger maker (KAORI HEAT TREATMENT CO., LTD., since 1970, Taoyuan; TPEx: 8996) with a data-center cooling division offering in-row liquid-to-liquid CDUs above 800 kW per unit, in-rack CDUs, single-server cooling and immersion systems of 30-400 kW.

productLines.name: In-row liquid-to-liquid CDUs
productLines.note: In-row CDUs whose brazed plate heat exchangers support over 800 kW of cooling per unit, scalable past 3 MW with parallel units and customizable for thermal loads from 800 kW to 2.5 MW, serving one-to-many cabinet direct-to-chip liquid cooling systems.

productLines.name: In-rack CDUs and single-server cooling
productLines.note: Data-center product family alongside in-row CDUs and immersion: in-rack coolant distribution units using Kaori BPHEs for compact on-demand heat removal, plus single-server liquid cooling, presented under Kaori's Data Center Advanced Liquid Cooling program which claims PUE of 1.1 or lower.

productLines.name: Immersion cooling systems
productLines.note: Customized immersion cooling solutions from 30 kW to 400 kW with centralized temperature control; Kaori cites about 13 MW of immersion cooling deployed and case-study CDU experience from 80 kW to 2 MW, with customized CDU, immersion tank and piping network design.

productLines.name: Brazed plate heat exchangers
productLines.note: Core component and product, designed and manufactured in-house since 1994: stainless steel plates with 99.9% pure copper brazing, standard pressure up to 30 bar (140 bar on request), maximum 200 degrees C, CE (PED) and UL certified.

facts.text: June 23, 2026: Kaori broke ground on a new facility in Qiaotou with production targeted by 2027, and in 2026 it announced participation in OCP APAC Summit 2026 (Taipei, August 11-12) and Super Computing 2026 (Chicago, November).

January 31, 2024: trade press covered Kaori's independently developed large-scale in-row 800 kW liquid-to-liquid CDU for servers and direct-to-chip cold-plate cabinets, designed to manage heat output across multiple cabinets.
Kaori Heat Treatment Co., Ltd. has operated since 1970, building on metal processing and plate heat exchanger technologies; it has designed and manufactured brazed plate heat exchangers since 1994.

faq.q: What CDU capacity does Kaori offer?
faq.a: Kaori in-row liquid-to-liquid CDUs support over 800 kW of cooling per unit and can be scaled past 3 MW with parallel units; the company cites customizable thermal loads from 800 kW to 2.5 MW and case-study CDU experience ranging from 80 kW to 2 MW.

faq.q: Does Kaori provide immersion cooling?
faq.a: Yes. It offers customized immersion cooling solutions from 30 kW to 400 kW with centralized temperature control, and cites roughly 13 MW of immersion cooling deployed, including customized CDU, immersion tank and piping network design.

faq.q: What is Kaori's core technology?
faq.a: Brazed plate heat exchangers, designed and manufactured in-house since 1994: stainless steel plates with 99.9% pure copper brazing, standard pressure up to 30 bar (140 bar on request), maximum 200 degrees C, CE (PED) and UL certified. These BPHEs are key CDU components.

faq.q: Is Kaori expanding capacity?
faq.a: Yes. On June 23, 2026 Kaori announced breaking ground on an NT$3.25 billion facility in Qiaotou, with production targeted by 2027.

profiles.name: KENMEC Mechanical Engineering
profiles.tagline: Taiwanese automation and thermal engineering group (established 1976, Nangang District, Taipei; TPEx: 6125) whose thermal solutions division supplies liquid-to-liquid and liquid-to-air CDUs, rear door heat exchangers, two-phase immersion systems (PUE 1.02), cold plates and manifolds for data centers.

productLines.name: In-cabinet and rack-type CDUs
productLines.note: Liquid-to-liquid and liquid-to-air CDUs in in-cabinet and rack-type formats: in-cabinet L2L with dual pump backup, quick connectors and variable-frequency flow/temperature control; rack-type L2L with built-in heat exchanger and 1+1 backup motor; rack-type L2A with hot-swappable fans, no external chiller, ORv3 cabinet and built-in power shelf/bus bar.

productLines.name: Rear door heat exchangers (RDHx)
productLines.note: Rear-door liquid cooling with no water leakage risk inside the rack, compatibility with various cabinet sizes, optional external fans to raise cooling capacity; listed as deployed at government, telecom, biotech and semiconductor company data centers.

productLines.name: Two-phase immersion cooling
productLines.note: Two-phase immersion system using phase change between gas and liquid with no additional active cooling components; company-stated PUE of 1.02, maintenance without downtime and no dielectric fluid leakage; a second-generation solution underwent real-machine verification with partners at Computex Taipei 2024.

productLines.name: Cold plates and manifolds
productLines.note: Chip cold plates with uniform cooling surface, no water leakage risk and flow channel direction customizable to customer requirements; manifolds offered in standard round and square tube options, customizable per rack design. Coolants offered include mineral oil, coolant and dielectric fluid.

facts.text: May 20, 2025: at Computex 2025 in Taipei, KENMEC jointly showcased AI data center full-lifecycle solutions with Agaruda, combining digital twins, BIM, IoT asset management and CFD thermal simulation, integrating its cooling equipment with AI-based simulation for data center planning.

At Computex Taipei 2024, KENMEC conducted real-machine verification of its second-generation two-phase immersion cooling solution with partners and announced development of a high-efficiency water-to-air Sidecar for AI high-density liquid-cooled server cabinets.

KENMEC was established in July 1976 in Taiwan and renamed KENMEC Mechanical Engineering Co., Ltd. after a March 1987 reorganization; headquarters are in Nangang District, Taipei City, with about 1,000 Taiwan employees and plants in Ruifang, Kaohsiung, Pingzhen, Suzhou, Kunshan and Hanoi.

faq.q: What CDU types does KENMEC offer?
faq.a: Both liquid-to-liquid and liquid-to-air CDUs, in in-cabinet and rack-type formats. Features include dual pump backup and variable-frequency flow/temperature control on the in-cabinet L2L, a built-in heat exchanger with 1+1 backup motor on the rack-type L2L, and an ORv3 rack-type L2A with hot-swappable fans and no external chiller.

faq.q: Does KENMEC provide immersion cooling?
faq.a: Yes. Its two-phase immersion cooling system uses phase change between gas and liquid with no additional active cooling components; the company states a PUE of 1.02, maintenance without downtime and no dielectric fluid leakage. A second-generation solution underwent real-machine verification at Computex Taipei 2024.

faq.q: Where have KENMEC liquid cooling products been deployed?
faq.a: Its applications page lists data center cooling cases at government, telecom, biotech and semiconductor company data centers, using rear door heat exchanger and water-cooled rear door products.

faq.q: What is KENMEC beyond liquid cooling?
faq.a: Founded in 1976 and headquartered in Nangang District, Taipei City, KENMEC Mechanical Engineering (TPEx: 6125) builds whole-plant automation, logistics centers, ASRS and MRT systems, and lists cooling solutions for data center, server, communication, energy and automotive industries among its product lines.

profiles.name: LG Electronics
profiles.tagline: Korean electronics maker LG Electronics (founded 1958, Seoul; KRX: 066570) sells a chip-to-chiller liquid cooling portfolio: cold plates, a 600 kW CDU validated against NVIDIA AI infrastructure standards in July 2026, larger CDU models announced, chillers and DCCM control software, tested at its Pyeongtaek site.

productLines.name: 600 kW Coolant Distribution Unit
productLines.note: CDU validated against NVIDIA AI infrastructure standards in July 2026 after meeting over 100 technical evaluation criteria covering cooling performance, reliability and failover for AI data centers; company-stated temperature control precision of plus or minus 0.25 degrees C; 1 MW, 2.5 MW and 4 MW models announced for sequential validation.

productLines.name: Direct-to-chip cold plates
productLines.note: Direct-to-chip (DTC) cooling delivers coolant to GPUs and CPUs and operates as hybrid cooling alongside air cooling; virtual sensor technology provides real-time monitoring and leak detection across the cooling loop.

productLines.name: Chillers and chip-to-chiller portfolio
productLines.note: Chilled water production with key components including inverters and magnetic bearing compressors produced in-house, sold together with CDUs and cold plates as a chip-to-chiller offering; the Data Center Cooling Control Manager (DCCM) adds predictive control and centralized monitoring via standard communication protocols.

facts.text: July 27, 2026: LG Electronics announced it secured validation for its 600 kW Coolant Distribution Unit against NVIDIA AI infrastructure standards, meeting over 100 technical evaluation criteria on cooling performance, reliability and failover; the same post cites recent project wins at North American hyperscaler facilities and the Sinar Mas SM+ Data Center in Jakarta.

LG operates a dedicated chip-to-chiller validation site in Pyeongtaek, South Korea, testing system-wide transient responses, temperature changes and low-load stability across the whole cooling chain, and has announced plans to seek sequential validation of 1 MW, 2.5 MW and 4 MW CDU models.
LG Electronics dates its founding to 1958 (company site: Since 1958); its cooling announcements are issued from Seoul, South Korea.

faq.q: What CDU capacity has LG Electronics had validated by NVIDIA?
faq.a: A 600 kW Coolant Distribution Unit secured validation against NVIDIA AI infrastructure standards in July 2026 after meeting over 100 technical evaluation criteria covering cooling performance, reliability and failover for high-performance AI data centers.

faq.q: What larger CDU models has LG announced?
faq.a: The company has announced plans to secure validation for 1 MW, 2.5 MW and 4 MW CDU models sequentially. These are announced future models, not yet validated at the time of the July 2026 announcement.

faq.q: What is included in LG's chip-to-chiller approach?
faq.a: Cold plates for direct-to-chip cooling of GPUs and CPUs working as hybrid cooling with air, CDUs, and chillers with in-house-produced inverters and magnetic bearing compressors, plus the Data Center Cooling Control Manager (DCCM) for predictive control and centralized monitoring via standard communication protocols.

faq.q: Where does LG Electronics test its data center cooling?
faq.a: At a dedicated chip-to-chiller validation site in Pyeongtaek, South Korea, which tests system-wide transient responses, temperature changes and low-load stability across the whole cooling chain. The company states temperature control precision of plus or minus 0.25 degrees C, with results that may vary.

profiles.name: Lotes
profiles.tagline: Connector maker in Keelung, Taiwan, producing CPU sockets, memory and I/O connectors, with a Liquid Cooling Solution category of UQD/UQDB and MQD quick-disconnect couplings for cold plate and manifold cooling in AI and hyperscale data centers.

productLines.name: UQD / UQDB
productLines.note: Quick-disconnect coupling families listed under the Liquid Cooling Solution category on the LOTES product site; the category page shows the AUQD0001~0016 product line. The published pages do not state flow-rate or pressure specifications.

productLines.name: MQD
productLines.note: Coupling family featured by LOTES for cold plate and manifold cooling in AI and hyperscale data centers; listed alongside UQD/UQDB in the company's liquid cooling category.

productLines.name: FT
productLines.note: Product family listed in the Liquid Cooling Solution category together with UQD/UQDB and MQD; the company's public pages give no further specifications for it.

facts.text: LOTES published a news item dated June 2, 2026, 'LOTES Powers the Future of AI Factories with NVIDIA MGX', on joining the NVIDIA MGX ecosystem for AI servers.
LOTES received Science Based Targets initiative (SBTi) certification for science-based carbon reduction targets, announced in a company news item dated October 14, 2025.

faq.q: What liquid-cooling interconnects does LOTES offer?
faq.a: The Liquid Cooling Solution category on lotes.cc lists UQD/UQDB quick-disconnect couplings (the category page shows the AUQD0001~0016 line), the MQD family featured for cold plate and manifold cooling in AI and hyperscale data centers, and an FT family; the public pages publish no flow-rate or pressure figures.

faq.q: Is liquid cooling LOTES' core business?
faq.a: No. Founded in 1986 and headquartered in Keelung, Taiwan, LOTES is a connector maker whose catalogue covers CPU sockets, memory connectors, slot/edge-card, I/O and cable assemblies, with liquid cooling couplings as one product category.

faq.q: Where does LOTES trade?
faq.a: LOTES states on its site that it has been publicly listed on the Taiwan Stock Exchange under code 3533 since 2007.

profiles.name: Mitsubishi Electric
profiles.tagline: Electronics and industrial group whose CritiCool line serves data center cooling with MECH-iC oil-free centrifugal chillers for warm-water operation, MEWALL fanwall thermal walls and DX-P wall-mounted direct-expansion units, built with group company Mitsubishi Electric Hydronics & IT Cooling Systems S.p.A. of Italy.

productLines.name: MECH-iC chiller
productLines.note: Compact, oil-free centrifugal chiller system engineered for warm-water operation; published dimensional drawings cover 350-ton and 500-ton models. The vendor page gives no kW or refrigerant figures.

productLines.name: MEWALL thermal wall
productLines.note: Thermal wall (fanwall) cooling line; model drawings reference 402 and 462 fanwall outlines. The vendor page describes space and energy-efficiency benefits without publishing capacity numbers.

productLines.name: CritiCool DX-P
productLines.note: Wall-mounted direct-expansion units for pre-fabricated modular data centers and container cooling, in 10 kW, 20 kW and 40 kW nominal sizes (34,100-149,000 Btu/h), upflow or downflow; the 40 kW model is offered only in downflow with inverter compressor, and an optional economizer extends operating range to -40 degrees F.

facts.text: On July 30, 2026, Mitsubishi Electric announced MEHITS US, Inc., established in August 2026 in Mason, Ohio under Mitsubishi Electric US Holdings, converting part of an existing site in Mason to produce IT cooling equipment from April 2027, with plans to expand the lineup to liquid-cooling-compatible equipment.

On July 14, 2026 Mitsubishi Electric announced the acquisition of the APAC and COMPAC groups (Utrecht Province, Netherlands), HVAC sales, installation and maintenance companies whose experience includes designing, selling, installing and maintaining data center server room cooling systems, in order to grow its data center cooling business in Europe

faq.q: What products make up CritiCool data center cooling?
faq.a: MECH-iC compact oil-free centrifugal chillers for warm-water operation (published drawings for 350-ton and 500-ton models), MEWALL thermal walls (402 and 462 fanwall outlines) and DX-P wall-mounted direct-expansion units in 10, 20 and 40 kW sizes with an optional economizer rated to -40 degrees F.

faq.q: Is Mitsubishi Electric adding US production for data center cooling?
faq.a: Yes, per its July 30, 2026 release: MEHITS US, Inc. in Mason, Ohio was established in August 2026, converting part of an existing site to make IT cooling equipment from April 2027, and the lineup is planned to expand to liquid-cooling-compatible equipment.

faq.q: Where is Mitsubishi Electric based and how is it listed?
faq.a: The company's July 30, 2026 release was issued in Tokyo and states it trades on TOKYO as 6503. The pages opened for this profile did not show a founding year, so it is recorded as NOT_FOUND.

profiles.name: Mitsubishi Heavy Industries
profiles.tagline: Industrial group whose data center offering includes a 12 ft, 40 kVA-class container-type data center combining immersion, air and water cooling, container-type immersion cooling technology demonstrated with KDDI and NESIC since 2021, and one-stop power, cooling and monitoring solutions for edge data centers.

productLines.name: DIAVAULT edge data centers
productLines.note: On-premise edge data center brand launched in February 2026 for factories, research sites and other industrial locations, covering installations from small scale to multi-megawatt inference data centers; the demonstration facility at the Yokohama Hardtech Hub cools AI GPU servers with two-phase direct-to-chip cooling

productLines.name: Container-type data center (40 kVA-class, 12 ft)
productLines.note: Simultaneously houses servers using immersion cooling (25 kVA), air cooling (8 kVA) and water cooling (8 kVA); reserves a 1.4 m x 1.3 m interior service space; expected PUE 1.05 for immersion alone and 1.14 combined, in a 40-degree C environment, per the October 2023 announcement.

productLines.name: Container-type immersion cooling data center
productLines.note: The program under development since 2021 with KDDI and NEC Networks & System Integration Corporation, aimed at small containerized data centers that cool servers with liquid; the 40 kVA-class hybrid container announced in 2023 is its successor.

productLines.name: Data center one-stop solutions
productLines.note: MHI positions itself as a single point of contact for highly reliable power supply, cooling and monitoring systems with integrated control for data centers, including micro-edge facilities processing data at the network periphery.

facts.text: Launched DIAVAULT, a brand for its on-premise edge data centers for industry, on February 24, 2026, and opened a demonstration AI data center at its Yokohama Hardtech Hub whose GPU servers are cooled by two-phase direct-to-chip cooling

On October 4, 2023, MHI announced the 40 kVA-class 12 ft container-type data center with immersion/air-cooled hybrid cooling (immersion 25 kVA, air 8 kVA, water 8 kVA), with demonstration testing at the Yokohama Hardtech Hub and commercialization planned by the end of fiscal 2023.

A March 29, 2022 MHI release cited on the company's news page reports a 43% reduction in server power consumption with a container-type data center using liquid-cooled servers, in trial operation at the KDDI Oyama Technical Center aiming for commercial availability in FY2024.

MHI notes that since 2021 it has conducted demonstration experiments with KDDI Corporation and NEC Networks & System Integration Corporation toward practical container-type data centers that use an immersion cooling system with liquid to cool servers in Japan.

faq.q: What is MHI's container-type data center?
faq.a: A 12 ft, 40 kVA-class container that simultaneously houses servers using immersion cooling (25 kVA), air cooling (8 kVA) and water cooling (8 kVA), with 1.4 m x 1.3 m of interior service space; in a 40-degree C environment the expected PUE is 1.05 for immersion alone and 1.14 combined.

faq.q: Who has MHI worked with on immersion cooling?
faq.a: Since June 2021, MHI, KDDI and NEC Networks & System Integration Corporation (NESIC) have run demonstration experiments on container-type immersion cooling data centers; a March 29, 2022 release cited by MHI reported a 43% server power-consumption reduction in trial operation at the KDDI Oyama Technical Center.

faq.q: When was the hybrid container announced?
faq.a: October 4, 2023; MHI planned to commercialize the 40 kVA-class unit by the end of fiscal 2023 after demonstration testing at the Yokohama Hardtech Hub, with Dell Technologies Japan providing a verification server and NESIC verifying IT equipment installation and server maintenance procedures.

profiles.name: MSI
profiles.tagline: Computing hardware company (founded 1986) whose Enterprise Platform Solutions include a 21-inch 44OU OCP ORv3 liquid-cooled rack with an integrated 100 kW liquid-to-liquid CDU, liquid-cooled NVIDIA MGX GPU servers, and DC-MHS multi-node platforms for AI and cloud data centers.

productLines.name: 21-inch 44OU ORv3 Liquid-Cooled Rack
productLines.note: Supports up to 100 kW deployments with an integrated liquid-to-liquid Coolant Distribution Unit; configurable with 28x 1OU2N Open Compute multi-node systems, using 48V busbar power distribution for high-density AI infrastructure.

productLines.name: CG681-S6093 (NVIDIA MGX)
productLines.note: Liquid-cooled 6U dual-socket AMD EPYC platform supporting up to 8 NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Liquid Cooled Edition GPUs, 32 DDR5 DIMMs and NVIDIA ConnectX-8 SuperNICs with up to 8x 400 Gbps networking, for AI training and HPC.

productLines.name: CD281-S4051-X4 (DC-MHS)
productLines.note: Liquid-cooled 2OU 4-node 21-inch Open Compute platform; each node supports one AMD EPYC 9005 processor, 12 DDR5 DIMMs and 4 E1.S NVMe bays, for AI inference and cloud-native infrastructure.

productLines.name: XpertStation WS300 (NVIDIA DGX Station)
productLines.note: Desktop AI supercomputer on NVIDIA DGX Station architecture with the GB300 Grace Blackwell Ultra Desktop Superchip, up to 748 GB coherent memory, 7.1 TB/s HBM3e bandwidth and a liquid-cooled thermal design in a deskside form factor.

facts.text: On June 2, 2026, MSI announced at COMPUTEX 2026 its 21-inch 44OU ORv3 liquid-cooled rack architecture with integrated liquid-to-liquid CDU (up to 100 kW), liquid-cooled NVIDIA MGX servers including the CG681-S6093, and DC-MHS platforms, stating it is extending MGX collaboration toward next-generation Vera Rubin rack-scale platforms.
In its CloudFest 2025 release (March 18, 2025) MSI states that its CD270-S4051-X4 2U 4-node server has a modular architecture that supports air cooling up to 400 W or liquid cooling up to 500 W

faq.q: What liquid-cooled rack does MSI offer?
faq.a: The 21-inch 44OU ORv3 liquid-cooled rack architecture supports up to 100 kW deployments with an integrated liquid-to-liquid CDU, can be configured with 28x 1OU2N Open Compute multi-node systems, and uses 48V busbar power distribution for large-scale AI infrastructure.

faq.q: Which liquid-cooled servers were shown at COMPUTEX 2026?
faq.a: The CG681-S6093 liquid-cooled 6U dual-socket AMD EPYC platform with up to 8 NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Liquid Cooled Edition GPUs and 8x 400 Gbps networking; the liquid-cooled CD281-S4051-X4 2OU 4-node DC-MHS platform; and the XpertStation WS300 desktop AI supercomputer with a liquid-cooled thermal design.

faq.q: Is MSI a listed company?
faq.a: MSI (Micro-Star International) states on its about page that it was founded in 1986 and has grown from motherboards into servers, automotive electronics and AI. The official pages opened for this profile did not show a stock listing code or headquarters city, so those fields are recorded as NOT_FOUND.

profiles.name: Nidec
profiles.tagline: Electric motor manufacturer headquartered in Kyoto that has built a data center liquid cooling line: in-rack CDUs up to 300 kW in 4U, an in-row CDU, quick disconnects and manifolds, and a prototype 2 MW-class Project Deschutes CDU compliant with Google's Open Compute Project specification.

productLines.name: In-Rack CDU
productLines.note: Four generations: Gen1.0 EIA 200 kW, Gen2.0 EIA 250 kW, Gen2.5 OCP 250 kW and Gen3.0 OCP 300 kW, in a 4U form factor; Gen2.5 and Gen3.0 are OCP ORv3 rack compliant with 51VDC busbar input, N+1 redundant pumps and control units, and hot-swappable components; managed via Redfish.

productLines.name: Project Deschutes CDU (prototype)
productLines.note: Prototype coolant distribution unit compliant with Google's Open Compute Project specification: 2 MW-class cooling capacity and 80 PSI high pressure to drive high-performance cold plates, a low approach temperature design, and an IEEE 519 ultra-low harmonic distortion VFD; under development toward commercial release.

productLines.name: CDU In-Row, Quick Disconnect & Manifold
productLines.note: Lineup items on Nidec's liquid cooling site alongside the in-rack units; the company describes chillers, piping and CDUs as fully integrated, cites independently developed compact high-performance CDU pumps, and states over 13 kpcs of in-rack CDUs shipped globally.

facts.text: Nidec's liquid cooling lineup page lists its CDU In-Rack, CDU In-Row and Quick Disconnect & Manifold products for OCP Global Summit 2026 and Data Center World Asia 2026, and states a cumulative total of over 13 kpcs of In-Rack CDUs shipped globally.

On December 3, 2025, Nidec announced the development of a prototype Project Deschutes CDU compliant with the Google Open Compute Project specification, exhibited at SC25 in St. Louis in November 2025; the company says it is accelerating development toward commercial release and will engage with the OCP community.

faq.q: What CDUs does Nidec sell today?
faq.a: The In-Rack CDU line spans four generations: Gen1.0 EIA at 200 kW, Gen2.0 EIA at 250 kW, Gen2.5 OCP at 250 kW and Gen3.0 OCP at 300 kW, all in a 4U form factor, with OCP ORv3 compliance and 51VDC busbar input on Gen2.5 and Gen3.0, N+1 redundant pumps and hot-swappable critical components.

faq.q: What is the Project Deschutes CDU?
faq.a: A prototype coolant distribution unit compliant with Google's Open Compute Project specification, announced December 3, 2025 and exhibited at SC25: 2 MW-class cooling capacity, 80 PSI operating pressure, a low approach temperature design and an IEEE 519 ultra-low harmonic distortion VFD. Nidec describes it as a prototype and says development continues toward commercial release.

faq.q: Which racks do the in-rack CDUs target?
faq.a: Per Nidec's product page, Gen1.0 targets racks with a single NVIDIA HGX B200, Gen2.0 a single HGX B300, Gen2.5 the NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 and MGX servers, and Gen3.0 the latest industry GPUs.

profiles.name: Panasonic
profiles.tagline: Electronics group whose Heating & Ventilation A/C Company launched a liquid cooling systems business for generative AI data centers in Europe in March 2026, offering 400 kW and 800 kW CDUs and R1234ze(E) free-cooling chillers, built on its 2023 acquisition of Italy's Tecnair.

productLines.name: Coolant Distribution Units (400 kW / 800 kW)
productLines.note: Two CDU models at 400 kW and 800 kW for generative AI data centers in Europe, with orders accepted from March 4, 2026; CDU models of 1,200 kW and above are under development, with order acceptance slated to begin within March 2026 per the announcement.

productLines.name: Free-cooling chillers (800 kW / 1,200 kW)
productLines.note: Two free-cooling chiller models at 800 kW and 1,200 kW using R1234ze(E), a low-GWP refrigerant with GWP of 1; free cooling uses outdoor temperatures up to 10 degrees C to generate chilled water.

productLines.name: Hybrid air and liquid cooling systems
productLines.note: Combined air and liquid cooling offering that Panasonic states cuts power consumption and footprint versus the individual approaches; air-side close control units come from Tecnair, and targets include hyperscale, colocation and edge data centers.

facts.text: On March 4, 2026, Panasonic announced its liquid cooling systems business for generative AI data centers in Europe, accepting orders from the same date for 400 kW and 800 kW CDUs and 800 kW and 1,200 kW free-cooling chillers on R1234ze(E), with 1,200 kW-and-above CDUs under development.

Panasonic acquired Italy-based Tecnair S.p.A. in 2023, whose close control air-conditioning units (CCUs) for air cooling form the basis of the European data center cooling expansion announced in March 2026.

faq.q: What liquid cooling systems does Panasonic sell for AI data centers?
faq.a: Coolant distribution units in 400 kW and 800 kW models plus free-cooling chillers in 800 kW and 1,200 kW models using R1234ze(E) refrigerant (GWP 1); CDUs of 1,200 kW and above are under development. Orders in Europe have been accepted since March 4, 2026.

faq.q: How do the chillers save energy?
faq.a: The free-cooling chillers use outdoor temperatures up to 10 degrees C to generate chilled water, and Panasonic states that combining air cooling (close control units) with liquid cooling cuts power consumption and footprint compared with using either approach alone.

faq.q: What is behind Panasonic's European cooling business?
faq.a: Panasonic acquired Italy-based Tecnair S.p.A. in 2023, whose close control air-conditioning units form the basis of the European data center cooling expansion; the liquid cooling business targets hyperscalers, colocation and edge data centers.

profiles.name: PKI
profiles.tagline: Korean total solution provider, active in semiconductor and display equipment, materials and components, that integrates direct liquid cooling and single/two-phase immersion cooling systems for high-density server data centers and HPC, as exclusive distributor of LiquidStack in Korea.

productLines.name: Direct Liquid Cooling (DLC) integration
productLines.note: System integration services for direct liquid cooling aimed at performance and energy efficiency in high-density server data centers and high-performance computing environments, per the company's AI liquid cooling business overview.

productLines.name: Immersion cooling integration (1PIC / 2PIC)
productLines.note: System integration for single-phase immersion cooling (1PIC) and two-phase immersion cooling (2PIC); PKI supplied a commercial-scale 48U immersion cooling tank used for testing and validation under near-real-world commercial conditions.

productLines.name: LiquidStack products in Korea
productLines.note: PKI describes itself as LiquidStack's official partner and the exclusive distributor of LiquidStack in Korea, delivering liquid cooling solutions for AI data centers with local engineering support, and runs liquid cooling R&D proof-of-concept projects with domestic and international partners.

facts.text: In April 2026 Korean trade press described PKI as LiquidStack’s official distributor and partner in Korea, with business covering direct liquid cooling (CDU) solutions for AI data centers and liquid-cooling design for high-power GPU environments, ahead of HVAC KOREA 2026 (May 13-15, Coex)

An August 26, 2025 industry article describes PKI as LiquidStack's official Korean partner and a core partner in Samsung Electronics' qualification of Chemours' Opteon two-phase immersion cooling fluid, described as Samsung's first approved two-phase fluid; PKI provided a commercial-scale 48U immersion tank, and SSD testing met all compatibility goals.

faq.q: What does PKI provide for data center liquid cooling?
faq.a: PKI provides system integration for direct liquid cooling (DLC) and for single-phase and two-phase immersion cooling (1PIC, 2PIC) in high-density server data centers and HPC environments, and distributes LiquidStack products in Korea with local engineering support.

faq.q: What is PKI's relationship with LiquidStack?
faq.a: PKI's own site describes it as LiquidStack's official partner and the exclusive distributor of LiquidStack in Korea, delivering liquid cooling solutions for AI data centers; it also runs liquid cooling R&D proof-of-concept projects with domestic and international partners.

faq.q: What two-phase fluid work involved PKI?
faq.a: An August 26, 2025 industry article describes PKI as a core partner in Samsung Electronics' qualification of Chemours' Opteon two-phase immersion fluid, Samsung's first approved two-phase fluid; PKI supplied a commercial-scale 48U immersion tank and testing supported SSD compatibility goals.

profiles.name: Quanta Computer
profiles.tagline: ODM established in 1988 and headquartered in Taoyuan City, whose QCT (Quanta Cloud Technology) brand sells rack-scale AI infrastructure including QoolRack direct-to-chip liquid cooling racks with in-rack CDUs and fully liquid-cooled NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 platforms.

productLines.name: QoolRack liquid-to-air (L2A)
productLines.note: Rack-level direct-to-chip cold plate cooling with an in-rack CDU and rear-door heat exchanger; 30U of space between the CDU and a top-of-rack management switch housing up to 15 QuantaGrid D54Q-2U servers; per-slot TDP 700 W with 800 W-plus shown in tests; PUE down to 1.07 with unchilled air.

productLines.name: QoolRack liquid-to-liquid (L2L)
productLines.note: Variant for sites with existing hot and cold manifold piping; same direct-to-chip rack architecture with in-rack CDU. The February 2023 article reports rack-level cooling power cut by nearly 70% (up to 66.8%) versus air cooling, with a DC-SCM module in the CDU.

productLines.name: QoolRack Sidecar
productLines.note: Liquid-to-air cooling accessory for NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 and HGX 8-GPU accelerated racks, presented in May 2025; integrates into existing air-cooled data centers without infrastructure modifications and improves PUE.

productLines.name: Liquid-cooled AI servers
productLines.note: QuantaGrid D75U-1U for the NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 rack-scale system: fully liquid-cooled, 72 GPUs unified via NVLink Switch, four ConnectX-8 SuperNICs at 800 Gb/s each, BlueField-3 DPU; and the liquid-cooled QuantaGrid D75L-2U for HGX B300.

facts.text: On May 19, 2025, QCT announced at COMPUTEX 2025 the fully liquid-cooled QuantaGrid D75U-1U for NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 and the liquid-cooled QuantaGrid D75L-2U for HGX B300, plus the QoolRack Sidecar liquid-to-air accessory for GB300 NVL72 and HGX 8-GPU racks.

QCT's QoolRack article of February 2, 2023 describes liquid-to-air and liquid-to-liquid direct-to-chip racks with in-rack CDU and DC-SCM management, reporting rack-level cooling power reductions of nearly 70% (up to 66.8%) versus air cooling and PUE of 1.07 with unchilled air.
Quanta Computer was established in 1988 and its stock was listed on the Taiwan Stock Exchange on January 8, 1999, per the company's official information page.

faq.q: What is QoolRack?
faq.a: QCT's rack-level direct-to-chip liquid cooling line: a liquid-to-air rack with an in-rack CDU and a liquid-to-liquid rack for sites with existing hot/cold manifold piping. The February 2023 article reports PUE down to 1.07 on unchilled air and rack-level cooling power cut by up to 66.8% versus air cooling.

faq.q: How is a QoolRack liquid-to-air rack configured?
faq.a: The L2A rack offers 30U of space between the bottom in-rack CDU and a top-of-rack management switch, housing up to 15 QuantaGrid D54Q-2U servers with per-slot TDP of 700 W (800 W-plus shown in tests), and the CDU includes a DC-SCM module.

faq.q: What did QCT show at COMPUTEX 2025?
faq.a: On May 19, 2025, QCT announced the fully liquid-cooled QuantaGrid D75U-1U for NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 (72 GPUs on NVLink, four 800 Gb/s ConnectX-8 SuperNICs), the liquid-cooled D75L-2U for HGX B300, and the QoolRack Sidecar that adds liquid-to-air cooling to GB300 NVL72 and HGX 8-GPU racks without infrastructure modifications.

profiles.name: ToneCooling

productLines.name: GB200 direct-to-chip cold plate kit

productLines.name: GB300 direct-to-chip cold plate kit

facts.text: ToneCooling's website (page dated October 2026) publishes direct-to-chip cold plate test figures for NVIDIA GB200 kits (1200 W + 1200 W + 300 W at 2.5 L/min, 35 ± 5 kPa) and GB300 kits (1,066.94 W at 1.7 L/min, 0.0133/0.0130 degrees C/W thermal resistance), and lists a US entity, ToneCooling Texas LLC, alongside European and Australian entities.

faq.q: What does ToneCooling make?
faq.a: Custom direct-to-chip cold plates for GPUs and CPUs (GB200/GB300 kits, H200, AMD SP5, Intel/AMD platforms), cold plate assembly with manifold, cooling distribution units and thermal management systems for data centers, per its website.

faq.q: What performance does ToneCooling publish for its GB200 and GB300 kits?
faq.a: The site's test data shows the GB200 kit handling 1200 W + 1200 W + 300 W at 2.5 L/min and 35 ± 5 kPa, and the GB300 kit at 1,066.94 W GPU heat load at 1.7 L/min with 0.0133/0.0130 degrees C/W thermal resistance (test data last updated April 2025).

faq.q: Where is ToneCooling based and how large is it?
faq.a: Headquartered in Boluo, Huizhou, Guangdong, China, with a 30,000 m2 facility and about 200 employees, founded in 2004; the site also lists ToneCooling Texas LLC in the United States plus European and Australian entities.

faq.q: Is ToneCooling publicly listed?
faq.a: The site describes the company as a private national high-tech enterprise with no stock listing mentioned. Caution: the TPEx 7892 listing named in some references belongs to a different, similarly-named Taiwanese liquid cooling company, not tonecooling.com.

profiles.name: Wiwynn

productLines.name: Advanced cooling technology portfolio

productLines.name: OCP Global Summit 2026 thermal hardware

facts.text: On October 20, 2026, Wiwynn published a recap of its OCP Global Summit 2026 presence, covering thermal demos including diamond-based microchannel cooling, a 6 kW double-sided cold plate with cavity PCBA and VPD, and a lightweight cold plate with inner manifold design, alongside NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 and AMD Helios rack-scale systems.

faq.a: Its advanced cooling page covers cold plate liquid cooling, two-phase immersion cooling and a universal cooling management system, and the site lists an Air-Assisted Liquid Cooling Solution technology topic; the page cites saving 90% cooling energy and 9K+ OCP racks per quarter.

profiles.name: UfiSpace

productLines.name: S9331-64HO3L liquid-cooled switch
productLines.note: 102.4 Tbps switch with 64 x 1.6T OSFP ports in a 2OU ORv3 form factor, powered by the Broadcom Tomahawk 6 ASIC and liquid-cooled; demonstrated live at OCP Global Summit 2026 operating with a Cooling Distribution Unit (CDU) for real-time cooling validation of 1.6T AI fabric thermal feasibility.

productLines.name: Open networking and data center switch portfolio
productLines.note: Disaggregated networking hardware and software including cell site gateways, aggregation and core/edge routers, data center switches spanning 1G-800G (with 1.6T stated as in development), AI networking platforms, fronthaul multiplexers and NetGence software for telecom and cloud/data center markets.

facts.text: In a press release dated October 14, 2026, UfiSpace announced a live liquid-cooling demonstration at OCP Global Summit 2026 (October 12-15, San Jose, California, booth D19): the S9331-64HO3L 102.4 Tbps, 64-port 1.6T OSFP, 2OU ORv3 switch operating with a CDU to validate thermal feasibility for 1.6T AI fabric networks.

The same October 2026 release states the S9331-64HO3L is powered by the Broadcom Tomahawk 6 ASIC and runs with a Cooling Distribution Unit (CDU) for real-time cooling validation, framing liquid cooling as a response to extreme power densities and strict thermal constraints in AI data centers.

faq.q: What did UfiSpace demonstrate at OCP Global Summit 2026?
faq.a: A live liquid-cooling platform: the S9331-64HO3L, a 102.4 Tbps switch with 64 x 1.6T OSFP ports in a 2OU ORv3 form factor, operating with a CDU for real-time cooling validation, announced October 14, 2026 (summit held October 12-15, 2026, San Jose, booth D19).

faq.q: Why is UfiSpace applying liquid cooling to switches?
faq.a: Per the company's release, AI workloads push data centers toward extreme power densities and strict thermal constraints, and the 1.6T transition requires ecosystem alignment across silicon, optics, thermal management and NOS partners; validating liquid cooling feasibility lets partners and customers design future AI data centers with confidence.

faq.q: Which silicon and switch chip does the liquid-cooled switch use?
faq.a: The S9331-64HO3L is powered by the Broadcom Tomahawk 6 ASIC, per the October 2026 announcement.

productLines.name: Cooling fans and thermal modules

profiles.name: Global Standard Technology (GST)

facts.text: On 12 November 2026 Shinsung E&G announced an all-in-one server-and-cooling AIO product at Data Center Korea: a vertically integrated module combining a cooling unit with server racks, supporting up to 8 racks per module and 16-140 kW per rack, with air cooling and direct liquid cooling (DLC) for staged expansion as heat loads grow.

profiles.name: Amphenol
profiles.tagline: Amphenol Industrial Operations, based in Endicott, New York and part of interconnect manufacturer Amphenol, supplies quick-disconnect and blind-mate liquid cooling connectors (UQD/UQDB, MQD, SHQD, LQC, BMQC) used in direct-to-chip cooling loops from server trays to CDU source lines in AI data centers.

productLines.name: UQD / UQDB quick disconnects
productLines.note: Push-pull UQD and blind-mate UQDB connectors stated to meet OCP Universal Quick Disconnect specs; offered in OCP sizes 02, 04, 06 and 08, inline or right-angle, barb or threaded; operating pressure 0-0.6 MPa with safe maximum 2 MPa; stainless steel housings and dry-break bidirectional shut-off valves.

productLines.name: SHQD source-line connectors
productLines.note: High-flow source-line quick disconnects for CDU-to-manifold runs, available in 1 in, 1.5 in and 2 in sizes with rated flow up to 800 L/min, dual interlock safety features, and thread, hose barb or sanitary flange terminations.

productLines.name: MQD compact quick disconnects
productLines.note: Compact push-pull quick disconnects for space-constrained computer-tray cooling loops, in sizes 02, 03 and 04 with straight and 90-degree versions, low flow resistance, corrosion-resistant materials and QR-code traceability.

productLines.name: LQC and BMQC connectors
productLines.note: Screw-to-connect LQC connectors for higher-flow cold plate and manifold loops, and BMQC blind-mate connectors tolerant to misalignment for rack-level Open Rack V3 installations.

facts.text: Amphenol Industrial Operations expanded its liquid cooling connector portfolio for AI data centers: MQD compact disconnects in sizes 02, 03 and 04, UQD/UQDB Rev 2.0 with more fully defined geometry and improved flow performance, and SHQD source-line connectors rated up to 800 L/min for CDU-to-manifold lines.

Announced launch of the UQD and UQDB liquid cooling connector series meeting OCP Universal Quick Disconnect specifications: four standardized OCP sizes (02, 04, 06, 08), inline or right-angle body styles, barb or threaded terminations, 0-0.6 MPa operating pressure with a safe maximum of 2 MPa.

faq.q: Which OCP specification do Amphenol Industrial's liquid cooling connectors follow?
faq.a: The UQD and UQDB series are stated to meet OCP Universal Quick Disconnect specifications and are offered in the four standardized OCP sizes 02, 04, 06 and 08; the UQD/UQDB Rev 2.0 update aligns with updated Open Compute Project requirements for high-performance liquid cooling systems.

faq.q: What flow do the SHQD source-line connectors support?
faq.a: SHQD connectors are offered in 1 in, 1.5 in and 2 in sizes with a rated flow of up to 800 L/min and dual interlock safety features, with thread, hose barb or sanitary flange terminations for CDU-to-manifold connections.

faq.q: What coolants can be used with these connectors?
faq.a: The connectors are compatible with deionized water, ethylene glycol and propylene glycol coolants, with stainless steel housings and EPDM-based aerospace-grade seal options (FKM and FMVQ also offered).

faq.q: Who offers these connectors and from where?
faq.a: The liquid cooling connector families are offered by Amphenol Industrial Operations, based in Endicott, New York, part of Amphenol.

profiles.name: API Heat Transfer
profiles.tagline: API Heat Transfer, a heat exchanger manufacturer with US roots in Buffalo, New York (company formed 1962, heritage to 1947), supplies gasketed plate, shell-and-tube, brazed and dry-cooler heat exchangers for data center liquid cooling, including direct-to-chip, rear-door and immersion architectures.

productLines.name: SIGMA M186 gasketed plate heat exchanger
productLines.note: Plate-and-frame unit supporting up to 15 MW of cooling capacity per unit, positioned for AI, HPC and high-density data center cooling across water-side free cooling and primary loop duties.

productLines.name: Shell and tube heat exchangers
productLines.note: Custom shell and tube, extended-surface, U-tube and Type 500 units with capacities up to 30 MW, used for large liquid cooling loop duties in data centers.

productLines.name: Brazed and bar-plate heat exchangers
productLines.note: Aluminum brazed plate and T-bar units up to 3 MW, including compact colocation cooling modules for space-constrained data center installs.

productLines.name: V-Bank dry coolers
productLines.note: Dry heat rejection packages delivering 2.5+ MW per site in roughly 500 sq ft, used at immersion cooling and crypto data center sites.

facts.text: Launched the SIGMA M186 heat exchanger for large-scale data center cooling: a gasketed plate-and-frame unit purpose-engineered for hyperscale and AI data center applications.

faq.q: How much cooling can one SIGMA M186 unit support?
faq.a: The SIGMA M186 gasketed plate-and-frame heat exchanger supports up to 15 MW of cooling capacity per unit and is positioned for AI, HPC and high-density data center cooling, covering water-side free cooling and primary loop scenarios.

faq.q: Which data center cooling architectures do API heat exchangers support?
faq.a: The company states its primary heat exchanger technologies are compatible with direct-to-chip, rear-door and immersion cooling architectures, as well as CDU and liquid loop isolation.

profiles.name: Armstrong Fluid Technology
profiles.tagline: Armstrong Fluid Technology supplies Design Envelope pumps and the Design Envelope EVERCOOL integrated automation platform for data center chiller plants, positioned for rapid deployment in mission-critical cooling with hot-standby redundancy and brand-agnostic control of chillers, towers and pumps.

productLines.name: Design Envelope EVERCOOL
productLines.note: Automation and optimization for air-cooled or water-cooled chilled water systems in data centers; meets Uptime Institute requirements for all Tiers; controls up to six chillers, six cooling towers, six chilled water and six condenser water pumps with redundant sensors and valves; cites up to 30% less site work and up to 40% lower cooling plant energy costs.

productLines.name: Design Envelope pumps

productLines.name: Plant optimization peripherals

Announced the launch of Design Envelope EVERCOOL, an automation platform for mission-critical cooling that meets Uptime Institute requirements for data centers, reduces site commissioning time by up to 30% and coordinates cooling system operation to cut energy costs by up to 40%.

faq.q: What is Design Envelope EVERCOOL?
faq.a: An integrated automation and optimization solution for data center chiller plants. It is pre-engineered, pre-programmed and pre-tested, works with all brands of chillers, pumps and automation systems, and meets Uptime Institute requirements for all Tiers of data centers.

faq.q: How large a plant can EVERCOOL control?
faq.a: The platform controls up to six chillers, six cooling towers, six chilled water pumps and six condenser water pumps with redundant sensors and valves, and the company states there are no limitations in plant size and cooling capacity.

faq.q: What savings does Armstrong cite for EVERCOOL?
faq.a: Armstrong cites up to 25% shorter design time, up to 30% less site work, up to 40% lower cooling plant energy costs using demand-based control and patented parallel control optimization, and up to 25% lower equipment life cycle cost via Active Performance Management.

faq.q: Where is Armstrong Fluid Technology based?
faq.a: The company issues its official announcements from Toronto, Ontario, Canada, as shown by the Toronto datelines on its media blog releases.

profiles.name: AAON (BASX)

productLines.name: BASX Coolant Distribution Units (CDUs)
productLines.note: Liquid-to-liquid CDUs regulating coolant flow, temperature and pressure between IT equipment and facility water loops; design capacity starting at 2 MW with stated plans to exceed 8 MW, N+1 redundancy, stainless steel build and 25- and 50-micron filtration to protect cold plates; liquid-to-air retrofit cited at roughly 20-50 kW per rack.

productLines.name: BASX free cooling chillers
productLines.note: Heat rejection for the coolant loop that uses ambient outdoor conditions when possible to reduce mechanical cooling demand, integrated with BASX CDUs as a complete direct-to-chip ecosystem.

productLines.name: Direct-to-chip rack components
productLines.note: Cold plates and rack manifolds listed by BASX as components of its direct-to-chip liquid cooling systems, paired with the CDU and heat rejection equipment.

productLines.name: Data center air-side equipment
productLines.note: Computer room air handlers (CRAHs), air-cooled systems and direct evaporative coolers for data centers, slated for production at the new Memphis, Tennessee facility alongside liquid-to-liquid and liquid-to-air CDUs.

facts.text: Production of the BASX-brand custom thermal management systems ordered for a liquid cooling deployment was slated to start in early 2025 at Longview, Texas, in existing and newly constructed facilities, with the majority of deliveries in the first half of 2025.

Announced purchase of a 787,000 sq ft facility in Memphis, Tennessee to expand production capacity for the data center market, slated to make air-cooled systems, CRAHs, direct evaporative coolers and liquid-to-liquid plus liquid-to-air CDUs, with limited production expected in early 2025.

Announced it was awarded liquid cooling data center orders under the BASX brand, including a custom-designed thermal management system supporting a liquid cooling deployment for a hyperscale-type customer's data center.

faq.q: Under which brand does AAON sell data center liquid cooling equipment?
faq.a: AAON sells data center cooling equipment under its BASX brand. AAON is headquartered in Tulsa, Oklahoma, was founded in 1988 and trades on NASDAQ under the ticker AAON; BASX liquid cooling equipment is manufactured in Longview, Texas, with Memphis, Tennessee capacity added.

faq.q: What capacity do BASX CDUs support?
faq.a: BASX liquid-to-liquid CDUs have a design capacity starting at 2 MW per unit with stated plans to exceed 8 MW, N+1 redundancy, stainless steel construction and 25- and 50-micron filtration to protect cold plates.

faq.q: Where are BASX data center products manufactured?
faq.a: In Longview, Texas (existing and new facilities producing from early 2025) and at a 787,000 sq ft Memphis, Tennessee facility announced in November 2024 for CRAHs, air-cooled systems, direct evaporative coolers and liquid-to-liquid and liquid-to-air CDUs.

faq.q: What did the October 2024 liquid cooling order cover?
faq.a: AAON announced data center cooling orders under the BASX brand, including a custom-designed thermal management system supporting a liquid cooling deployment for a hyperscale-type customer's data center, with the majority of production and delivery in the first half of 2025.

profiles.name: Advanced Cooling Technologies
profiles.tagline: Advanced Cooling Technologies (ACT), founded in 2003 and based in Lancaster, Pennsylvania, builds pumped two-phase liquid cooling for AI and HPC data centers: two-phase CDUs at 1 MW, 200 kW and 15 kW, single- and two-phase cold plates and manifolds, with a dedicated US cold plate manufacturing facility announced in 2026.

productLines.name: Two-phase coolant distribution units
productLines.note: Direct-to-chip two-phase CDUs in three sizes: a 1 MW unit with 200-1200 kW dynamic load range validated in 2026 at more than 1 MW total cooling capacity and within 5 degC chilled-water approach; a 200 kW end-of-row unit with N+1 pump redundancy; and a 15 kW in-rack unit in an 8U, 19-inch rack format for edge and telecom loads. One CDU cools up to 10 racks.

productLines.name: Single- and two-phase cold plates
productLines.note: Cold plates that remove heat at the source for high-power data center hardware; ACT announced a dedicated 50,000 sq ft Lancaster, Pennsylvania facility with initial capacity expected to exceed approximately 500,000 cold plates annually for AI processors.

productLines.name: Manifolds and liquid-air heat exchangers
productLines.note: Custom manifolds for uniform fluid distribution across cold plates in direct-to-chip loops, plus liquid-air heat exchangers listed among ACT's active thermal solutions for rejecting heat to air.

productLines.name: Tekgard environmental control units and chillers
productLines.note: Tekgard ECUs, the Vaphtek ECU and Tekgard chillers round out the product range for environmental control and cooling duties; ACT also provides full-rack integration of cold plates, manifolds and CDUs.

facts.text: Announced a 50,000 sq ft manufacturing facility in Lancaster, Pennsylvania dedicated to US production of single-phase and two-phase cold plates for AI processors, with initial capacity expected to exceed approximately 500,000 cold plates annually, ramping in phases.

Validated its 1 MW two-phase CDU with more than 1 MW of total cooling capacity, a 200-1200 kW dynamic load range and chilled-water temperature approach within 5 degC, testing thermal performance, stability and control response across varying loads and conditions.

faq.q: What CDU capacities does ACT offer?
faq.a: ACT offers two-phase CDUs at three scales: a 1 MW unit (200-1200 kW dynamic load range, validated in 2026 at more than 1 MW cooling capacity and within 5 degC chilled-water approach), a 200 kW end-of-row unit with N+1 pump redundancy, and a 15 kW in-rack unit in an 8U, 19-inch format for edge and telecom applications.

faq.q: How many racks can one ACT CDU cool?
faq.a: ACT states that one of its CDUs reliably cools up to 10 racks, regulating temperature, pressure and flow for direct-to-chip liquid cooling.

faq.q: Where does ACT manufacture cold plates?
faq.a: In Lancaster, Pennsylvania, where a dedicated 50,000 sq ft facility announced in May 2026 is expected to produce more than approximately 500,000 single-phase and two-phase cold plates annually for AI processors.

faq.q: When was ACT founded and where is it based?
faq.a: Advanced Cooling Technologies, Inc. was founded in 2003 as an R&D company and is headquartered in Lancaster, Pennsylvania, where it also manufactures.

profiles.name: Accelsius
profiles.tagline: Accelsius, based in Austin, Texas and founded by Innventure, develops the NeuCool two-phase direct-to-chip liquid cooling platform using a non-conductive dielectric refrigerant, spanning the in-rack IR150 (up to 150 kW) and row-based MR250 (250 kW+) CDUs for AI and HPC racks.

productLines.name: NeuCool IR150 in-rack CDU
productLines.note: Rack-level two-phase direct-to-chip unit integrating a two-phase CDU into a 200 mm portion of an 800 mm-wide enclosure with 42U of IT space; up to 150 kW cooling; R-1233zd(E) refrigerant; 55 psi max pressure; 375 L/min facility flow; 20 micron filtration; ASHRAE W27 rated, W45 derated; 1+1 hot-swappable pumps; max 2.6 kW consumption.

productLines.name: NeuCool MR250 row CDU
productLines.note: Row-based two-phase direct-to-chip CDU rated at 250 kW+ per rack for large-scale high-density deployments, with a 15-inch NeuView touchscreen, vaporators and manifolds.

productLines.name: NeuCool platform and cold plates
productLines.note: Two-phase direct-to-chip cooling with a non-conductive dielectric refrigerant: 4500W+ per socket, 0.020 degC/W thermal resistance at a 700W+ TDP, roughly 75-80% of CPU and GPU heat removed, supporting Intel, AMD EPYC and NVIDIA Grace, H100, H200, B200 and MI325X/MI355X hardware.

productLines.name: NeuCool Thermal Simulation Rack (TSR)
productLines.note: Thermal test platform offered alongside the CDUs for validating two-phase direct-to-chip cooling deployments before production use.

facts.text: Announced the IR150 will be deployed at the EdgeConneX Global Training Center in Houston, Texas - described by the company as the first deployment of its fully integrated IT rack plus CDU, which confines the failure domain to a single rack.

Announced general availability of the NeuCool IR150 at Data Center World 2026 (April 20-23, Washington, DC) and launched the NeuCool HyperStart program to help hyperscalers, neoclouds and partners validate two-phase direct-to-chip cooling and incorporate it into reference designs.

Debuted the NeuCool IR150 at NVIDIA GTC on March 16, 2026: up to 150 kW in an 800 mm enclosure with 200 mm for cooling and 600 mm for servers, warm-water compatible to ASHRAE W45 (45 degC facility water), supporting NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs and designed with headroom for Vera Rubin.

faq.q: What is the NeuCool IR150?
faq.a: A rack-level two-phase direct-to-chip unit that combines a two-phase CDU, 42U of IT space and built-in liquid and vapor manifolds in one 800 mm-wide enclosure, with up to 150 kW of cooling capacity; about 200 mm is allocated to cooling infrastructure and 600 mm to servers.

faq.q: What refrigerant does NeuCool use?
faq.a: A non-conductive dielectric refrigerant, R-1233zd(E), with an A1 safety rating and low global warming potential; no water runs in the rack, so a leak will not damage IT equipment. R-515B specifications were listed as expected mid-2025.

faq.q: Besides the IR150, what CDUs does Accelsius offer?
faq.a: The NeuCool MR250, a row-based two-phase CDU rated at 250 kW+ per rack with a 15-inch NeuView touchscreen, plus the NeuCool Thermal Simulation Rack for pre-deployment thermal testing.

faq.q: Who founded Accelsius and where is it based?
faq.a: Accelsius LLC is based in Austin, Texas and was founded by Innventure, Inc. (NASDAQ: INV); it is also an NVIDIA Inception program member.

profiles.name: Advanced Thermal Solutions
profiles.tagline: Advanced Thermal Solutions, Inc. (ATS) supplies a broad liquid cooling catalogue spanning laboratory units to data center infrastructure: the 4 MW CDU-X, a 235 kW rack-mount CDU, ArctiQ direct-to-chip cold plates, heat exchangers, chillers, flow meters and leak detectors.

productLines.name: CDU-X coolant distribution unit
productLines.note: Floor-mounted liquid-to-liquid CDU delivering 4 MW of cooling with redundant pumps and PLC automation, aimed at AI, HPC and mission-critical data center liquid cooling loops.

productLines.name: iCDM-X cooling distribution module
productLines.note: Compact self-contained module providing up to 1.6 MW of cooling for AI GPUs and other chips with only 3 kW of power draw and no external coolant; integrates pumps, heat exchangers and digital monitoring of temperature, pressure and flow for smaller AI data centers.

productLines.name: CDU-RM250 rack CDU and iCDM modules
productLines.note: 4U rack-mount liquid-to-liquid CDU delivering 235 kW with redundant operation for rack-level data center cooling, alongside 10 kW and 20 kW liquid-to-air iCDM modules (including a rugged IP65 version with PLC control) for labs, testing and immersion cooling.

productLines.name: ArctiQ DLC cold plates
productLines.note: Processor-specific direct-to-chip cold plates for AI processors, GPUs and CPUs with optimized coolant flow paths; the wider cold plate range covers microchannel, tubed, dual-sided high-flow, drillable DIY and custom designs.

productLines.name: Heat exchangers, chillers and monitoring
productLines.note: High-fin-density liquid-to-air heat exchangers and compact picoHEX units, recirculating chillers from 150 W to 2,300 W plus thermoelectric and immersion models, digital flow meters tracking flow and temperature, and leak detectors that automatically shut off coolant flow.

facts.text: Published a technical article on hybrid air-plus-liquid cooling for data centers, covering combined use of CDUs and direct-to-chip cold plates with air cooling for high-density racks.

Introduced the ATS iCDM-X cooling distribution module with up to 1.6 MW of cooling for AI GPUs at 3 kW power draw with no external coolant required, together with ICEcrystal cold plates delivering 1.5 kW of jet impingement cooling onto AI chip hotspots.

faq.q: What is ATS's largest coolant distribution unit?
faq.a: The CDU-X, a floor-mounted liquid-to-liquid CDU delivering 4 MW of cooling with redundant pumps and PLC automation for AI, HPC and mission-critical data centers.

faq.q: What did ATS introduce in June 2025?
faq.a: The iCDM-X cooling distribution module, providing up to 1.6 MW of cooling for AI GPUs with 3 kW power draw and no external coolant, plus ICEcrystal cold plates delivering 1.5 kW of jet impingement cooling directly onto AI chip hotspots.

faq.q: What rack-level CDU does ATS offer?
faq.a: The CDU-RM250, a 4U rack-mount liquid-to-liquid CDU delivering 235 kW with redundant operation for rack-level data center cooling; smaller 10 kW and 20 kW liquid-to-air iCDM modules serve labs and testing.

faq.q: What cold plates and accessories does ATS catalog include?
faq.a: ArctiQ processor-specific direct-to-chip cold plates plus microchannel, tubed, dual-sided and custom designs, liquid-to-air heat exchangers, picoHEX compact units, chillers from 150 W to 2,300 W, digital flow meters and leak detectors that shut off coolant flow automatically.

profiles.name: Celestica
profiles.tagline: Electronics design and manufacturing company that builds liquid-cooling hardware for hyperscaler data centers: in-row and in-rack cooling distribution units (CDUs), cold plates and manifolds, integrated into AI racks co-designed from the ASIC level upward.

productLines.name: Liquid cooling distribution units (CDUs)
productLines.note: Coolant distribution units offered in two form factors: in-row CDUs placed between racks (higher capacity, easier maintenance, need floor space) and in-rack CDUs built into the rack (smaller footprint, simpler deployment, suited to edge and high-density deployments).

productLines.name: Cold plates and manifolds
productLines.note: Cold plates and fluid manifolds for direct liquid cooling of processors, used in both single-phase systems and dual-phase (liquid-to-vapor) architectures that the company describes as offering higher heat transfer.

productLines.name: Platform Solutions rack integration
productLines.note: Custom compute nodes, blades and full rack integration marketed as open Platform Solutions for AI; Celestica states its engineers co-design solutions with silicon partners, beginning at the ASIC/chip level and extending to complete racks.

facts.text: On October 12, 2026 Celestica introduced the DS6005, a 1.5 Open Rack Unit data center switch that combines co-packaged optics with liquid cooling, shown at the OCP Global Summit

On September 17, 2025 Celestica published an overview of its liquid cooling offering for AI infrastructure: cooling distribution units in in-row and in-rack form factors, cold plates and manifolds, and single-phase and dual-phase liquid cooling for high-density AI racks

faq.q: What liquid-cooling hardware does Celestica offer for data centers?
faq.a: Cooling distribution units (CDUs) in in-row and in-rack form factors, plus cold plates and manifolds, supporting single-phase and dual-phase liquid cooling. The company states its advanced CDU designs have helped hyperscaler customers optimize data center thermal footprints.

faq.q: What is the difference between Celestica's in-row and in-rack CDUs?
faq.a: In-row CDUs sit between racks and offer higher capacity and easier maintenance but require floor space. In-rack CDUs are built into the rack, giving a smaller footprint and simpler deployment, which the company positions for edge and high-density deployments.

faq.q: Does Celestica sell complete liquid-cooled racks?
faq.a: Yes. Within its Platform Solutions for AI infrastructure, Celestica co-designs solutions with silicon partners from the ASIC/chip level through custom nodes and blades to complete racks, including liquid-cooled configurations for hyperscaler customers.

profiles.name: DDC Solutions
profiles.tagline: San Diego manufacturer of ultra-high-density rack containment cabinets that combine air and liquid cooling inside the rack; its S-Series supports up to 100 kW air-side per cabinet and 1MW+ with direct-liquid-cooling integration for AI and GPU deployments. A subsidiary of Daikin Applied since August 2025.

productLines.name: S-4 high-density cooling cabinet
productLines.note: Enterprise and mixed-density rack containment unit with a flexible footprint that supports standard and OCP racks; provides high-density air-side cooling with a liquid-ready design for adding direct-to-chip cooling later.

productLines.name: S-5 GPU cooling cabinet
productLines.note: 42-inch wide, deeper form factor built for next-generation GPU roll-in racks, in-rack CDUs and external electrical demarcation; part of the S-Series platform rated up to 1MW+ cooling per rack with integrated CDU.

productLines.name: GPUVault enclosure
productLines.note: Retrofit-first enclosure for legacy and low-ceiling facilities: two containment units with a heat exchanger in the middle deliver up to 200 kW combined air-side cooling, with secure water routing for adding liquid cooling.

productLines.name: DCIM software
productLines.note: Data center infrastructure management software for real-time monitoring and automated per-cabinet cooling control of DDC's hybrid air+liquid cooling cabinets.

facts.text: On March 10, 2026 DDC announced the S-5 GPU cooling cabinet, a 42-inch-wide, 96-inch-deep enclosure that takes up to 100 kW of air-side load per cabinet with optional liquid-to-chip coolant paths; the S-Series platform spans 85 kW (S-4), 100 kW (S-5) and 200 kW (GPUVault, a three-cabinet module) and supports 1 MW+ with direct-to-chip cooling; initial S-5 shipments began in April 2026

Daikin Applied completed its acquisition of DDC Solutions, announced August 18, 2025. DDC operates as a Daikin Applied subsidiary with its full leadership team remaining in place, adding ultra-high-density cooling cabinets and management software for data centers to Daikin Applied's portfolio.

faq.q: What does DDC Solutions make?
faq.a: Ultra-high-density cooling cabinets and management software for data centers, using a patented hybrid system that combines air and liquid cooling directly within the rack. Models include the S-4, the GPU-focused S-5, and the retrofit-oriented GPUVault.

faq.q: How much heat can a DDC cabinet handle?
faq.a: Per the March 2026 release: up to 85 kW air-side for the S-4, up to 100 kW for the S-5 and up to 200 kW combined for the GPUVault, with direct-to-chip liquid integration supporting 1 MW+ per rack. The S-4 is liquid-ready so direct-to-chip cooling can be added later.

faq.q: Who owns DDC Solutions?
faq.a: Daikin Applied completed its acquisition of DDC Solutions, announced August 18, 2025. DDC operates as a Daikin Applied subsidiary, and the full DDC Solutions leadership team remained in their current roles.

faq.q: Can DDC cabinets fit standard or OCP racks?
faq.a: The S-4 supports standard and OCP rack widths with a flexible footprint, while the S-5 uses a 42-inch wide, deeper form factor for GPU roll-in racks, in-rack CDUs and external electrical demarcation.

profiles.name: ChemTreat
profiles.tagline: Industrial water treatment company and Veralto operating company supplying coolant chemistry for data center liquid cooling: CTSolutions D2C propylene glycol 25% and 50% heat transfer fluids, monitoring and Dow Coolant Care Network support, serving over 200 data center facilities in North America.

productLines.name: CTSolutions D2C coolant programs
productLines.note: Direct-to-chip coolant chemistry: propylene glycol 25% and 50% heat transfer fluids, aqueous coolants with bio-static capability, and specialty stabilized oxidizing and non-oxidizing biocides, backed by certified coolant performance testing, in-line monitoring, leak detection and automated feed systems.

productLines.name: Dow Coolant Care Network services
productLines.note: As a strategic service provider nationally and the only preferred service provider in Virginia, ChemTreat handles sampling, mitigation and fluid health optimization with Dow-qualified labs for DOWFROST LC and DOWFROST HD heat transfer fluids used in direct-to-chip cooling loops and facility loops, from design phase through steady-state operations.

productLines.name: Facility cooling water treatment
productLines.note: Cooling tower and facility water chemistry for data center campuses: FlexPro and FlexCorr non-phosphorus/low-phosphorus corrosion inhibitors, MultiCuRE yellow metal protection, CalciTect and QuadDetect tagged deposit control, SurfClean 2.0 halogen stabilizer and biodispersant, plus adiabatic media-life and Legionella sampling programs.

facts.text: ChemTreat joined Dow's Coolant Care Network as a strategic service provider nationally for AI data center cooling, announced May 18, 2026. The network coordinates fluid supply, testing, data analysis and in-field support; ChemTreat serves over 200 data center sites and is the only preferred service provider in Virginia.

ChemTreat published the white paper The Framework for Operational Readiness in Data Center Cooling Systems (2026): CDUs move heat from the technology cooling system loop to facility water through plate-and-frame heat exchangers, cold plates need laminar flow, coolant particles should stay below 1 µm during commissioning, and continuous monitoring is needed to catch chemistry drift

faq.q: What coolant chemistry does ChemTreat offer for direct-to-chip loops?
faq.a: CTSolutions D2C programs: propylene glycol 25% and 50% heat transfer fluids, aqueous coolants with bio-static capability, and specialty stabilized oxidizing and non-oxidizing biocides, supported by certified coolant performance testing, in-line monitoring, leak detection and automated feed systems.

faq.q: What is ChemTreat's role in Dow's Coolant Care Network?
faq.a: Announced May 18, 2026, ChemTreat is a strategic service provider nationally and the only preferred service provider in Virginia. It handles sampling, mitigation and fluid health optimization with Dow-qualified labs for DOWFROST LC and DOWFROST HD fluids used in direct-to-chip and facility loops.

faq.q: How many data centers does ChemTreat serve?
faq.a: ChemTreat states it supports over 200 data center facilities across North America, covering cooling water, closed loops, adiabatic systems and direct-to-chip coolant programs.

faq.q: Who owns ChemTreat and where is it based?
faq.a: ChemTreat is listed among Veralto's operating companies, described there as offering industrial water treatment solutions. The company says it is headquartered in Richmond, Virginia, with its footer address in Glen Allen, VA 23060.

profiles.name: Carrier
profiles.tagline: HVAC and building technology company (NYSE: CARR) whose QuantumLeap portfolio provides chip-to-chiller data center thermal management: AquaEdge and AquaForce chillers, Aero air handling units, coolant distribution units for direct-to-chip liquid cooling, Nlyte DCIM software and lifecycle services.
profiles.hq: Palm Beach Gardens, Florida, United States

productLines.name: Coolant Distribution Units (CDUs)
productLines.note: Direct-to-chip CDUs bridging IT equipment to facility cooling, in sizes from 1.3 to 5MW with approach temperatures as low as 3.6 F (2 C) versus the common 7.2 F (4 C). Carrier cites up to 50% less non-IT energy use than legacy cooling and up to 15% chiller energy savings with a high-efficiency heat exchanger option; available worldwide since November 2025.
