productLines.name: AquaEdge and AquaForce chillers
productLines.note: AquaEdge 30CF air-cooled centrifugal, AquaForce 30XV air-cooled screw, and AquaEdge 19MV/19DV water-cooled chillers (19DV with EquiDrive compressors; restart to full capacity in under 150 seconds). The QuantumLeap chiller generation is marketed as 30% more efficient than prior generations, with free cooling and elevated chilled water temperatures.

productLines.name: Aero air handling units
productLines.note: Aero 39DC and 39M air handling units, custom and semi-custom with configurable fans, filters and factory controls, forming the airside of the QuantumLeap data center cooling suite.

productLines.name: Integrated data center management software
productLines.note: Integrated Data Center Management unifies cooling with WebCTRL building automation and Nlyte DCIM (Asset Optimizer, Energy Optimizer). Carrier states Nlyte is deployed in more than 300 data centers managing over one million racks, alongside the Abound digital platform for remote diagnostics and predictive maintenance.

facts.text: On November 4, 2025 Carrier announced a new Coolant Distribution Unit for its QuantumLeap portfolio: unit sizes from 1.3 to 5MW, approach temperatures as low as 3.6 F (2 C), cited savings of up to 50% in non-IT energy use versus legacy cooling technologies, with worldwide availability through multiple Carrier manufacturing sites.

On February 6, 2025 Carrier introduced QuantumLeap, a suite of data center thermal management solutions extending from chip to chiller: chillers marketed as 30% more efficient than prior generations, a coolant distribution unit for direct-to-chip liquid cooling first shown at SuperComputing24, Automated Logic controls, Nlyte DCIM deployed in more than 300 data centers, and global lifecycle service with the Abound platform.

faq.q: What is Carrier QuantumLeap?
faq.a: A suite of thermal and integrated management solutions for data centers introduced on February 6, 2025, spanning chip to chiller: AquaEdge and AquaForce chillers, Aero air handling units, coolant distribution units for direct-to-chip liquid cooling, Automated Logic controls, Nlyte DCIM software and lifecycle services with the Abound digital platform.

faq.q: What CDU capacities and performance does Carrier publish?
faq.a: Coolant Distribution Units come in sizes from 1.3 to 5MW with approach temperatures as low as 3.6 F (2 C), compared with the more common 7.2 F (4 C). Carrier cites up to 50% reduction in non-IT energy use versus legacy cooling and up to 15% chiller energy savings with the high-efficiency heat exchanger option.

faq.q: Are Carrier's data center CDUs available now?
faq.a: Yes. In its November 4, 2025 announcement Carrier stated the CDU is now available worldwide through multiple Carrier manufacturing sites, supporting global supply and in-region sourcing at scale.

faq.q: What software does Carrier offer for data center cooling?
faq.a: Integrated Data Center Management unifies cooling systems with WebCTRL building automation and Nlyte DCIM, including Nlyte Asset Optimizer and Energy Optimizer. Carrier states Nlyte is deployed in more than 300 data centers managing over one million racks.

profiles.name: Cofan Thermal
profiles.tagline: Thermal management manufacturer headquartered in Dallas, Texas, with 30+ years in thermal products, offering direct liquid-cooling cold plates, OSFP thermal solutions for 800G to 3.2T optical transceivers adaptable to air- and liquid-cooled systems, vapor chambers and custom heatsinks, manufactured across Taiwan, Vietnam and China.

productLines.name: Cold plates
productLines.note: Heat exchanger components integrated into electronic systems that circulate a cooling fluid through channels to efficiently remove heat generated by components and maintain optimal operating temperatures, for direct liquid cooling of electronics.

productLines.name: OSFP heatsinks for optical transceivers
productLines.note: Thermal solutions supporting optical transceivers from 800G up to 3.2T, described as adaptable to both air- and liquid-cooled systems for efficient thermal performance across a wide range of deployment scenarios.

productLines.name: Vapor chambers and heat pipes
productLines.note: Flat sealed vapor-chamber devices containing a small amount of liquid that vaporizes and condenses to transfer heat away from components, complemented by sealed heat-pipe assemblies using phase-change principles.

productLines.name: Custom thermal design and CFD services
productLines.note: Computational Fluid Dynamics studies and custom thermal design, with engineering, prototyping and integration offered from the company's USA sales and support operations; listed certificates include ITAR, ISO, IATF, OHSAS, RoHS and UL.

facts.text: Cofan Thermal's current product homepage (last modified August 12, 2026) lists liquid-cooling cold plates and OSFP heatsinks for 800G-3.2T optical transceivers among active product lines, with cold plate product imagery published in August 2026 and OSFP imagery from March 2026.
Opened its Vietnam manufacturing facility, according to a company blog item dated February 2025

Announced a factory expansion for liquid-cooled cold plates, enlarging the production floor and upgrading equipment for liquid-cooled cold plate manufacturing, according to a company blog item dated April 2024

faq.q: What liquid-cooling products does Cofan Thermal offer?
faq.a: Cold plates that circulate cooling fluid through channels to remove heat from electronic components, OSFP heatsink solutions for optical transceivers from 800G up to 3.2T adaptable to both air- and liquid-cooled systems, and vapor chambers and heat pipes that move heat via phase change.

faq.q: Where does Cofan Thermal operate?
faq.a: Headquarters in Dallas, Texas (R&D, sales, marketing and financing), plus Fremont, California and Toronto, Ontario. Manufacturing and engineering sites include Vietnam (heatsink and metal fabrication), Taiwan (R&D, CFD and MCPCB manufacturing) and several Dongguan, China plants for passive/active cooling, sheet metal and vapor chamber manufacturing.

faq.q: What engineering services does Cofan Thermal provide?
faq.a: Computational Fluid Dynamics studies to design and implement cooling solutions, custom thermal design, engineering, prototyping and integration from its USA operations. Listed certificates: ITAR, ISO, IATF, OHSAS, RoHS and UL.

faq.q: How long has Cofan Thermal been in business?
faq.a: The company states more than 30 years in thermal products and manufacturing, spanning design, prototyping and production. An exact founding year is not published on its site.

profiles.name: Dober
profiles.tagline: Dober is a family-owned specialty chemical formulator in Woodridge, Illinois whose COOLWAVE DC line of USP-grade propylene glycol coolants serves single-phase direct-to-chip liquid cooling in AI/HPC data centers. COOLWAVE DC-25 is a prediluted PG25 coolant recognized under the Open Compute Project.

productLines.name: COOLWAVE DC-25
productLines.note: Prediluted 25% USP-grade propylene glycol coolant for single-phase direct-to-chip cold-plate loops; freeze protection to 10.3 F (-12.1 C), burst protection to -4.0 F (-20.1 C), boiling point up to 214.7 F; compatible with copper, aluminum, plastics and elastomers.

productLines.name: COOLWAVE DC-30
productLines.note: USP-grade propylene glycol blend for direct-to-chip cooling with freeze protection to -7.9 F (-13.4 C), burst protection to -18.0 F (-27.5 C) and boiling point up to 216 F; viscosity 2.75 mPa-s at 20 C.

productLines.name: COOLWAVE DC-55
productLines.note: USP-grade propylene glycol blend for cold climates and outdoor loops; freeze protection to -40 F (-40 C), burst protection below -60 F, boiling point up to 221 F; viscosity 8.78 mPa-s at 20 C and 2.89 mPa-s at 50 C.

productLines.name: DC-Custom
productLines.note: Custom-engineered data center coolant formulations offered alongside the standard DC series; specifications vary by formulation and are defined with the customer.

facts.text: Dober announced that COOLWAVE DC-25 earned Open Compute Project recognition, initially OCP Inspired and later stated by Dober as an OCP Accepted solution for data center liquid cooling.

The OCP marketplace lists COOLWAVE DC 25 as a prediluted 25% USP-grade propylene glycol coolant for single-phase cold-plate cooling, associated with the approved OCP propylene glycol heat transfer fluid contribution and meeting ASTM D8039 and D8040 corrosion requirements.

profiles.ocp: COOLWAVE DC 25 is listed in the OCP marketplace as an OCP Accepted, ready-to-use PG25 direct-to-chip coolant, associated with the OCP-approved propylene glycol heat transfer fluid guidelines contribution (https://www.opencompute.org/marketplace/facilities-physical-infrastructure/coolwave-dc-heat-transfer-fluids).

faq.q: What is COOLWAVE DC-25?
faq.a: A prediluted 25% USP-grade propylene glycol coolant for single-phase direct-to-chip cold-plate loops, with freeze protection to 10.3 F (-12.1 C) and corrosion inhibitors meeting ASTM D8039/D8040 requirements. Dober lists it as an OCP Accepted solution.

faq.q: Which fluids make up the COOLWAVE DC line?
faq.a: COOLWAVE DC-25, DC-30 and DC-55, all USP-grade propylene glycol blends, plus DC-Custom formulations. Freeze protection ranges from 10.3 F on DC-25 down to -40 F on DC-55, with burst protection below -60 F on DC-55.

faq.q: What OCP recognition does Dober hold?
faq.a: Dober announced COOLWAVE DC-25 initially earned OCP Inspired recognition and is now stated as OCP Accepted. The OCP marketplace associates the fluid with the approved OCP propylene glycol heat transfer fluid contribution.

faq.q: Is Dober a public company?
faq.a: No. Dober describes itself as a third-generation family business founded in 1957, headquartered in Woodridge, Illinois.

profiles.name: Ecolab (Nalco Water)
profiles.tagline: Ecolab, through its Nalco Water business, supplies coolant chemistry, monitoring and lifecycle services for direct-to-chip liquid cooling in AI and HPC data centers. Its Liquid Cooling All In program combines 3D TRASAR technology and propylene glycol coolants with cold-plate products from CoolIT, an Ecolab company.

productLines.name: Liquid Cooling All In
productLines.note: Full-lifecycle direct liquid cooling offering for HPC and AI data centers: 3D TRASAR chemistry and monitoring for direct-to-chip loops and cooling water, propylene glycol coolant with quality-control protocols, and Lifecycle Performance Services covering design, installation, commissioning and ongoing operations, with CoolIT cold-plate products.

productLines.name: 3D TRASAR for Direct-to-Chip Liquid Cooling
productLines.note: Monitoring and support program for direct-to-chip loops: continuous coolant health monitoring, quarterly on-site checks and 24/7 remote monitoring from the Ecolab Global Intelligence Center; watches glycol degradation, contamination from server change-outs, and fluid loss or leaks.

productLines.name: Nalco Water propylene glycol coolant
productLines.note: Propylene glycol heat-transfer fluid for direct liquid cooling loops, supplied with quality-control protocols and paired with 3D TRASAR monitoring within the Liquid Cooling All In program.

facts.text: Ecolab's Liquid Cooling All In program is a full-lifecycle direct liquid cooling offering for AI and HPC data centers combining Nalco Water chemistry, 3D TRASAR monitoring and lifecycle services; Ecolab exhibited the program at SC26 in Chicago, November 15-20, 2026.
Within the program, CoolIT operates as an Ecolab company, supplying data center and server cold-plate products and global professional services alongside Ecolab's coolant chemistry and monitoring.

faq.q: What is Ecolab's Liquid Cooling All In program?
faq.a: A full-lifecycle direct liquid cooling offering for AI and HPC data centers. It combines 3D TRASAR chemistry and monitoring, propylene glycol coolant with quality-control protocols, and lifecycle performance services covering design through ongoing operations, with CoolIT cold-plate products.

faq.q: What does 3D TRASAR for direct-to-chip cooling monitor?
faq.a: It continuously monitors coolant health, glycol degradation from high-temperature operation, contamination such as server change-out debris, and fluid loss or leaks, with quarterly on-site checks and 24/7 remote monitoring from the Ecolab Global Intelligence Center.

faq.q: What is CoolIT's relationship to Ecolab?
faq.a: CoolIT is an Ecolab company. Its data center and server cold-plate products and global professional services are offered inside Ecolab's Liquid Cooling All In program alongside Nalco Water chemistry.

faq.q: Where is Ecolab headquartered and how is it listed?
faq.a: Ecolab is headquartered at 1 Ecolab Place, St. Paul, Minnesota, and its shares are listed on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker ECL. The company describes more than a century of innovation; its founding year is not stated on the pages reviewed.

profiles.name: Gradian Thermal Solutions
profiles.tagline: Gradian Thermal Solutions is a Maple Grove, Minnesota manufacturer of data center liquid cooling equipment, operating the former DeepCoolAI liquid cooling line. It supplies liquid-to-liquid and liquid-to-air CDUs, active rear-door heat exchangers, load banks and coolant refill carts for high-density AI workloads.

productLines.name: In-Rack Liquid-to-Liquid CDUs
productLines.note: In-rack coolant distribution units rated 80-200 kW, supporting standard 19-inch racks and OCP ORv3 rack architectures for rack-scale direct liquid cooling.

productLines.name: In-Row Liquid-to-Liquid CDUs
productLines.note: In-row coolant distribution units rated 600 kW to 2.5 MW as standard, modular up to 5 MW, 7.5 MW, 10 MW and beyond for facility-wide direct liquid cooling deployment.

productLines.name: Liquid-to-Air CDUs
productLines.note: Liquid-to-air CDUs offered in in-row and in-rack configurations for scalable cooling from a single rack to facility-wide deployment where no facility water loop is available.

productLines.name: Active Rear Door Heat Exchangers
productLines.note: Active rear-door heat exchangers that capture heat at the rack exhaust for air-to-liquid cooling of high-density racks within the Gradian liquid cooling portfolio.

productLines.name: Load Banks and Coolant Refill Carts
productLines.note: Air, liquid and hybrid load banks for validation and deployment execution, plus mobile self-contained carts for filling, flushing and replenishing liquid cooling loops.

facts.text: As of 2026, DeepCoolAI operates as part of Gradian Thermal Solutions, with the same team headquartered in Maple Grove, Minnesota, offering CDUs, rear-door heat exchangers, load banks and refill carts under the Gradian brand.

The company's current liquid-to-liquid CDU range spans in-rack units of 80-200 kW supporting 19-inch and OCP ORv3 rack architectures and in-row units of 600 kW to 2.5 MW standard, modular to 5 MW, 7.5 MW and 10 MW and beyond.

faq.q: What CDU configurations does Gradian offer?
faq.a: Liquid-to-liquid CDUs in in-rack (80-200 kW, fitting standard 19-inch and OCP ORv3 racks) and in-row (600 kW to 2.5 MW standard, modular to 5, 7.5 and 10 MW and beyond) configurations, plus liquid-to-air CDUs from single-rack to facility-wide scale.

faq.q: What is the relationship between DeepCoolAI and Gradian?
faq.a: DeepCoolAI is now part of Gradian Thermal Solutions. The same team, headquartered in Maple Grove, Minnesota, continues to offer the liquid cooling products under the Gradian name.

faq.q: Does Gradian supply equipment beyond CDUs?
faq.a: Yes: active rear-door heat exchangers, air, liquid and hybrid load banks for validation and deployment, rack manifolds, and mobile self-contained carts for filling, flushing and replenishing liquid cooling loops.

faq.q: Where can I find the company's founding date or ownership details?
faq.a: Not published on the pages reviewed: Gradian's site states its Maple Grove, Minnesota headquarters but does not state a founding year or ownership structure, so these are marked NOT_FOUND here.

profiles.name: Hose Master
profiles.tagline: Hose Master is a Cleveland, Ohio manufacturer of corrugated stainless steel metal hose and metal expansion joints. Its Masterflex hose assemblies connect liquid cooling components including manifolds, cold plates, CDUs, immersion systems and rear-door heat exchangers in hyperscale data centers.

productLines.name: Masterflex corrugated metal hose
productLines.note: Close-pitch corrugated stainless steel hose assemblies with external braid for pressure tolerance, positioned by Hose Master for hyperscale data center cooling applications across manifolds, cold plates, CDUs, immersion cooling and rear-door heat exchangers; all-stainless construction supports fire safety.

productLines.name: Corrugated hose series (Annuflex, PressureFlex HP, PressureMax HP)
productLines.note: Additional corrugated metal hose series offered alongside Masterflex in the company's general high-pressure flexible hose portfolio; Hose Master also manufactures stripwound metal hose.

productLines.name: Metal expansion joints and hose for cooling systems
productLines.note: Metal hoses and expansion joints for data center cooling infrastructure, listed for air-cooled and liquid-cooled systems (direct or indirect cooling), heat exchanger connections, pump and compressor connections, and air blowers.

facts.text: Hose Master's current data center offering supplies Masterflex corrugated stainless steel hose assemblies for hyperscale cooling applications spanning manifolds, cold plates, coolant distribution units, immersion cooling and rear-door heat exchangers.

In a current article, 'Why Liquid Cooling and Metal Hoses Are the Future of Data Centers', Hose Master states that liquid cooling can cut power use by as much as 15% and that liquids transfer heat up to 25 times more efficiently than air, arguing for stainless corrugated hose with welded fittings and seismic protection.

faq.q: Which Hose Master product is aimed at data center liquid cooling?
faq.a: Masterflex, a close-pitch corrugated stainless steel hose assembly with external braid for pressure tolerance. Hose Master describes it as well-suited to hyperscale data center cooling, with all-stainless construction supporting fire safety.

faq.q: Which liquid cooling components use Hose Master assemblies?
faq.a: The company lists manifolds, cold plates, coolant distribution units, immersion cooling and rear-door heat exchangers, plus heat exchanger, pump and compressor connections in air-cooled and liquid-cooled (direct or indirect) systems.

faq.q: Where does Hose Master operate from?
faq.a: Headquarters at 1233 East 222nd Street, Cleveland, Ohio, with additional locations in Houston, Atlanta and Reno.

faq.q: Is Hose Master publicly traded?
faq.a: Its founding year and ownership structure are not published on the pages reviewed, so both are marked NOT_FOUND here; only its Cleveland headquarters and three other US locations are stated.

profiles.name: Hyve Solutions
profiles.tagline: Hyve Solutions designs, integrates and thermally validates rack-scale direct liquid cooling for hyperscale AI and HPC customers, building complete liquid-cooled rack systems that ship wet or dry under unified design and manufacturing operations. It is part of TD SYNNEX.

productLines.name: Liquid Cooling Infrastructure Services
productLines.note: Rack-scale direct liquid cooling services: in-house design, integration and thermal validation under unified design and manufacturing operations; DLC cold plates move heat through closed-loop systems integrated with Hyve compute, networking and rack platforms for AI, HPC and enterprise.

productLines.name: Liquid-cooled test pods (Olive Branch, MS)
productLines.note: Liquid-cooled pods brought up at the Olive Branch, Mississippi facility in summer 2025, offering extensive NVIDIA GPU testing with custom testing available on request for liquid-cooled systems.

productLines.name: Orion rack platform
productLines.note: Rack platform in Hyve's AI infrastructure portfolio offering both air and liquid cooling options, demonstrated at NVIDIA GTC 2025 with Vertiv liquid cooling technology.

facts.text: Hyve's current liquid cooling offering provides rack-scale, performance-tested direct liquid cooling systems with design, integration and thermal validation done in-house, integrated with its compute, networking and rack platforms, shipping wet or dry per customer requirements.

On March 18, 2025 at NVIDIA GTC, Hyve unveiled its AI infrastructure portfolio and announced it was bringing up liquid-cooled pods at its Olive Branch, Mississippi facility in summer 2025, offering extensive NVIDIA GPU testing with custom testing on request.
The GTC 2025 portfolio includes the Orion rack with air and liquid cooling options, demonstrated using Vertiv liquid cooling technology.

faq.q: What liquid cooling services does Hyve provide?
faq.a: Rack-scale direct liquid cooling covering design, integration and thermal validation in-house. DLC cold plates move heat through closed-loop systems, integrated with Hyve compute, networking and rack platforms, and complete racks ship wet or dry as the customer requires, validated before delivery.

faq.q: Where does Hyve test liquid-cooled systems?
faq.a: At liquid-cooled pods at its Olive Branch, Mississippi facility, announced in March 2025 for bring-up in summer 2025, providing extensive NVIDIA GPU testing with custom testing available on request.

faq.q: Who owns Hyve Solutions?
faq.a: Hyve Solutions is part of TD SYNNEX, as stated on hyvesolutions.com.

faq.q: Where is Hyve headquartered and when was it founded?
faq.a: Its website does not state a headquarters city or founding year on the pages reviewed, so both are marked NOT_FOUND here; its liquid cooling test facility in Olive Branch, Mississippi is documented.

profiles.name: ExxonMobil
profiles.tagline: ExxonMobil Product Solutions supplies the EM DC series of PFAS-free, single-phase dielectric immersion cooling fluids for AI, HPC and edge data centers. In November 2025, Intel designated ExxonMobil's single-phase immersion fluids as warranty-supported for 4th and 5th generation Xeon processors.

productLines.name: EM DC 3150 series (3150/3151/3152)
productLines.note: Low-viscosity PFAS-free single-phase immersion cooling fluids, 5.0-6.4 cSt at 40 C per ASTM D445 with flash points of 149-157 C per ASTM D92, for high-performance and edge computing data centers.

productLines.name: EM DC 3220
productLines.note: PFAS-free single-phase immersion cooling fluid with 19.0 cSt viscosity at 40 C per ASTM D445 and 220 C flash point per ASTM D92.

productLines.name: EM DC 3235 Super
productLines.note: PFAS-free single-phase immersion cooling fluid with 14.3 cSt viscosity at 40 C per ASTM D445 and 234 C flash point per ASTM D92.

productLines.name: EM DC 3250
productLines.note: PFAS-free single-phase immersion cooling fluid with 31.0 cSt viscosity at 40 C per ASTM D445 and 246 C flash point per ASTM D92, the highest flash point in the listed range.

productLines.name: EM DC 1210 (AP)
productLines.note: PFAS-free single-phase immersion cooling fluid with 30.4 cSt viscosity at 40 C per ASTM D445 and 225 C flash point per ASTM D92.

facts.text: ExxonMobil's current data center portfolio lists PFAS-free single-phase immersion cooling fluids spanning 5.0 to 31.0 cSt at 40 C, with a collaboration with Intel to develop and certify energy-efficient liquid cooling for Xeon technology and partnerships with UNICOM Engineering and Submer.

On November 17, 2025, Intel designated ExxonMobil's single-phase immersion fluids 'Intel Supported Immersion Fluids', warranty-supported for 4th and 5th generation Intel Xeon processors, with an immersion warranty rider covering the immersion tank, ExxonMobil fluids and IT equipment validated at Intel labs, extendable to other tank and IT configurations.

faq.q: What are ExxonMobil's EM DC fluids?
faq.a: A portfolio of PFAS-free single-phase dielectric immersion cooling fluids for high-performance and edge computing data centers, with viscosities from 5.0 to 31.0 cSt at 40 C (ASTM D445) and flash points from 149 to 246 C (ASTM D92).

faq.q: What did the November 2025 Intel announcement cover?
faq.a: ExxonMobil's single-phase immersion fluids were designated 'Intel Supported Immersion Fluids', recognized as warranty-supported for 4th and 5th generation Intel Xeon processors. Intel offers an immersion warranty rider covering the tank, ExxonMobil fluids and IT equipment validated at Intel labs, extendable to other configurations.

faq.q: Which partners are named on ExxonMobil's data center cooling page?
faq.a: Intel, with whom ExxonMobil is collaborating to develop and certify next-generation liquid cooling for Xeon technology, plus UNICOM Engineering and Submer.

faq.q: Where is ExxonMobil headquartered?
faq.a: The corporation's global headquarters is its 385-acre campus in Spring, Texas (Houston area), opened in 2014 and built to accommodate more than 10,000 employees and visitors.

profiles.name: Gates
profiles.tagline: Gates (NYSE: GTES) is a Denver, Colorado maker of engineered fluid power and power transmission products. Its data center liquid cooling portfolio spans UQD/UQDB quick disconnect couplings, Data Master and MegaFlex EPDM cooling hose, and ThermalCool pumps for in-rack and in-row CDUs.

productLines.name: UQD/UQDB Quick Disconnect Couplings
productLines.note: Universal quick disconnect couplings providing secure, spill-free connections for in-rack liquid cooling applications, listed on the OCP marketplace and associated with Intel's UQD Specification Rev 1.0; designed to work with Gates Data Master cooling hoses.

productLines.name: Data Master cooling hose
productLines.note: Hose line from 7/32 to 1 inch ID with zinc-free, peroxide-cured EPDM tube; flame-resistant to UL94 V-0, ozone-resistant and compatible with coolants such as PG25; used in CRAC/CRAH units, chilled water systems, direct-to-chip liquid cooling and in-row/in-rack cooling.

productLines.name: Data Master MegaFlex hose
productLines.note: Large-ID, high-flow hose variant announced March 28, 2025 in 1.25-2 inch sizes (now listed up to 4 inch ID) for high-flow supply loops and glycol transfer in large-scale data centers; peroxide-cured EPDM tube and MegaFlex design technology for faster coolant flow.

productLines.name: ThermalCool Data Center Pumps
productLines.note: Axial flux pumps made to customer specifications for in-rack and in-row coolant distribution units within the Gates data center cooling portfolio.

facts.text: The current Data Master hose line spans 7/32 to 1 inch ID with MegaFlex up to 4 inch ID, UL94 V-0 flame resistance, ozone resistance and PG25 coolant compatibility, serving CRAC/CRAH, chilled water, direct-to-chip and in-row/in-rack cooling.

Gates' current data center cooling systems portfolio also lists ThermalCool axial flux pumps built to specification for in-rack and in-row CDUs, alongside UQD/UQDB couplings, and describes Gates as a Silver Member of the Open Compute Project.

On March 28, 2025 Gates announced the expansion of its data center cooling portfolio with Data Master MegaFlex large-diameter hose in 1.25-2 inch sizes, available beginning April 2025, featuring a peroxide-cured EPDM tube and, per Gates, up to 75% tighter minimum bend radius than competitive alternatives.

profiles.ocp: Gates describes itself as a Silver Member of the Open Compute Project, and its Universal Quick Disconnect couplings are listed on the OCP marketplace, associated with the approved Intel UQD Specification Rev 1.0 contribution; the OCP listing currently shows no separate OCP recognition (https://www.opencompute.org/marketplace/facilities-physical-infrastructure/gates-universal-quick-disconnect-uqd-couplings).

faq.q: What does Gates sell for data center liquid cooling?
faq.a: UQD/UQDB quick disconnect couplings for spill-free in-rack connections, the Data Master hose family (7/32 to 1 inch ID, plus MegaFlex up to 4 inch ID) with zinc-free peroxide-cured EPDM tubes, and ThermalCool axial flux pumps for in-rack and in-row CDUs.

faq.q: When did Gates launch Data Master MegaFlex?
faq.a: Announced March 28, 2025, available beginning April 2025 in 1.25-2 inch sizes for high-flow supply loops and glycol transfer; Gates states a peroxide-cured EPDM tube and up to 75% tighter minimum bend radius than competitive alternatives. The line is now listed up to 4 inch ID.

faq.q: Are Gates UQD couplings OCP Accepted?
faq.a: Gates states it is a Silver Member of the Open Compute Project, and its UQD couplings are listed on the OCP marketplace associated with Intel's UQD Specification Rev 1.0. The OCP listing itself currently shows no OCP recognition for the product.

faq.q: Where is Gates based and how is it listed?
faq.a: Gates issued its March 2025 data center announcement from Denver, Colorado, and the company trades on the New York Stock Exchange under ticker GTES; a founding year is not stated on the pages reviewed.

profiles.name: Jabil
profiles.tagline: Jabil is an NYSE-listed electronics manufacturing services company building AI data-center infrastructure, including rack-level liquid cooling: microchannel cold plates from its Mikros acquisition, integrated CDU and rack plumbing, manifolds and liquid-cooled switch integration.

productLines.name: Microchannel cold plates (Mikros)
productLines.note: Microchannel cold-plate design and manufacturing from Mikros Technologies, acquired October 2024; Jabil presents cold plates as the foundation of its AI data-center liquid-cooling stack for direct-to-chip cooling.

productLines.name: Integrated CDU and rack plumbing
productLines.note: Integrated coolant distribution unit and rack plumbing solutions for AI racks, designed for flexible compatibility with air, liquid and hybrid cooling systems per Jabil's data-center infrastructure pages.

productLines.name: Manifolds
productLines.note: Rack manifold designs for distributing coolant to server cold plates within direct-to-chip liquid-cooling loops, offered alongside Jabil's CDU and rack plumbing integration services.

productLines.name: Liquid-cooled switch integration
productLines.note: Integration of liquid-cooled switches for networking and AI clusters, plus thermal strategies for co-packaged optics (CPO).

facts.text: Jabil's newsroom carried a September 9, 2026 Global SMT & Packaging article, 'Liquid Cooling: From Engineering Solutions to Commercial Enterprise', on the commercialization of its Mikros liquid-cooling business.
IEEE Spectrum's October 13, 2025 article 'Next-Gen AI Needs Liquid Cooling' featured Jabil's Mikros microchannel cold-plate technology for next-generation AI systems.

Jabil announced the acquisition of Mikros Technologies on October 3, 2024 to support demand for liquid cooling in AI data centers, adding microchannel cold-plate capability to its data-center infrastructure business.

faq.q: Does Jabil make liquid cooling hardware itself?
faq.a: Yes. Following its October 2024 acquisition of Mikros Technologies, Jabil designs and manufactures microchannel cold plates and offers integrated CDU and rack plumbing solutions, manifold designs and liquid-cooled switch integration for AI data centers.

faq.q: Where does co-packaged optics fit in?
faq.a: Jabil's data-center infrastructure pages list thermal strategies for co-packaged optics (CPO) alongside liquid-cooled switch integration, so thermal management extends to optical and networking hardware, not only server cold plates.

faq.q: Is Jabil a contract manufacturer or a cooling vendor?
faq.a: Jabil is an NYSE-listed electronics manufacturing services company. In data centers it integrates liquid cooling at rack level - cold plates, CDU and plumbing, manifolds, liquid-cooled switches - and supports air, liquid and hybrid cooling systems.

faq.q: When did Jabil enter direct-to-chip liquid cooling?
faq.a: Jabil announced its acquisition of microchannel cold-plate specialist Mikros Technologies on October 3, 2024, to support demand for liquid cooling in AI data centers.

profiles.name: Mikros Technologies
profiles.tagline: Mikros Technologies designs single- and two-phase microchannel cold plates for direct-to-chip liquid cooling, with published heat-flux control up to 1,000 W/cm2 and liquid-to-chip cooling cited at the 1 MW Frontier supercomputer scale; it has operated as a Jabil company since October 2024.

productLines.name: MIKROMATRIX microchannel cold plates
productLines.note: MIKROMATRIX is Mikros' liquid-cooling technology platform for single- and two-phase direct-to-chip cooling of CPUs, GPUs, transceivers, IGBTs, lasers and optics; Jabil's acquisition release cites cooling capability over one kilowatt per square centimeter.

productLines.name: AX-NV2 cold plate for NVIDIA B200
productLines.note: Direct-to-chip cold plate announced November 13, 2024, described by Mikros as customizable cooling ready for NVIDIA's B200 GPU in the Blackwell generation.

productLines.name: Two-phase microchannel cooling
productLines.note: Mikros designs both single- and two-phase liquid cooling; its site cites heat control at 1,000 W/cm2 and 'Liquid-to-Chip Cooling at the 1 MW Frontier' supercomputer.

facts.text: A September 9, 2026 Global SMT & Packaging feature, 'Liquid Cooling: From Engineering Solutions to Commercial Enterprise', profiled how the Mikros liquid-cooling team moved from collaborative engineering services to commercial cold-plate production at scale under Jabil.
On November 13, 2024, Mikros announced the AX-NV2 direct-to-chip cold plate, described as customizable cooling ready for NVIDIA's B200 GPU (Blackwell).

Jabil completed its acquisition of Mikros Technologies on October 1, 2024 (announced October 3, 2024), bringing proprietary microchannel cold plates able to cool over one kilowatt per square centimeter into Jabil's AI data-center offering.

faq.q: What heat flux can Mikros cold plates handle?
faq.a: Mikros materials cite microchannel cold plates that can cool over one kilowatt per square centimeter, and the company's site states heat-flux control at 1,000 W/cm2; designs span single- and two-phase operation.

faq.q: Which NVIDIA GPUs does Mikros support?
faq.a: Mikros announced the AX-NV2 direct-to-chip cold plate on November 13, 2024 as customizable cooling ready for NVIDIA's B200 GPU in the Blackwell generation.

faq.q: Who owns Mikros today?
faq.a: Mikros operates as a Jabil company; Jabil completed the acquisition on October 1, 2024 and announced it on October 3, 2024 to support demand for liquid cooling in AI data centers.

faq.q: Has Mikros liquid cooling been used at supercomputer scale?
faq.a: Mikros' site cites 'Liquid-to-Chip Cooling at the 1 MW Frontier', referencing its liquid-to-chip cooling technology at the 1 MW scale of the Frontier supercomputer.

profiles.name: Lennox International
profiles.tagline: Lennox International is an NYSE-listed HVAC manufacturer with more than 130 years of thermal expertise. Its new Lennox Data Center Solutions unit offers PhaseFlow, a modular refrigerant-based heat rejection platform for AI and high-density data centers that supports single- and two-phase direct-to-chip cooling strategies.

productLines.name: PhaseFlow
productLines.note: Modular, scalable, refrigerant-based heat rejection platform: cools the process fluid for rack-level heat removal, supports air cooling plus single- and two-phase direct-to-chip strategies, and delivers refrigerant directly to CDUs, with air-cooled or optional low-water adiabatic configurations.

productLines.name: PhaseFlow waterless configuration
productLines.note: Waterless PhaseFlow setup excludes cooling towers and cooling-tower water use and is stated at zero operational water, with N+1 redundancy as baseline and N+X or 2N options.

facts.text: Lennox's PhaseFlow data center pages cite modeling by Syska Hennessy Group that found 10-25% lower energy use than conventional chillers in a 200 MW reference architecture using Phoenix BIN weather data.

Lennox Data Center Solutions presents PhaseFlow as a modular cooling platform built for AI and high-density data centers, in which a single refrigerant-based facility loop supports air cooling plus single-phase and two-phase direct-to-chip cooling strategies

faq.q: What is PhaseFlow?
faq.a: PhaseFlow is Lennox's modular, scalable, refrigerant-based cooling platform for data centers. It operates in the heat rejection loop, cooling the process fluid responsible for rack-level heat removal, and supports air cooling plus single- and two-phase direct-to-chip cooling strategies.

faq.q: Does PhaseFlow support direct-to-chip liquid cooling?
faq.a: Yes. Lennox states PhaseFlow supports single- and two-phase direct-to-chip cooling strategies and delivers refrigerant directly to CDUs, noting additional efficiency potential with two-phase liquid cooling architectures.

faq.q: How water-efficient is PhaseFlow?
faq.a: PhaseFlow's waterless configuration excludes cooling towers and is stated at zero operational water use; an optional low-water adiabatic configuration is also offered, with refrigerants including CO2 and lower-GWP HFO/HFC options.

faq.q: Is Lennox new to data centers?
faq.a: Lennox introduced Lennox Data Center Solutions on November 19, 2026, applying its stated 130+ years of thermal expertise to AI and high-density data center cooling, starting with the PhaseFlow platform.

profiles.name: Nautilus Data Technologies
profiles.tagline: Nautilus Data Technologies develops the EcoCore liquid-cooling platform - in-row, facility-wide and containerized CDUs rated up to 10 MW of heat rejection with zero-water cooling technology - and operates its own waterborne Stockton data center, targeting AI retrofits and new builds.

productLines.name: EcoCore FCD
productLines.note: Facility-wide CDU providing 4,000 kW of heat rejection per unit; supports hot aisle, rear-door, immersion and direct-to-chip cooling, deployed as skidded units off the white space per Nautilus' retrofit guidance.

productLines.name: EcoCore XCD
productLines.note: Perimeter-deployable containerized CDU rated up to 10 MW of heat rejection per module, placing facility-scale liquid cooling outside the data hall.

productLines.name: EcoCore RCD
productLines.note: In-row CDU rejecting up to 2 MW of heat in 1.2 m2 of floor space, available in liquid-to-liquid and liquid-to-air configurations.

productLines.name: EcoCore Infrastructure
productLines.note: Prefabricated 2.5 MW blocks made of nine combined units covering MEP, structure and data hall; Nautilus states the platform scales from 500 kW to multi-megawatt capacity in under 9 months with N+1 redundancy.

facts.text: Nautilus announced on August 4, 2026 that it had been named an NVIDIA AI Infrastructure Partner, supporting its EcoCore liquid-cooling platform for AI workloads.
Nautilus announced on May 27, 2026 that its cooling unit surpassed AI GPU performance targets.
On September 8, 2025, Nautilus announced an expanded suite of EcoCore CDU products for AI data center cooling.

faq.q: What rack densities does Nautilus cooling target?
faq.a: Nautilus materials frame legacy designs at 5-15 kW per rack against AI loads pushing 50 kW, 100 kW and beyond; its 2015 waterborne prototype achieved a PUE of 1.05 with 75 kW rack densities, later 120 kW.

faq.q: Is Nautilus a component vendor or an operator?
faq.a: Both: it sells the EcoCore CDU product line and operates its own Stockton data center, where its waterborne approach was first prototyped in 2015 and recognized by the US Navy and NetApp.

faq.q: How fast can EcoCore capacity be deployed?
faq.a: Nautilus states the platform scales from 500 kW to multi-megawatt capacity in under 9 months, with N+1 redundancy and prefabricated 2.5 MW blocks that combine MEP, structure and data hall units.

faq.q: What does Nautilus recommend for AI retrofits?
faq.a: Its retrofit guidance says most near-term AI capacity comes from existing colocation, hyperscale and enterprise sites, and that facility-scale CDUs let operators phase in high-density AI cooling alongside live workloads with minimal disruption.

profiles.name: NextGenergy
profiles.tagline: NextGenergy, a Toronto company incorporated in 2025, supplies prefabricated liquid-cooling systems for AI data halls - factory-built skids, ORv3 racks, CDUs and cooling plant - plus liquid-loop testing, commissioning and field services across North America; its founding team credits nearly 1,000 MW of prior liquid-cooling delivery.

productLines.name: Prefabricated cooling skids
productLines.note: Factory-built skids for AI data halls, designed or integrated by NextGenergy and built by qualified manufacturing partners; performance is confirmed per project rather than quoted as fixed ratings.

productLines.name: CDUs (integrated per project)
productLines.note: CDUs are selected from several manufacturers per project, with data sheets covering rated heat load (kW), flows, pressure drop, pump redundancy (N, N+1, 2N), MAWP and wetted materials at stated conditions.

productLines.name: Racks, manifolds and cold plates
productLines.note: ORv3 and 19-inch racks, rack manifolds and quick disconnects, plus direct-to-chip cold plates and coolants within its prefabricated platform offering.

productLines.name: Liquid-loop field services
productLines.note: Liquid-loop testing, commissioning and operations across North America, organized around a four-gate commissioning process and a three-tier operations programme.

facts.text: On November 18, 2026, NextGenergy published a white paper on commissioning and site acceptance for liquid-cooled AI data centres.
On October 1, 2026, NextGenergy opened registration for its Liquid Cooling Academy, a free Level 1 technician course offered in English and Chinese.

NextGenergy states it was incorporated in 2025; its founding team's liquid-cooling experience runs from 2020, with nearly 1,000 MW delivered through a previous company counted to the first quarter of 2026.

faq.q: Does NextGenergy manufacture its own CDUs?
faq.a: No. NextGenergy selects CDUs from several manufacturers per project; its data sheets cover rated heat load (kW), flows, pressure drop, pump redundancy (N, N+1, 2N), MAWP and wetted materials at stated conditions, with performance confirmed per project.

faq.q: What experience does the founding team have?
faq.a: The company states its founding team delivered nearly 1,000 MW of liquid cooling through a previous company, counted to the first quarter of 2026, with six years of liquid-cooling focus dating from 2020.

faq.q: What services come with the hardware?
faq.a: Field services cover liquid-loop testing, commissioning and operations across North America, organized around four commissioning gates and a three-tier operations programme.

faq.q: What training resources does NextGenergy offer?
faq.a: It opened registration for a free Level 1 Liquid Cooling Academy technician course in October 2026, runs a browser-based liquid cooling simulator, and published a white paper on commissioning and site acceptance for liquid-cooled AI data centres.

profiles.name: NIBCO
profiles.tagline: NIBCO INC., an Elkhart, Indiana manufacturer of valves and fittings, offers a comprehensive hydronic portfolio for data center liquid cooling - ball, butterfly, check and balancing valves, strainers, actuators and air separators - led by the 585HP ball valve rated up to 1,000 PSI.

productLines.name: Liquid-cooling valve portfolio
productLines.note: Ball valves, butterfly valves, check valves, balancing valves, strainers, actuators and air separators positioned as a full range of hydronic system components for data center cooling from a single manufacturer.

productLines.name: NIBCO 585HP ball valve
productLines.note: High-performance ball valve rated up to 1,000 PSI for high-pressure data center cooling loops, backed by extended warranties per NIBCO's liquid-cooling article.

facts.text: NIBCO's August 12, 2026 article presented its comprehensive data-center liquid-cooling portfolio - ball, butterfly, check and balancing valves, strainers, actuators and air separators - led by the 585HP high-performance ball valve rated up to 1,000 PSI.

The same August 2026 article states the portfolio's valves and fittings use lead-free copper alloys and low-carbon stainless steel, chosen for durability and compatibility with modern cooling fluids such as propylene glycol and deionized water.

faq.q: What NIBCO products apply to data center liquid cooling?
faq.a: NIBCO's article lists ball valves, butterfly valves, check valves, balancing valves, strainers, actuators and air separators as a full range of hydronic components from a single manufacturer, led by the 585HP high-performance ball valve rated up to 1,000 PSI.

faq.q: What materials and fluids are the valves designed for?
faq.a: Valves and fittings are made of lead-free copper alloys and low-carbon stainless steel, chosen for durability and compatibility with modern cooling fluids; the article names propylene glycol and deionized water.

faq.q: Where is NIBCO based?
faq.a: NIBCO INC. lists its address as 1516 Middlebury Street, Elkhart, Indiana, in the contact details of its liquid-cooling blog post.

faq.q: What rack densities does NIBCO cite as the driver?
faq.a: The article frames rising rack densities - from around 15 kW toward more than 100 kW - as the driver for reliable hydronic components in next-generation data center cooling loops.

profiles.name: Molex
profiles.tagline: Molex, a Koch-owned connectivity and electronics manufacturer based in Lisle, Illinois, supplies OCP-compliant liquid-cooling interfaces, cold plate cages, leak-detection cables and liquid-cooled busbars; its multi-channel liquid-cooled busbars support currents up to 15,000 A for AI racks approaching the 1-MW threshold.

productLines.name: Multi-Channel Liquid Cooled Busbars
productLines.note: Liquid-cooled power busbars with up to seven coolant channels, supporting currents up to 15,000 A (roadmap to 25,000 A) with a stated 15C T-Rise at 15,000 A; Molex simulations cite up to 20% greater cooling efficiency than single-channel designs, with ORV3 and HPR footprint compatibility.

productLines.name: VaporConnect Optical Feedthrough Modules
productLines.note: Cassette-based sealed optical feedthroughs for two-phase immersion tanks, up to 576 fibers per module with MPO, LC and VSFF connector options and helium-leak-tested gaskets; reference designs became commercially available in Q1 2025.

productLines.name: OCP-compliant liquid-cooling interfaces and cold plate cages
productLines.note: Blind-mate, dry-break liquid-cooling interfaces plus integrated cold plate cages and floating thermal bridges that move heat away from processors and transceivers while reducing fluid ingress risk during maintenance.

productLines.name: Leak Detection Cables
productLines.note: Leak-detection cables with integrated telemetry that detect moisture and fluid anomalies early across liquid-cooled and immersion-cooled AI infrastructure.

facts.text: At Computex 2026 (announced June 2, 2026), Molex debuted Multi-Channel Liquid Cooled Busbars supporting currents up to 15,000 A with a 15C T-Rise, up to seven coolant channels and up to 20% greater cooling efficiency than single-channel designs in Molex simulations, compatible with ORV3 and HPR mechanical standards.

Molex's VaporConnect optical feedthrough reference designs became commercially available in Q1 2025, per the September 23, 2024 introduction of the cassette-based modules for two-phase immersion cooling tanks.
On September 23, 2024, Molex introduced VaporConnect Optical Feedthrough Modules for two-phase immersion cooling, with up to 576 fibers per module and MPO, LC and VSFF connector options.

faq.q: What is Molex's liquid-cooled busbar?
faq.a: Debuted at Computex 2026, the Multi-Channel Liquid Cooled Busbar integrates liquid cooling into the power path, with up to seven coolant channels, currents up to 15,000 A (roadmap to 25,000 A) and a 15C T-Rise at 15,000 A; Molex simulations cite up to 20% greater cooling efficiency than single-channel designs.

faq.q: Which mechanical standards does it fit?
faq.a: The busbars maintain footprint compatibility with ORV3 and HPR mechanical standards and work with dielectric and non-dielectric liquids, easing integration into existing facility cooling loops and transitions toward 1-MW rack architectures.

faq.q: What does Molex offer for leak safety?
faq.a: OCP-compliant dry-break liquid-cooling interfaces reduce fluid ingress risk during maintenance, and leak-detection cables with integrated telemetry detect moisture and fluid anomalies early in liquid-cooled and immersion-cooled environments.

faq.q: Is Molex a cold plate maker?
faq.a: Molex positions integrated cold plate cages and thermal bridges within its thermal management ecosystem, moving heat away from processors and transceivers alongside connectivity products such as Mirror Mezz connectors (up to 270 differential pairs) and PowerWize.

profiles.name: Modexus Solutions (Airedale)
profiles.tagline: Airedale by Modine is the data center cooling brand of Modine Manufacturing, whose Data Centers & Commercial HVAC business now operates as Modexus Solutions following a shareholder-approved corporate name change. It builds DCS chillers from 200 kW to 3+MW, 400 kW-2 MW+ coolant distribution units and edge cooling for AI infrastructure.

productLines.name: Coolant Distribution Units (CDU)
productLines.note: Liquid-liquid heat exchanger CDU rated 400 kW to 2 MW+ with N+1 pumps, drives and filters; a skid-based CDU for scalable data center deployment was unveiled in October 2025.

productLines.name: DCS chillers (TurboChill, DeltaChill, OptiChill)
productLines.note: TurboChill DCS rated 200-1,830 kW, DeltaChill DCS 110-1,010 kW and OptiChill DCS 1.85 MW using R134a; TurboChill DCS gained a stainless-steel extension for liquid-cooled data centers in November 2025, and TurboChill 3+MW launched in February 2026.

productLines.name: EdgeBox 10
productLines.note: Edge data center cooling unit with a 10 kW thermal load (18 kW with appropriate heat rejection), 5.6 sq ft footprint, stated partial PUE of 1.03 and 8RU of server capacity at under 60 dB.

facts.text: On May 26, 2026, Modine announced a long-term capacity agreement with a strategic data center customer that guarantees supply of Airedale by Modine cooling products for calendar years 2027 through 2029.
In February 2026, Airedale by Modine launched TurboChill 3+MW chillers, advancing air-cooled efficiency for AI data centers.
In November 2025, Airedale by Modine announced a stainless steel extension of the TurboChill DCS chiller for liquid cooling data centers, following an October 2025 unveiling of its skid-based CDU.
In August 2025, Modine opened an India facility to manufacture data center cooling equipment for the APAC region.

faq.q: What CDU capacity does Airedale by Modine offer?
faq.a: Its CDU is a liquid-liquid heat exchanger rated 400 kW to 2 MW+ with N+1 pumps, drives and filters; a skid-based CDU for scalable deployment was unveiled in October 2025.

faq.q: Which chillers serve liquid-cooled AI data centers?
faq.a: The DCS line spans TurboChill DCS (200-1,830 kW), DeltaChill DCS (110-1,010 kW) and OptiChill DCS (1.85 MW, R134a); a stainless-steel TurboChill DCS extension for liquid-cooling data centers followed in November 2025, and TurboChill 3+MW launched in February 2026.

faq.q: Who owns Airedale?
faq.a: Airedale products are branded 'Airedale by Modine'; Modine's Data Centers & Commercial HVAC business now operates as Modexus Solutions after shareholders approved a corporate name change, and the company trades as NYSE: MOD.

faq.q: Does Airedale serve edge deployments?
faq.a: The EdgeBox 10 handles a 10 kW thermal load (18 kW with appropriate heat rejection) in a 5.6 sq ft footprint, with a stated partial PUE of 1.03 and 8RU of server capacity at under 60 dB.

profiles.name: Sanmina
profiles.tagline: Sanmina is a US electronics manufacturing services provider that completed its acquisition of ZT Systems' data center infrastructure manufacturing business from AMD on October 27, 2025, adding large New Jersey and Texas facilities with advanced liquid cooling capabilities for cloud and AI rack integration.

productLines.name: ZT Systems rack integration (Sanmina business)
productLines.note: Data center infrastructure manufacturing business acquired from AMD in October 2025; large state-of-the-art facilities in New Jersey and Texas described as having advanced liquid cooling capabilities, plus an operation in the Netherlands, serving hyperscaler and OEM customers.

productLines.name: AI, Compute & Storage Infrastructure
productLines.note: Sanmina product line covering cloud and AI infrastructure manufacturing, listed alongside Thermal & Power Systems on the company's corporate page.

productLines.name: Thermal & Power Systems
productLines.note: Sanmina product line listed on its corporate page, covering thermal and power systems manufacturing for its communications networks and cloud infrastructure end markets.

facts.text: Sanmina completed its acquisition of ZT Systems' data center infrastructure manufacturing business from AMD on October 27, 2025, adding large manufacturing facilities in New Jersey and Texas with advanced liquid cooling capabilities and an operation in the Netherlands.

Under the completed transaction, Sanmina becomes a preferred NPI manufacturing partner for AMD cloud rack and cluster-scale AI solutions, and the company states the deal expands its ability to serve hyperscaler and OEM customers in the Cloud and AI end-market.

faq.q: What did Sanmina acquire from AMD?
faq.a: Sanmina completed the acquisition of ZT Systems' data center infrastructure manufacturing business on October 27, 2025. The deal adds large manufacturing facilities in New Jersey and Texas with advanced liquid cooling capabilities, plus an operation in the Netherlands.

faq.q: Does Sanmina manufacture AI rack-scale systems?
faq.a: Sanmina states it becomes a preferred NPI manufacturing partner for AMD cloud rack and cluster-scale AI solutions, and that the acquisition deepens hyperscaler relationships across its Cloud and AI end market.

faq.q: Where is Sanmina headquartered and how is it listed?
faq.a: The October 2025 announcement was issued from San Jose, California, and the release identifies Sanmina Corporation as trading on NASDAQ under the ticker SANM.

faq.q: Where does Sanmina perform liquid-cooled rack integration?
faq.a: Through the acquired ZT Systems business: large manufacturing facilities in New Jersey and Texas described as having advanced liquid cooling capabilities, plus an operation in the Netherlands.

profiles.name: Smardt
profiles.tagline: Smardt is a Montreal, Canada chiller manufacturer describing oil-free innovation since 2005. Its data center range spans a 300-2,500 kW coolant distribution unit, chilled-water fan walls, CRAH/CRAC units, dry coolers and chillers up to 12,660 kW that the company says support warmer-water and direct-to-chip liquid cooling loops.

productLines.name: Coolant Distribution Unit (CDU)
productLines.note: 300-2,500 kW (85-711 TR) CDU that transfers heat from liquid-cooled IT equipment to the facility water loop; secondary rated flow 20.4-196.5 m3/h, temperature control +/-0.5 C, differential pressure +/-0.1 bar, primary side 35 C, secondary up to 39 C, sound level up to 65 dB(A), redundant core components.

productLines.name: Water-cooled oil-free chillers
productLines.note: Core range 160-5,625 kW and Ultra range 1,055-12,660 kW water-cooled chillers; the company describes oil-free innovation since 2005 across its chiller portfolio.

productLines.name: Air-cooled chillers
productLines.note: AeroPure AF 211-2,500 kW, AE/AD 140-1,760 kW and E-Class 160-1,860 kW air-cooled chiller ranges for heat rejection duty.

productLines.name: Data center air products
productLines.note: Chilled Water Fan Wall 85-500 kW, Dual Cooling Source Fan Wall 45-250 kW, CRAH 35-230 kW and CRAC 30-90 kW for white-space cooling alongside the liquid cooling line.

productLines.name: Dry Cooler
productLines.note: 340-1,418 kW dry coolers that reject heat from liquid cooling loops using outdoor air, with optional spray/wet-film enhancement, modular capacity expansion and EC fans.

facts.text: Smardt exhibited at Data Centre World Asia 2026 at Marina Bay Sands, Singapore (29 September 2026) and presented its data center cooling expertise in Guangzhou, China (21 March 2026).

Smardt documented a rapid-replacement chiller deployment for a mission-critical New York-region data center, with chillers of roughly 400 TR per unit delivered in early 2025 after one chiller was damaged in transport just before delivery.

faq.q: What coolant distribution units does Smardt offer for data centers?
faq.a: A single CDU product line covering 300-2,500 kW (85-711 TR), with secondary rated flow of 20.4-196.5 m3/h, temperature control of +/-0.5 C, differential pressure control of +/-0.1 bar, primary side 35 C and secondary side up to 39 C.

faq.q: Does Smardt support direct-to-chip liquid cooling?
faq.a: The company states that its chillers, dry coolers and CDUs support warmer water and direct-to-chip loops, responding to the shift to liquid cooling for AI and high-density compute.

faq.q: What heat rejection options does Smardt provide for liquid cooling loops?
faq.a: Dry coolers from 340 to 1,418 kW with EC fans and optional spray or wet-film enhancement, plus air-cooled chillers up to 2,500 kW and water-cooled chillers up to 12,660 kW.

faq.q: Where is Smardt based and since when?
faq.a: Smardt's site lists locations in the Montreal area (Dorval and Kirkland), Quebec, Canada, and the company describes oil-free innovation since 2005.

profiles.name: Old World Industries
profiles.tagline: Old World Industries is a Northbrook, Illinois producer of automotive and commercial fluids whose THERMAL CHARGE glycol heat transfer fluid line targets data center liquid cooling. Its prediluted PG25 propylene glycol fluid is rated for direct-to-chip liquid cooling, closed-loop systems and data center cooling loops.

productLines.name: THERMAL CHARGE PG25 Heat Transfer Fluid
productLines.note: Prediluted, ready-to-use propylene glycol/deionized water formula with a proprietary corrosion inhibitor package; freeze point 12 F (-11 C), boiling point 213 F (101 C); rated for direct-to-chip liquid cooling, closed-loop systems and data center cooling; sold in bulk or 55-gallon drums.

productLines.name: THERMAL CHARGE propylene glycol fluids
productLines.note: Propylene glycol heat transfer fluid variants including PG, PG Orange, PGSE, PGXL and PGHD within the commercial THERMAL CHARGE brand, alongside PEAK and FINAL CHARGE coolants.

productLines.name: THERMAL CHARGE ethylene glycol fluids
productLines.note: Ethylene glycol heat transfer fluid variants including EG, EGSE, EGHD, XL and XL NOAT for commercial closed-loop cooling applications.

facts.text: On October 14, 2026 OWI published industry guidance on heat transfer fluid liquid cooling reducing data center costs, citing cooling energy cut by up to 90 percent, facility-wide energy use reduced 20-30 percent and server hardware life extended by up to 25 percent.

A July 15, 2026 OWI article on data center heat transfer described glycol-based closed-loop cooling for direct-to-chip cold plates, immersion cooling and rear-door heat exchangers, and promoted THERMAL CHARGE PG25 as its fluid for these liquid cooling loops.

faq.q: Which OWI fluid is rated for direct-to-chip liquid cooling?
faq.a: THERMAL CHARGE PG25, a prediluted propylene glycol/deionized water formula with a proprietary corrosion inhibitor package, freeze point of 12 F (-11 C) and boiling point of 213 F (101 C), sold in bulk or 55-gallon drums; the company claims it has one of the longest service lifespans of any glycol HTF on the market.

faq.q: What glycol chemistries does the THERMAL CHARGE line cover?
faq.a: Propylene glycol variants (PG, PG Orange, PGSE, PGXL, PGHD) and ethylene glycol variants (EG, EGSE, EGHD, XL, XL NOAT), with PG25 as the prediluted data center offering.

faq.q: Where is Old World Industries headquartered?
faq.a: At 3100 Sanders Road, Suite 400, Northbrook, Illinois 60062; the company cites five decades of liquid cooling expertise and 50 Years of Excellence on its site, but states no founding year.

faq.q: What benefits does OWI cite for glycol liquid cooling in data centers?
faq.a: In its October 14, 2026 industry article OWI cites cooling energy cut by up to 90 percent, facility-wide energy use reduced 20-30 percent, an 18-24 month payback period, and server hardware life extended by up to 25 percent.

profiles.name: Nortek Data Center Cooling
profiles.tagline: Nortek Data Center Cooling, part of Madison Air and based in Oklahoma City, supplies coolant distribution units for AI and hyperscale data centers. Its CDU line covers 300 kW to over 1.2 MW in compact 2N-redundant form factors serving direct liquid cooling plates, rear-door heat exchangers and in-row coolers.

productLines.name: Coolant Distribution Units (CDU)
productLines.note: Liquid cooling CDUs supplying coolant directly to technical racks at 300 kW to over 1.2 MW; down to 48U size; 2N redundancy as default with hot-swappable components; moves heat from a closed-loop pressurized secondary circuit to a chilled-water primary loop, serving liquid cooling plates, rear-door heat exchangers and in-row coolers.

productLines.name: Skidded CDU (announced)
productLines.note: Announced skidded CDU configurable from 1 MW to more than 5 MW in the base offering, with interconnected modules scaling beyond 10 MW, aimed at high-density AI, HPC and hyperscale operators who would otherwise line up multiple 1 MW units.

productLines.name: CoilWall Series
productLines.note: Fan coil wall units bringing cooled air into data center halls; packaged cabinet design with minimal onsite construction, modular customizable variants (CoilWall Array, Base, Cased), in-house optimized coils, high-performance fans and free-cooling support using outdoor air.

productLines.name: CRAH and RDHX families
productLines.note: Computer room air handlers and rear-door heat exchanger product families listed alongside the CDU and CoilWall lines; the site notes related patented technology also appears in Nortek CRAHs, StatePoint and custom air handlers.

facts.text: In October 2025 Nortek announced a skidded CDU for liquid-cooled data centers configurable from 1 MW to more than 5 MW, with interconnected modules able to scale beyond 10 MW, targeted at high-density AI, HPC and hyperscale deployments.

The same announcement notes that Nortek DCC deployed its StatePoint liquid cooling technology at Empyrion Digital's 29.4 MW KR1 Gangnam data center in Seoul, South Korea, and lists DigitalEdge as a customer in the Philippines.

faq.q: What CDU capacities does Nortek Data Center Cooling offer?
faq.a: The standard CDU line ranges from 300 kW to over 1.2 MW in sizes down to 48U with 2N redundancy as default; an announced skidded CDU is configurable from 1 MW to more than 5 MW, with interconnected modules scaling beyond 10 MW.

faq.q: What loads can Nortek CDUs serve?
faq.a: Direct liquid-cooling plates, rear-door heat exchangers and in-row coolers; the CDU moves heat from a closed-loop pressurized secondary circuit into a chilled-water primary loop and is marketed as AI-ready for hyperscale, colocation and edge applications.

faq.q: Who owns Nortek Data Center Cooling?
faq.a: The company's own announcement describes Nortek DCC as part of Madison Air; its headquarters address is 200 W. John Kilpatrick Service Road, Oklahoma City, Oklahoma.

faq.q: Are the larger skidded CDUs shipping today?
faq.a: The 1 MW to 5 MW+ skidded CDU with modules scaling beyond 10 MW is described as announced in October 2025; the shipping line documented on the CDU product page remains 300 kW to over 1.2 MW.

profiles.name: RLE Technologies (Parameter)
profiles.tagline: RLE leak detection is now a brand of Parameter, formed in 2024 from RLE Technologies and NDSL, the Cellwatch parent. Its XD Series modular platform is purpose-built for liquid-cooled AI data centers, alongside the LD Series of sensing cables and spot sensors. Acuity Inc. agreed in October 2026 to acquire Parameter.
profiles.ownership: Brand of Parameter; acquisition by Acuity (NYSE: AYI) agreed in October 2026, closing expected late 2026

productLines.name: XD Series leak detection
productLines.note: Newer modular leak detection line for liquid-cooled AI and data center facilities, featuring native MQTT protocols, PoE+ capability and full-stack local relays, designed for high-density deployments at scale with emphasis on speed, precision and simplified deployment.

productLines.name: LD Series leak detection
productLines.note: Controllers, sensing cables and spot detectors described as built on 40 years of industry technology; usable as a full system or component-by-component with third-party systems, with real-time leak location, configurable thresholds, signal buffering against false alerts, and BMS integration via BACnet, Modbus and SNMP.

productLines.name: CellWatch battery monitoring
productLines.note: Sister Parameter brand from the NDSL side of the merger, providing battery monitoring for mission-critical facilities alongside RLE leak detection and environmental monitoring.

facts.text: On October 26, 2026 Parameter Technologies announced a definitive agreement to be acquired by Acuity Inc. (NYSE: AYI), upon closing becoming part of Distech Controls within the Acuity Intelligent Spaces segment; the transaction is expected to close in late 2026.

Parameter's current line-up includes the XD Series, a modular leak detection platform with native MQTT protocols, PoE+ capability and full-stack local relays, purpose-built for liquid-cooled AI data centers and high-density deployments at scale.

May River Capital announced on December 11, 2024 that NDSL Group, parent of Cellwatch battery monitoring, had merged with RLE Technologies, the Fort Collins leak detection specialist, forming the platform company now operating as Parameter.

faq.q: What is the relationship between RLE Technologies and Parameter?
faq.a: RLE Technologies merged with NDSL Group, the parent of Cellwatch battery monitoring, in a combination announced December 11, 2024 by May River Capital; the merged company operates as Parameter and sells RLE leak detection as a brand.

faq.q: What leak detection does Parameter offer for liquid-cooled AI data centers?
faq.a: The XD Series modular platform with native MQTT protocols, PoE+ capability and full-stack local relays, plus the LD Series of controllers, sensing cables and spot detectors with BACnet, Modbus and SNMP integration.

faq.q: Is Parameter being acquired?
faq.a: Yes. On October 26, 2026 Parameter Technologies announced a definitive agreement to be acquired by Acuity Inc. (NYSE: AYI); upon closing it will become part of Distech Controls within the Acuity Intelligent Spaces segment, with closing expected in late 2026.

faq.q: Where is the company located?
faq.a: Parameter is headquartered at 4557 Denrose Ct, Fort Collins, Colorado, with engineering and service operations in Raleigh, North Carolina and sales and service capabilities in Milton Keynes, United Kingdom.

profiles.name: Penflex
profiles.tagline: Penflex, founded 1902 and based in Gilbertsville, Pennsylvania, manufactures flexible stainless steel hose and braid assemblies used from CDU internals to facility water systems in data center liquid cooling. Its Clean ID manufacturing removes internal lubricants, and the company states it is the first U.S. metal hose manufacturer.

productLines.name: Clean ID hose assemblies
productLines.note: Hose made without internal tooling, lubricants or forming fluid for cleanliness-critical cooling loops; Clean ID P3, introduced as a sister product to the P3 corrugated lineup, targets data center, HVAC and cryogenic applications; assemblies are argon-purged at welding, can be helium mass spectrometer leak tested and bagged for shipment.

productLines.name: P3 Series annular hose
productLines.note: Lightweight, flexible annular corrugated stainless hose for tight spaces, used in CDU connections including pumps, heat exchangers, manifolds and supply/return lines.

productLines.name: P5 Series large diameter hose
productLines.note: Large diameter annular hose used for HVAC connections such as chiller and pump tie-ins in facility water systems serving data centers.

productLines.name: Data Center Hoses
productLines.note: Flexible metal hose assemblies in austenitic stainless steel compatible with glycol and commercial refrigerants, available in diameters from 1/4 in to 24 in, used inside CDUs, as transfer lines between cooling components and as conduit protection.

facts.text: On May 21, 2026 Penflex reported its data center cooling hose feature in Industrial Supply Magazine's May/June 2026 issue, introducing the Clean ID P3, a sister product to the P3 corrugated hose lineup made without internal lubricant, targeted at data center, HVAC and cryogenic applications.

The same May 2026 feature notes that Penflex has expanded production capacity and, driven by Buy American Act requirements, is developing an AIS-certified line of hose and braid that is melted and drawn in the United States from local wire and strip suppliers.

faq.q: What hose assemblies does Penflex offer for data center liquid cooling?
faq.a: Stainless steel braided assemblies in diameters from 1/4 in to 24 in, including Clean ID hose made without internal lubricants, the lightweight P3 annular series and the large-diameter P5 series for HVAC connections.

faq.q: Where are these hoses used in a liquid-cooled facility?
faq.a: Inside cooling distribution units (pumps, heat exchangers, manifolds, supply and return lines), in facility water systems such as chiller and pump connections, and as conduit protection; the company says they support direct-to-chip, immersion and rear-door heat exchanger approaches.

faq.q: What is Clean ID manufacturing?
faq.a: A process that makes hose without internal tooling, lubricants or forming fluid so the inside is clean without post-cleaning; assemblies are TIG welded with argon purging by ASME Section IX certified welders and can be helium mass spectrometer tested.

faq.q: How long has Penflex been in business and where is it located?
faq.a: Penflex dates its start to 1902 and describes itself as the first U.S. metal hose manufacturer; it operates from a 100,000 sq ft headquarters and factory in Gilbertsville, Pennsylvania, with a Houston warehouse added in 2020.

profiles.name: Tranter
profiles.tagline: Tranter manufactures gasketed plate-and-frame and welded shell-and-plate heat exchangers. Its Superchanger line with GT and AT plate series is offered for CDUs in direct-to-chip liquid cooling, free cooling and heat recovery in data centers.

productLines.name: Superchanger with GT plates
productLines.note: Gasketed plate-and-frame heat exchangers positioned by Tranter for high-capacity liquid cooling in modern data center infrastructure, including CDU duty for direct-to-chip cooling; Tranter cites LMTDs as low as 1 K on the GT-165 plate.

productLines.name: AT (AHRI) series
productLines.note: Gasketed plate heat exchanger series with AHRI Certified performance, offered for data center liquid cooling applications including free cooling with cooling tower intermediate duty and seawater free cooling.

productLines.name: Shell and plate heat exchangers
productLines.note: Welded plate-pack units applied as water-cooled chiller evaporators and condensers, heat pump evaporators, high-temperature heat recovery condensers and compressor oil coolers in data center cooling plants.

facts.text: Published the article 'How Tranter plate heat exchangers support data center sustainability' on 17 September 2026, on plate heat exchanger use in data center cooling.
Released the customer case 'Precision cooling for a digital powerhouse' on 28 October 2025, describing a data center precision-cooling application of Tranter plate heat exchangers.

faq.q: What does Tranter supply for data center liquid cooling?
faq.a: Gasketed plate heat exchangers under the Superchanger line, with GT plates for high-capacity liquid cooling and AT plates with AHRI Certified performance, plus welded shell-and-plate units. Tranter lists CDUs for direct-to-chip liquid cooling, free cooling and heat recovery as applications.

faq.q: Where are Tranter plate heat exchangers used in a data center?
faq.a: Tranter lists CDU duty for direct-to-chip liquid cooling, open-air and seawater free cooling, cooling tower intermediate exchangers, chiller evaporators and condensers, and hybrid and high-temperature heat recovery.

faq.q: Does Tranter publish certified performance for data center duty?
faq.a: Yes, the AT (AHRI) plate series is listed with AHRI Certified performance for reliable liquid cooling on Tranter's data centers page; the GT series targets high-capacity liquid cooling.

faq.q: When was Tranter founded and who owns it?
faq.a: Tranter states it was founded in 1932 and has been in business for over 90 years. Its website does not state an owner or parent company, so ownership is NOT_FOUND.

profiles.name: ZAxis
profiles.tagline: ZAxis is a privately owned maker of leak test instruments and precision metering pumps in Salt Lake City. Its testers cover pressure/vacuum decay, mass flow and helium trace-gas methods used to leak-test cold plates, CDUs, manifolds and quick disconnects for data center liquid cooling.

productLines.name: Liquid-Cooling Component Leak Testers

productLines.name: OCP UQDB / OCP BMQC
productLines.note: Blind-mate coupling solutions developed within the OCP initiative: UQDB features +/- 1 mm radial misalignment tolerance, while BMQC tolerates +/- 5 mm radial and 2.7 degrees angular misalignment, suiting chassis moving in and out of racks.

productLines.name: LQC for CDUs
productLines.note: Non-drip high-flow quick coupling with a screw-to-connect mechanism for data center Coolant Distribution Units, offering high flow capacity, minimal pressure drop and connection under working pressure.

productLines.name: ultraFLOW
productLines.note: Compact, lightweight flat-face non-drip quick connectors with low pressure drop, designed for connecting and disconnecting immersion cooling tanks in limited spaces while carrying facility cooling water.

facts.text: As of 2026, CEJN's data center page lists OCP UQD hand-mate couplings with spill-free hot-swap function, OCP UQDB blind-mate couplings with +/- 1 mm radial misalignment tolerance, OCP BMQC with +/- 5 mm radial and 2.7 degree angular tolerance, and screw-to-connect CDU couplings.
CEJN launched ultraFLOW, a quick connector for liquid cooling of electronics, in 2018, after beginning to launch quick connectors for liquid cooling in the late 2010s.

faq.q: What does CEJN offer for data center liquid cooling?
faq.a: OCP UQD hand-mate couplings for manifolds, OCP UQDB and BMQC blind-mate couplings for chassis, screw-to-connect high-flow couplings for CDUs, and ultraFLOW flat-face couplings for immersion cooling tanks.

faq.q: What misalignment tolerances do the blind-mate couplings have?
faq.a: The OCP UQDB features +/- 1 mm radial misalignment tolerance; the OCP BMQC has +/- 5 mm radial and 2.7 degrees angular misalignment tolerance, per the CEJN data center page.

faq.q: Is CEJN involved in the Open Compute Project?
faq.a: CEJN states it is a contributor to the OCP community, designing interchangeable quick connect solutions alongside industry and chassis manufacturers, and says UQDB and BMQC were developed within OCP with CEJN as one of the main contributors.

faq.q: Who owns CEJN and where is it based?
faq.a: CEJN AB in Skovde, Sweden, is the international head office; the company describes itself as an independent, family-owned business founded in 1955 and now led by the third generation of owners.

profiles.name: Boston Limited
profiles.tagline: Boston Limited is a UK-based server and AI infrastructure solutions provider active for over three decades. It sells GlacierCore CDUs and liquid, immersion and rear-door cooling deployments, integrating partner technologies from Castrol, LM TEK, Submer, Supermicro and ZutaCore.
profiles.ownership: Subsidiary of SourceCode (per Boston site branding)

productLines.name: GlacierCore CDU line
productLines.note: Models 1100-0, 1110-0, 1200-0, 1210-0 and 1220-0 are featured as Boston's liquid cooling solutions; the page does not publish kW or flow specifications for these units.

productLines.name: Immersion cooling deployments
productLines.note: Full-system immersion in dielectric, non-conductive liquid within sealed tanks, described with protection against short circuits and airborne contaminants and heat capture through a heat exchanger for reuse or recovery.

productLines.name: Single- and two-phase DLC and RDHx
productLines.note: Single-phase DLC cools CPUs, GPUs and memory via cold plates; two-phase DLC uses a dielectric fluid that boils at approximately 40-50 degrees C inside the cold plate; RDHx rear doors cool hot exhaust air for retrofit environments.

productLines.name: Partner cooling portfolio
productLines.note: Boston lists cooling solution partners: Castrol ON immersion fluids, LM TEK liquid cooling, Submer end-to-end immersion systems, Supermicro liquid-cooled server platforms and ZutaCore direct-on-chip technology.

facts.text: Boston's liquid cooling page (published January 2026, updated November 2026) features the GlacierCore line - models 1100-0, 1110-0, 1200-0, 1210-0 and 1220-0 - and cooling types spanning immersion, single- and two-phase DLC and rear-door heat exchangers.

The same page names Castrol ON immersion fluids, LM TEK liquid cooling, Submer immersion systems, Supermicro liquid-cooled server platforms and ZutaCore direct-on-chip technology as Boston's cooling solution partners.

faq.q: What liquid cooling types does Boston offer?
faq.a: Immersion cooling in sealed dielectric tanks, single-phase direct liquid cooling with cold plates on CPUs, GPUs and memory, two-phase DLC with a dielectric boiling at roughly 40-50 degrees C, and RDHx rear-door systems for retrofit environments.

faq.q: Which GlacierCore CDU models are featured?
faq.a: GlacierCore 1100-0, 1110-0, 1200-0, 1210-0 and 1220-0 appear as featured liquid cooling solutions; no kW or flow specifications are published on the page.

faq.q: Which cooling partners does Boston work with?
faq.a: Castrol (ON immersion fluids), LM TEK (liquid cooling solutions), Submer (immersion systems), Supermicro (liquid-cooled server platforms) and ZutaCore (direct-on-chip cooling), per the Boston liquid cooling page.

faq.q: Who is Boston Limited?
faq.a: A UK-based solutions provider of servers, storage, workstations and AI infrastructure, active for over three decades, with presence listed across the UK, USA, Austria, Australia, France, Germany, India, Taiwan, South Africa and Switzerland.

profiles.name: Corintis
profiles.tagline: Swiss cooling-technology company developing microfluidic, chip-tailored liquid cooling: it designs, builds, tests and mass-produces microfluidic cold plates and co-packaged cooling for high-power data-center chips, with a Glacierware design platform in closed beta.

productLines.name: Microfluidic cold plates and co-packaged cooling
