productLines.note: Targeted microfluidic cooling tailored per chip; the company's platform covers design, build, test and mass production, targeting higher TDP with less flow rate and pressure drop. Homepage demo graphic cites a GPU at 1893 W with 40 °C+ inlet temperature.

productLines.name: Glacierware design platform
productLines.note: Cold-plate design platform listed as 'currently in closed beta'; positioned as the company's design environment for liquid-cooling co-design.

productLines.name: Cooling co-design services
productLines.note: Services for designing and validating liquid-cooling architectures for data-center and HPC applications, from co-design through testing.

facts.text: Corintis's Glacierware design platform is listed as 'currently in closed beta' on the company site, which also lists offices in Saint-Sulpice (Switzerland), Munich (Germany) and Bellevue, WA (USA).

Microsoft announced a cooling collaboration with Corintis: lab-scale microfluidic channels etched into the silicon removed heat up to three times better than cold plates (depending on workload and configuration) and cut the maximum temperature rise of silicon inside a GPU by 65 percent, cooling a server running a simulated Teams meeting.

profiles.ocp: Corintis SA co-leads the Cold Plate Performance workstream of OCP's Cooling Environments project, listed alongside ToffeeX and Celestica. Source: https://www.opencompute.org/projects/cooling-environments/cold-plate

faq.q: What does Corintis offer for data-center liquid cooling?
faq.a: Microfluidic cold plates and co-packaged cooling for high-power chips, covering design, build, test and mass production, plus the Glacierware design platform, which is currently in closed beta.

faq.q: Where is Corintis based?
faq.a: Headquartered at Rue des Jordils 38, 1025 Saint-Sulpice, Switzerland, with additional offices in Munich, Germany and Bellevue, Washington (USA).

faq.q: What did Microsoft announce with Corintis in 2025?
faq.a: A lab-scale microfluidic cooling collaboration: channels etched into the silicon removed heat up to three times better than cold plates and reduced the maximum temperature rise of silicon in a GPU by 65 percent.

faq.q: What is Corintis's role in the OCP?
faq.a: Corintis SA co-leads the Cold Plate Performance workstream within OCP's Cooling Environments project, listed alongside ToffeeX and Celestica.

profiles.name: Exaion
profiles.tagline: French operator of secure HPC/AI cloud data centres using immersion cooling, refurbished hardware and exclusively low-carbon energy, with waste heat recovered through local loops; it reports 4 data centres and deploys across Europe and North America, and is 64%-owned by MARA France since February 2026.
profiles.ownership: Subsidiary of MARA - MARA France acquired 64% of share capital (Feb 2026); EDF Group remains a minority shareholder

productLines.name: Immersion-cooled HPC/AI private cloud
productLines.note: Private cloud infrastructure and managed services for AI/HPC built on refurbished hardware, immersion cooling techniques and exclusively low-carbon energy; site lists 1,250 GPUs, 37 PB of storage and 99.9% availability across 4 data centres, hosted in its own data centres or on client premises.

productLines.name: Enterprise AI PaaS
productLines.note: Platform services for deploying LLMs (RAG, fine-tuning, inference) with open-source orchestration (OpenStack for IaaS, Kubernetes for PaaS); part of the Exaion offering that runs on its immersion-cooled infrastructure.

productLines.name: Waste-heat recovery loops
productLines.note: The company states that waste heat from its data centres is recovered through local loops, with CO2 and energy use monitored continuously.

facts.text: On 20 February 2026 MARA announced that MARA France acquired 64% of Exaion's share capital after French regulatory review; EDF Group remains a minority shareholder and a client, and NJJ acquired a 10% minority stake in MARA France.

Exaion's site lists 4 data centres, 1,250 GPUs and 37 PB of storage at 99.9% availability, states it uses immersion cooling and refurbished hardware powered exclusively by low-carbon energy, and that waste heat is recovered through local loops.

faq.q: Who owns Exaion?
faq.a: MARA France acquired 64% of Exaion's share capital, announced as completed on 20 February 2026; EDF Group remains a minority shareholder and a client, and NJJ holds a 10% minority stake in MARA France.

faq.q: What cooling technology does Exaion use?
faq.a: Its data centres use immersion cooling techniques with refurbished hardware and exclusively low-carbon energy sources; waste heat is recovered through local loops and CO2 and energy use are monitored continuously.

faq.q: What does Exaion sell?
faq.a: High-performance private infrastructure and managed cloud services for AI/HPC, including an Enterprise AI PaaS for LLM deployment (RAG, fine-tuning, inference), hosted in its own data centres or on client premises.

profiles.name: DUG Technology
profiles.tagline: Australian HPC-as-a-service and geoscience company whose patented DUG Cool immersion cooling runs its own data centres (Houston Skybox, called 'among the largest single-phase immersion-cooling deployments in the world' in the BAC announcement) and is licensed exclusively worldwide to Baltimore Aircoil for high-density data centres.

productLines.name: DUG Cool immersion cooling
productLines.note: Patented industrial immersion cooling 'developed by an operator, for operators', refined through production use for over a decade. Site claims power consumption reduced by up to 51% versus a traditional air-cooled data centre, water use reduced by up to 25%, a non-flammable, non-conductive and biodegradable fluid, and 85% less synthetic refrigerants.

productLines.name: DUG Nomad containers
productLines.note: Self-contained cooled containers for low-latency AI inference in edge, remote or integrated environments: the Nomad 10 fits a standard 10 ft Hi-Cube shipping container with up to 80 kW of IT heat rejection; the Nomad 40 scales to 1 MW. Runs NVIDIA H100 GPUs with no external chillers or plumbing.

productLines.name: DUG HPC Cloud (HPCaaS)
productLines.note: High-performance computing as a service from DUG's own immersion-cooled facilities, which the company describes as some of the largest immersion-cooled in the world; serves geoscience and other scientific workloads.

facts.text: DUG's Nomad container line, detailed in 2026-dated brochures, packages its cooling in a standard 10 ft Hi-Cube container: the Nomad 10 rejects up to 80 kW of IT heat and the Nomad 40 up to 1 MW, targeting NVIDIA H100-based AI inference with self-contained cooling and no external chillers.

On 7 August 2024 Baltimore Aircoil Company announced an exclusive worldwide licensing agreement with DUG Technology, covering the patented DUG Cool immersion-cooling technology for high-density data centres, with rights to use, manufacture, market and sell it; DUG's Skybox data centre in Houston was described as among the largest single-phase immersion-cooling deployments in the world.

faq.q: What is DUG Cool?
faq.a: A patented industrial immersion-cooling design refined through more than a decade of production use in DUG's own data centres. The company claims power consumption reduced by up to 51% and water use by up to 25% versus a traditional air-cooled data centre, using a non-flammable, non-conductive, biodegradable fluid.

faq.q: Who can buy DUG Cool technology?
faq.a: Baltimore Aircoil Company holds exclusive worldwide rights to use, manufacture, market and sell the patented DUG Cool technology under an agreement announced 7 August 2024; DUG continues to use it in its own HPC facilities.

faq.q: What is the DUG Nomad?
faq.a: A self-contained containerized data centre line: the Nomad 10 provides up to 80 kW of IT heat rejection in a standard 10 ft Hi-Cube container and the Nomad 40 up to 1 MW, for AI inference in edge or remote sites, with no external chillers or plumbing.

faq.q: What kind of company is DUG?
faq.a: Founded in 2003 and headquartered in West Perth, Australia, DUG Technology (ASX: DUG) provides geoscience services, the DUG Insight software suite and HPC as a service from immersion-cooled data centres.

profiles.name: E4 Computer Engineering
profiles.tagline: Italian HPC and AI system integrator that builds liquid-cooled supercomputing platforms: its EuroHPC TEXTAROSSA work delivered a two-phase, direct on-chip evaporative cooling demonstrator, and a 2025 partnership with UNICOM Engineering brings immersion cooling into its AI infrastructure offering.
profiles.ownership: Private - Italian joint-stock company (S.p.A.); no stock listing stated

productLines.name: Two-phase liquid-cooled servers (TEXTAROSSA/InQuattro)
productLines.note: Direct on-chip evaporative cooling: an aluminum or copper cold plate acts as a multi-micro-channel evaporator on CPU/GPU; dielectric, non-flammable, low-GWP coolant circulates in a hermetically sealed loop with a rack-level liquid-to-liquid condensing unit. Shown on Ampere Mt. Collins 2U with Altra Max (128 cores per socket, TDP up to 250 W, 8 TB memory).

productLines.name: Liquid-cooling retrofit for E4 systems
productLines.note: The two-phase thermal management solution can be applied to selected E4 systems that are already air cooled, replacing air cooling for the CPUs, which E4 identifies as the most thermally sensitive components, with stated improved Power Usage Effectiveness (no numeric PUE published).

productLines.name: Liquid-cooled HPC/AI cluster integration
productLines.note: Design, deployment and support of HPC clusters, AI and hyperconverged infrastructures for academic and industrial customers; since May 2025 paired with UNICOM Engineering's thermal management and immersion cooling solutions for high AI power densities in Italy and Switzerland.

facts.text: On 6 May 2025 UNICOM Engineering and E4 announced a strategic partnership for AI-ready infrastructure in the Italian and Swiss markets: UNICOM Engineering contributes expertise in liquid cooling technologies - thermal management and immersion cooling solutions - and custom servers, while E4 contributes design, deployment and support of complex HPC and AI environments.

At ISC 2023 in Hamburg (21-25 May 2023) E4 presented a server prototype from the EU EuroHPC project TEXTAROSSA with an innovative two-phase cooling system, described by E4 as a world premiere, built on the Ampere Mt. Collins 2U platform with Altra Max processors and aimed at near-future exascale computing.

faq.q: What liquid cooling technology does E4 use?
faq.a: A two-phase, direct on-chip evaporative system: a multi-micro-channel cold plate evaporates a dielectric, non-flammable, low-GWP coolant on the CPU or GPU inside a hermetically sealed loop, with a rack-level liquid-to-liquid condensing unit rejecting the heat.

faq.q: Which hardware has demonstrated it?
faq.a: An Ampere Mt. Collins 2U server with Altra Max ARM processors: dual socket, 128 cores per socket at 3 GHz, TDP up to 250 W per socket, up to 32 DDR4-3200 DIMMs and 8 TB memory, presented at ISC 2023 within the EuroHPC TEXTAROSSA project.

faq.q: What did E4 announce in 2025?
faq.a: A strategic partnership with UNICOM Engineering, announced 6 May 2025, combining UNICOM's liquid cooling technologies (thermal management and immersion cooling) and custom servers with E4's HPC/AI design and deployment for Italian and Swiss customers.

faq.q: Who is E4 Computer Engineering?
faq.a: An Italian company operating since 2002 (site copyright 2002-2021), headquartered in Scandiano, Reggio Emilia, that designs, deploys and supports HPC clusters, cloud, data analytics, AI and hyperconverged infrastructures.

profiles.name: Eviden (Bull)
profiles.tagline: European supercomputer maker whose BullSequana platforms rely on direct liquid cooling: the XH3500, unveiled November 2025, is 100% fanless with 40 °C warm-water facility supply and heat-reuse support, and the XH3000 architecture underlies JUPITER, Europe's first exascale system at Juelich.
profiles.ownership: Part of Atos Group - Eviden is the Atos Group brand for hardware and software products (Eviden SAS)

productLines.name: BullSequana XH3500
productLines.note: Converged HPC/AI supercomputing platform with 100% fanless 5th-generation Direct Liquid Cooling, warm water support (40 °C / 104 °F facility supply), an in-rack Coolant Distribution Unit for simplified scaling, full-rack direct liquid cooling for complete heat capture, and heat-reuse readiness. Unveiled 13 November 2025.

productLines.name: BullSequana XH3000
productLines.note: Supercomputer architecture on which EuroHPC JU's JUPITER is built: approximately 24,000 NVIDIA GH200 Grace Hopper Superchips delivering 1 exaflop, with a highly efficient warm-water cooling system whose waste heat is integrated into the Juelich campus heating network.

productLines.name: Direct liquid cooling subsystems
productLines.note: Rack-level liquid cooling implementation across the BullSequana XH line: in-rack CDUs, full-rack direct liquid cooling for complete heat capture and support for heat reuse and free-cooling strategies for greener operations.

facts.text: On 17 November 2025 EuroHPC JU announced that JUPITER, built on Eviden's BullSequana XH3000 architecture with approximately 24,000 NVIDIA GH200 Grace Hopper Superchips, propels Europe into the exascale era at 1 exaflop; its warm-water cooling feeds waste heat into the Juelich campus heating network and it ranked number 4 on the November 2025 TOP500.

On 13 November 2025 Eviden unveiled the BullSequana XH3500 converged HPC/AI platform with 100% fanless 5th-generation Direct Liquid Cooling, warm water support at 40 °C facility supply, and cooling that supports heat reuse and free-cooling strategies.

faq.q: What is the BullSequana XH3500?
faq.a: Eviden's converged HPC/AI platform unveiled on 13 November 2025: 100% fanless 5th-generation direct liquid cooling with warm water support (40 °C / 104 °F facility supply), an in-rack CDU, full-rack direct liquid cooling for complete heat capture, and heat-reuse readiness.

faq.q: What is JUPITER and what cooling does it use?
faq.a: Europe's first exascale supercomputer, hosted at the Juelich Supercomputing Centre and built on Eviden's BullSequana XH3000 architecture with about 24,000 NVIDIA GH200 Superchips; it uses a highly efficient warm-water cooling system whose waste heat is integrated into the campus heating network.

faq.q: Who owns the Bull supercomputer business?
faq.a: Eviden is part of Atos Group and is described by the company as the Atos Group brand for hardware and software products; Bull is its supercomputing line.

faq.q: How efficient is JUPITER?
faq.a: EuroHPC JU states that JUPITER's booster partition delivers over 63 billion operations per watt, calling it the most energy-efficient exascale system worldwide, and it ranked number 4 on the November 2025 TOP500.

profiles.name: Gunter
profiles.tagline: Heat-rejection manufacturer (since 1931, 5 factories, presence in 80+ countries) whose dry, adiabatic and hybrid coolers serve data centers: High Density Dry Coolers and VARIO units with hydroBLU pre-cooling, grouped under a dedicated Gunter Data Center Solutions division announced in May 2026.

productLines.name: High Density Dry Cooler
productLines.note: Hybrid system combining dry and evaporative cooling for high heat-rejection loads, positioned by Gunter as avoiding the water waste and pollution associated with traditional cooling towers; part of the data center application portfolio.

productLines.name: V-shape VARIO Dry Cooler with hydroBLU
productLines.note: Fully configurable V-shaped dry cooler combined with the hydroBLU intelligent adiabatic pre-cooling solution; Gunter positions it as the choice for areas with high ambient temperatures, supporting free-cooling strategies where possible.

productLines.name: aicore air controls
productLines.note: Controls and IoT platform used with the dry and adiabatic coolers for precise control and efficient pre-cooling in high ambient conditions and to enable free-cooling strategies.

facts.text: In May 2026 the Gunter Group launched Gunter Data Center Solutions, a dedicated division combining Gunter and JAEGGI teams and integrating portfolios of dry coolers, adiabatic and hybrid solutions; the launch coverage reports more than 1,600 Gunter/JAEGGI units already deployed in data centers worldwide, providing over 4.5 GW of cooling capacity.

Gunter's data center page states that Gunter Data Center Solutions has engineered cooling solutions for data centers worldwide for over 35 years, and lists case studies in the UK/Germany, Italy (ESA), USA, Austria, Sweden and China.

faq.q: What does Gunter sell for data center cooling?
faq.a: Heat rejection: the High Density Dry Cooler (a hybrid of dry and evaporative cooling), V-shape VARIO dry coolers with hydroBLU adiabatic pre-cooling, and aicore air controls for precise control and free cooling.

faq.q: What is Gunter Data Center Solutions?
faq.a: A dedicated division launched by the Gunter Group in May 2026, combining Gunter and JAEGGI teams and integrating dry, adiabatic and hybrid cooling portfolios for data centers.

faq.q: How much data center cooling has Gunter deployed?
faq.a: Launch coverage in May 2026 reports more than 1,600 Gunter/JAEGGI units deployed in data centers worldwide, providing over 4.5 GW of cooling capacity across Europe, North America, South America and Asia.

faq.q: How long has Gunter been in business?
faq.a: The company traces its origins to 1931, with 5 factories, 3 logistics centers and presence in more than 80 countries, and says it has engineered data center cooling solutions for over 35 years.

profiles.name: Endress+Hauser
profiles.tagline: Process instrumentation group supplying the measurement layer for data-center liquid cooling: flow balancing across racks, temperature stability to avoid hotspots, pressure monitoring for leaks and pump issues, and liquid analysis of coolant quality, from the compact rack-level Picomag to Proline Promag meters on primary loops.
profiles.ownership: Family-owned - shares are held by the descendants of the founder; 18,000+ employees worldwide

productLines.name: Picomag compact electromagnetic flowmeter
productLines.note: Multivariable device combining volume flow, temperature and conductivity measurement in DN15 to DN50 (1/2 to 2 inch) lines; accuracy +/-0.8% o.r. +/-0.1% o.f.s, up to 750 l/min, medium -10 to 70 °C, max. 16 bar, IO-Link and 4-20 mA outputs, IP65/67, 5-year warranty; suited to secondary circuits, skids and tight spaces.

productLines.name: Data center cooling instrumentation portfolio
productLines.note: Flow, temperature, pressure and liquid analysis for cooling optimization: balanced flow for consistent heat transport across racks; pressure monitoring detects restrictions, leaks, imbalance or pump issues; liquid analysis guards coolant quality against contamination, corrosion or fouling across CDU primary and secondary loops.

productLines.name: Proline Promag W 300/500 electromagnetic flowmeters
productLines.note: Per Endress+Hauser's data-center announcement, Proline Promag W 300/500 covers larger-diameter primary cooling loops and complements the Picomag so that instrumentation spans every stage of a data center facility's cooling architecture.

facts.text: On 9 March 2026 Endress+Hauser announced a Picomag electromagnetic flowmeter variant for data centers and OEMs in the US market: available in 1 and 2 inch, delivered with Bluetooth deactivated from the factory for sites that prohibit wireless communication, with IO-Link and standard outputs, designed to integrate into standardized cooling skids, secondary distribution loops and rack-level cooling modules.

Endress+Hauser's data center cooling page positions its sensors, inline measurement, analyzer transmitters and digital integration as tools that help large data center facilities reduce energy use, improve water quality and extend equipment life across CDU primary and secondary loops.

faq.q: What does Endress+Hauser offer for data center cooling?
faq.a: Instrumentation across four families - flow, temperature, pressure and liquid analysis - to balance heat transport across racks, avoid hotspots and overcooling, detect leaks or pump issues, and monitor cooling fluid quality for contamination, corrosion or fouling.

faq.q: What is the data-center Picomag variant?
faq.a: Announced 9 March 2026 for the US market: a compact electromagnetic flowmeter combining flow, temperature and conductivity measurement in 1 and 2 inch lines, shipped with Bluetooth deactivated for data centers and OEMs that prohibit wireless communication, connecting via IO-Link, 4-20 mA, pulse, switch or 2-10 V.

faq.q: What are the Picomag's key specifications?
faq.a: DN15 to DN50 process connections, volume flow accuracy of +/-0.8% o.r. +/-0.1% o.f.s, measuring range up to 750 l/min, medium temperature -10 to 70 °C (85 °C short-term), maximum process pressure 16 bar, IP65/67 protection and a 5-year warranty.

faq.q: What does Endress+Hauser offer for primary loops?
faq.a: Proline Promag W 300/500 electromagnetic flowmeters for larger-diameter primary cooling loops, which the company says complement the Picomag to cover every stage of a data center's cooling architecture.

profiles.name: Continental
profiles.tagline: German technology company (founded 1871) whose Continental Industry division supplies data cooling hoses for direct-to-chip liquid cooling: ExtremeFlex DataGuard and DataGuard source lines feed server manifolds, while FlexCool Jumper and Blade hoses carry glycol-based coolant to individual server blades and their cold plates.
profiles.ownership: Officially listed on the German stock exchanges in Frankfurt, Hamburg, Hanover and Stuttgart; OTC ADR in the US

productLines.name: ExtremeFlex DataGuard
productLines.note: External feed line that transfers glycol-based coolants engineered for direct-to-chip cooling; part of Continental's Data Cooling Solutions portfolio for high-density data center equipment.

productLines.name: FlexCool Jumper
productLines.note: Receives cooling fluid from the source line system, transitioning from the manifold to individual server blades; the flexible jumper connecting rack distribution to each blade.

productLines.name: FlexCool Blade
productLines.note: Transfers coolant to the cold plate, targeting the portion(s) of the blade generating the most heat; the final hose link in the direct-to-chip cooling path.

productLines.name: DataGuard source line
productLines.note: Kink- and twist-resistant source line hose that delivers a constant supply of coolant directly to server manifolds, completing the four-product data cooling line-up.

facts.text: On its 2026 product page, Continental lists the four-product data cooling line-up for glycol-based direct-to-chip cooling and states that it is a participating member of the Open Compute Project (OCP); the group's ContiTech sector operates the continental-industry.com business.

Continental's Data Cooling Solutions brochure (2025 English edition, linked from the official product page) documents the data cooling hose portfolio for stable liquid-cooling cycles in high-density data center equipment: DataGuard and ExtremeFlex DataGuard source lines plus FlexCool Jumper and FlexCool Blade hoses.

faq.q: Which data cooling hoses does Continental offer?
faq.a: Four products: ExtremeFlex DataGuard, an external feed line for glycol-based direct-to-chip coolants; DataGuard, a kink- and twist-resistant source line to server manifolds; FlexCool Jumper, from manifold to server blades; and FlexCool Blade, to the cold plate.

faq.q: What coolants do the hoses carry?
faq.a: The page describes the hoses as transferring glycol-based coolants engineered for direct-to-chip cooling, from the source line system through manifolds to server blades and cold plates.

faq.q: Is Continental involved in the Open Compute Project?
faq.a: Yes - Continental states on its data cooling page that it is a participating member of the Open Compute Project (OCP).

faq.q: What is Continental?
faq.a: A German company founded in 1871, organized since 1 January 2026 into the Tires and ContiTech sectors; the data cooling hoses are sold through the Continental Industry (ContiTech) business, and the share is listed on the German stock exchanges in Frankfurt, Hamburg, Hanover and Stuttgart.

profiles.name: Iceotope
profiles.tagline: UK company, founded 2005 in Sheffield, that develops chassis-level precision liquid cooling for AI and HPC servers, delivered through OEM/ODM co-design and IP licensing, with published datacenter and edge reference designs.

productLines.name: Integrated liquid-cooled chassis (DL380-IC, XE7740-IC)
productLines.note: Chassis-level precision liquid cooling described as cooling processors, memory, storage and PSUs ('direct to everything'); data sheets are listed for DL380-IC and XE7740-IC integrated chassis; delivered through OEM/ODM co-design and IP licensing.

productLines.name: Datacenter reference design
productLines.note: Liquid-cooled chassis and server solutions for high-density, low-latency workloads, stated to be compatible with existing rack deployments; the company cites up to 6x more compute per square meter versus air cooling.

productLines.name: Edge reference design
productLines.note: Precision liquid-cooled AI inferencing clusters integrating compute, cooling, networking, memory and storage; stated to be deployable without facility water or dry chillers. The company cites 100% less water, 40% less power and 84% less cooling per kW of IT equipment power.

facts.text: Iceotope reported a portfolio milestone of 200 patents granted and pending across its chassis-level precision liquid cooling technology; the company site now cites 228 patents pending, issued and allowed.
At GITEX Global 2025 (October 9, 2025), Iceotope showcased its precision liquid cooling technology jointly with Giga Computing and nVent, focused on sustainable AI infrastructure.

faq.q: What exactly does Iceotope sell?
faq.a: Rather than selling finished racks, Iceotope co-designs and licenses its chassis-level precision liquid cooling to OEMs and ODMs and publishes reference designs; integrated-chassis data sheets listed include DL380-IC and XE7740-IC.

faq.q: How does chassis-level liquid cooling differ from cold-plate racks?
faq.a: Iceotope describes its approach as 'direct to everything', sealing liquid cooling at the chassis level to cover processors, memory, storage and PSUs, in contrast to cold-plate approaches; the company notes PSUs can generate up to 15% of total rack heat.

faq.q: Can Iceotope cooling be deployed at edge sites?
faq.a: The Edge reference design targets precision liquid-cooled AI inferencing clusters and is stated to be deployable without facility water or dry chillers.

faq.q: Where is the company based and who owns it?
faq.a: Iceotope was founded in 2005 in Sheffield, UK, and is privately held; no parent company or public listing is mentioned on its company page.

profiles.name: Refroid Technologies
profiles.tagline: Indian company, founded 2021 and headquartered in Hyderabad, supplying coolant distribution units, liquid racks and manifolds, immersion cooling pods and hybrid load banks for AI, HPC, high-density and edge data-center cooling.

productLines.name: Coolant Distribution Units, Liquid Racks & Manifolds
productLines.note: CDU and liquid rack/manifold products for AI, HPC, high-density data center, edge and modular deployments. The directory's source article covers SentraFlo liquid-to-liquid CDUs at 200 kW to 2 MW for direct-to-chip cooling; capacity figures are not published on the site pages opened (NOT_FOUND).

productLines.name: Immersion Cooling PODS (EcoPod, MiniPod, ISOPod)
productLines.note: EcoPod compact units for high-density workloads, MiniPod edge-ready pods, and ISOPod fully standardized pods stated to be built for hyperscale, mission-critical deployments. The company cites closed-loop zero-water designs and ASHRAE TC9.9 compliance.

productLines.name: Thermion Hybrid Load Banks
productLines.note: Load banks that simulate real-world IT loads for validating liquid and hybrid (air plus liquid) cooling infrastructure, used in commissioning of direct-to-chip and immersion installations.

facts.text: On May 22, 2025 Refroid launched the SentraFlo Series of liquid-to-liquid CDUs developed and made in India, with customizable capacities from 200 kW to 2 MW; shipments were to begin by the end of June 2025, and the range also covers rack manifolds and a secondary fluid network plumbing architecture

Refroid's website carries blog posts of June 16-17, 2025 on liquid cooling for next-generation data centers, including one on the AI revolution's demand for cooling that covers hybrid thermal simulators (load banks) and one on liquid immersion cooling for India's data infrastructure

faq.q: What immersion cooling products does Refroid offer?
faq.a: Three pod variants: EcoPod compact units for high-density workloads, MiniPod edge-ready pods, and ISOPod fully standardized pods stated to be built for hyperscale, mission-critical deployments.

faq.q: What are Thermion Hybrid Load Banks for?
faq.a: They simulate real-world IT loads to validate liquid and hybrid (air plus liquid) cooling infrastructure, supporting commissioning of direct-to-chip and immersion installations.

faq.q: Where is Refroid based and when was it founded?
faq.a: Refroid Technologies was founded in 2021 and is headquartered in Hyderabad, India; its ownership structure is not stated on the pages opened.

faq.q: What performance claims does the company publish?
faq.a: Refroid cites up to 50%+ cooling energy savings, closed-loop zero-water designs and ASHRAE TC9.9 compliance; no capacity figures were published on the site pages opened.

profiles.name: MTA
profiles.tagline: Italian manufacturer M.T.A. S.r.l., based in Tribano and part of the Trane Technologies group, supplies air-cooled, free-cooling and heat-recovery chillers used for data-centre cooling and heat rejection.
profiles.ownership: Subsidiary of Trane Technologies plc (M.T.A. S.r.l. a socio unico, under Trane Technologies direction and coordination)

productLines.name: Free-cooling chillers for data centres
productLines.note: MTA's data-centre page presents free-cooling chillers stated to ensure energy savings of up to 45% versus conventional chillers; free-cooling is offered as a dedicated category of its process-cooling line, alongside air-cooled and water-cooled chillers.

productLines.name: ARIES G air-cooled chillers
productLines.note: Air-cooled chillers with R454B refrigerant covering 160-858 kW cooling capacity; the March 2026 ARIES G FC version adds integrated free cooling for energy-efficient process cooling. Companion ranges include TAE G (7-244 kW, R513A/R454B) and TAEevo TECH (9-256 kW, R410A).

productLines.name: GEMINI modular chillers
productLines.note: Modular air-cooled chillers: GEMINI at 87-164 kW with R454B scroll compressors, and GEMINI N at 64-125 kW with R290 and inverter scroll compressors, launched 3 August 2026 for comfort and process cooling.

productLines.name: Chillers with integrated heat recovery
productLines.note: For data centres MTA also offers products with integrated heat recovery, stated to minimise waste energy consumption, plus remote monitoring stated to reduce installation cost.

facts.text: On 5 June 2026 MTA introduced modular low-GWP chillers and heat pumps offering 300 kW of heating and 320 kW of cooling capacity in a footprint of under 9 square metres.
On 15 May 2026 MTA launched the GEMINI modular air-to-water chillers and heat pumps using R454B refrigerant for scalable, compact installations.
On 6 March 2026 MTA launched ARIES G FC, air-cooled chillers with integrated free cooling for energy-efficient industrial process cooling.

faq.q: What does MTA offer for data-centre cooling?
faq.a: Free-cooling chillers stated to deliver energy savings of up to 45% versus conventional chillers, chillers with integrated heat recovery stated to minimise waste energy consumption, and remote monitoring stated to reduce installation cost.

faq.q: In what capacity ranges do MTA chillers run?
faq.a: Published air-cooled ranges include ARIES G at 160-858 kW (R454B), GEMINI at 87-164 kW, TAE G at 7-244 kW and TAEevo TECH at 9-256 kW; modular low-GWP units launched in June 2026 provide 320 kW cooling in under 9 square metres.

faq.q: Who owns MTA?
faq.a: M.T.A. S.r.l. a socio unico, headquartered in Tribano (PD), Italy, is subject to the direction and coordination of Trane Technologies plc; its founding year is not stated on the pages opened.

faq.q: What has MTA launched recently?
faq.a: In 2026 MTA launched ARIES G FC free-cooling chillers (6 March), the GEMINI modular R454B chillers and heat pumps (15 May) and the modular low-GWP chillers and heat pumps of 5 June; the GEMINI N R290 modular range followed on 3 August 2026.

profiles.name: Oleon
profiles.tagline: Oleochemicals producer of the Avril group supplying QLOE, a plant-based dielectric liquid for single-phase server immersion cooling aimed at HPC, hyperscale, edge and AI data centres.
profiles.ownership: Subsidiary of Avril (French agri-food group; site wording: a company of Avril)

productLines.name: QLOE immersion cooling fluids
productLines.note: Biobased dielectric liquids for single-phase immersion cooling of servers, made from plant-based raw materials. Published properties: flash point 210 C; PFAS-free, renewable and biodegradable; not classified as toxic, irritant or hazardous to humans; low viscosity; zero global warming potential and no bio-accumulation.

productLines.name: Data-centre immersion cooling programme
productLines.note: Marketed for HPC, hyperscale, edge, AI, deep learning, blockchain and GPU-as-a-Service workloads, with stated conformity with Open Compute Project standards, partnerships listing Submer, AI Green Bytes, Airsys, MIDAS and Iceotope, and an application lab in Venette (Paris area) offering live demonstrations.

facts.text: On 29 January 2026 Oleon announced a strategic collaboration with Iceotope covering its QLOE immersion cooling fluids, adding to earlier ecosystem partnerships with Submer, AI Green Bytes, Airsys and MIDAS listed on its server immersion cooling page.
On November 19, 2024 Oleon unveiled its Qloe brand of biobased immersion cooling liquids for data center cooling through immersion cooling, made from plant-based renewable materials

faq.q: What is QLOE?
faq.a: A range of plant-based dielectric liquids for single-phase immersion cooling of servers: flash point 210 C, PFAS-free, renewable, biodegradable, low viscosity, zero global warming potential, and not classified as toxic, irritant or hazardous to humans.

faq.q: Which data-centre workloads is QLOE aimed at?
faq.a: Oleon markets QLOE for HPC, hyperscale, edge, AI, deep learning, blockchain and GPU-as-a-Service installations, and states conformity with Open Compute Project standards.

faq.q: Who owns Oleon and where is it based?
faq.a: Oleon is a company of the French Avril group, registered in Belgium; the directory lists its head office as Edegem (Antwerp), Belgium. Its founding year is not stated on the pages opened.

faq.q: Where can QLOE be seen running?
faq.a: Oleon operates a QLOE application lab in Venette (Paris area), France, offering live demonstrations of immersion cooling setups; visits can be booked, and a bio-based installation in Venette is listed on its immersion cooling page.

profiles.name: Perstorp
profiles.tagline: Specialty chemicals group headquartered in Malmö, Sweden and part of PETRONAS Chemicals Group Berhad, supplying the Synmerse DC range of PFAS-free synthetic ester dielectric fluids for single-phase immersion cooling of AI and HPC data centres.
profiles.ownership: Subsidiary of PETRONAS Chemicals Group Berhad (Perstorp Holding AB)

productLines.name: Synmerse DC immersion cooling fluids
productLines.note: Synthetic ester dielectric fluids for single-phase immersion cooling, developed and tested with OEMs and ODMs. Four grades: Synmerse DC (balanced viscosity and fire safety), DC-L (ultra-low viscosity), DC-Lx (ultra-low viscosity with material compatibility) and DC-R (highest fire-safety requirements). PFAS-free, readily biodegradable, high fl …

productLines.name: Advanced liquid cooling fluid development with Intel (Open IP)
productLines.note: Announced 25 June 2024: a collaboration with Intel on Open IP Advanced Liquid Cooling to develop synthetic thermal management fluids. 2026 webinars cover dielectric fluids for cold-plate and direct-to-chip cooling - announced and under development, separate from the Synmerse immersion grades sold today.

facts.text: On 27 April 2026 Perstorp ran the webinar 'Cold Plate Cooling Reinvented: Trusted Dielectric Fluids for Next-Gen Data Centres', part of a 2026 liquid-cooling programme that also covered H-DINI high-density AI infrastructure supporting 6G.

Perstorp took part in the OCP Global Summit 2025 in San Jose (13-16 October 2025), listed among its data-centre sector events alongside next-generation liquid cooling at Data Centre World London on 4-5 March 2026.
On 1 October 2024 Perstorp launched Synmerse DC, described as a high-performing immersion cooling fluid for safe and reliable operations.
On 25 June 2024 Perstorp announced a collaboration with Intel on Open IP Advanced Liquid Cooling for the development of synthetic thermal management fluids.

faq.q: Which Synmerse grades does Perstorp offer?
faq.a: Four single-phase immersion grades: Synmerse DC for balanced viscosity and fire safety, DC-L for ultra-low viscosity, DC-Lx for ultra-low viscosity with material compatibility, and DC-R for the highest fire-safety requirements.

faq.q: Are Synmerse fluids PFAS-free?
faq.a: Yes. Perstorp states the synthetic ester fluids are PFAS-free and readily biodegradable, with high flash/fire point and extended fluid life from oxidative and thermal stability; numeric property values are not published on the page opened.

faq.q: Who owns Perstorp and where is it based?
faq.a: Perstorp Holding AB is headquartered at Neptunigatan 1, Malmö, Sweden, and is part of PETRONAS Chemicals Group Berhad; the founding year is not stated on the pages opened.

faq.q: What is the Intel collaboration about?
faq.a: Announced 25 June 2024, it covers development of synthetic thermal management fluids for Intel's Open IP Advanced Liquid Cooling; it is announced development work, separate from the Synmerse immersion grades on sale today.

profiles.name: KSB
profiles.tagline: German pump and valve manufacturer KSB SE & Co. KGaA, founded in 1871, supplies components for data-centre liquid cooling: hermetically sealed canned-motor pumps for coolant distribution units plus smart control and shut-off valves.

productLines.name: EtaSeco canned-motor pump
productLines.note: Hermetically sealed, low-maintenance canned-motor pump designed for liquid cooling applications in coolant distribution units (CDUs), with a stated design service life of 30 years and flexible integration into the available installation space. Flow-rate and motor-size figures are not published on the page opened.

productLines.name: BOA-Systronic ePIC measurement and control valve
productLines.note: Smart, pressure-independent measurement and control valve for CDU circuits: monitors and controls flow direction, volume flow rate, supply and return temperature, thermal output and quantity of heat, for optimal flow distribution and energy-efficient CDU operation.

productLines.name: BOAX-S/SF butterfly valves
productLines.note: Butterfly valves that shut off the cooling circuit quickly and reliably during maintenance or servicing without interrupting wider data-centre operations.

facts.text: KSB reported that its pumps were selected for 11 data centre cooling projects, with more than 600 units for the primary cooling systems across pump types including Etanorm, Etabloc, Omega, Movitec and MoviBloc, and nearly 300 pumps for the secondary cooling circuits and CDUs, among them the EtaSeco canned-motor pump

In a KSB technology article of October 30, 2024 on cooling data centres for artificial intelligence, KSB states that its EtaSeco canned-motor pump is ideal for CDUs in data centres and that its compact design lets it be integrated into modern cooling systems and CDUs

faq.q: What does KSB supply for liquid-cooled data centres?
faq.a: The EtaSeco canned-motor pump for CDU liquid cooling, BOA-Systronic ePIC measurement and control valves, and BOAX-S/SF butterfly valves, supporting rear-door heat exchangers, direct-to-chip cooling for racks above 100 kW, and immersion cooling.

faq.q: What is the EtaSeco pump designed for?
faq.a: A hermetically sealed, low-maintenance canned-motor pump for liquid cooling applications in CDUs, designed with a 30-year service life and flexible integration into the available installation space.

faq.q: What does the BOA-Systronic ePIC valve do?
faq.a: It is a smart, pressure-independent measurement and control valve that monitors and controls flow direction, volume flow rate, supply and return temperature, thermal output and quantity of heat, supporting energy-efficient CDU operation.

faq.q: Who is KSB?
faq.a: KSB SE & Co. KGaA was founded in Germany in 1871; the group's headquarters city and stock exchange listing are not stated on the pages opened (NOT_FOUND).

profiles.name: Valeo
profiles.tagline: Automotive supplier Valeo applies its heat-exchanger and thermal-systems technology to data-center liquid cooling, with aluminum rear-door heat exchangers, single-phase and two-phase direct-to-chip systems with CDUs, and zero-water immersion units for micro-edge compute.
profiles.ownership: Listed on the Paris Stock Exchange (per Valeo press-release boilerplate, February 2026)

productLines.name: Aluminium Rear Door Heat Exchanger
productLines.note: Aluminum radiator module installed on the rear of IT racks to capture heat at its source, from high-power IT workloads to edge data centers. Valeo's October 2025 release cites 30% greater heat-capture efficiency and 80% lower weight than copper versions, with automotive-grade corrosion protection.

productLines.name: Aluminum heat exchangers for rack doors and fan walls
productLines.note: Presented at OCP Global Summit 2026 and co-validated with OVHcloud: 38% increase in cooling capacity and 65% in power density versus traditional copper solutions, 25% lower fan electrical consumption, and corrosion coating tested to more than 10 years equivalent operating life.

productLines.name: Two-Phase Direct-to-Chip Liquid Cooling with CDU
productLines.note: Direct-to-chip liquid cooling shown at Data Centre World Paris 2025, using dielectric fluid instead of water in the cooling distribution unit. Valeo lists both single-phase and two-phase DLC systems in its data-center portfolio.

productLines.name: Edge Data Center Immersion Cooling Unit
productLines.note: Outdoor immersion cooling unit for micro-edge compute described as zero-water; 1 kW cooling capacity at 50°C ambient temperature in a 1U to 2U form factor, requiring no facility water.

facts.text: Ahead of OCP Global Summit 2026 (October 12-15, San Jose), Valeo presented aluminum heat-exchanger technology for rack rear-door modules and fan walls, reporting a 38% increase in cooling capacity and 65% in power density versus traditional copper solutions, 25% lower fan electrical consumption, and coating durability beyond a 10-year equivalent operating life, with testing being pushed to 15 years. The technology was co-validated with OVHcloud.

At Data Centre World Paris 2025 (November 5-6, Paris Expo Porte de Versailles), Valeo showcased aluminum rear-door heat exchangers with 30% greater efficiency and 80% lower weight than copper versions, a two-phase direct-to-chip system with a CDU using dielectric fluids instead of water, and an outdoor immersion cooling unit rated 1 kW at 50°C ambient for edge data centers.

faq.q: What liquid-cooling products does Valeo offer for data centers?
faq.a: Valeo's data-center cooling portfolio includes aluminum rear-door heat exchangers for rack doors and fan walls, single-phase and two-phase direct-to-chip liquid cooling systems with cooling distribution units, and zero-water immersion units for micro-edge compute applications.

faq.q: How does Valeo's aluminum rear-door heat exchanger compare with copper versions?
faq.a: Valeo reported in October 2025 that its aluminum RDHX captures heat with 30% greater efficiency and is 80% lighter than copper versions; at OCP Global Summit 2026 it reported a 38% increase in cooling capacity and 65% higher power density versus traditional copper solutions, plus 25% lower fan electrical consumption.

faq.q: Where has Valeo's data-center cooling technology been validated?
faq.a: Valeo states that its aluminum cooling technology for rack rear-door modules and fan walls was co-validated with OVHcloud, and that corrosion-protection coating testing has reached the equivalent of more than 10 years of operating life, with tests being extended toward 15 years.

faq.q: Is Valeo a data-center cooling specialist?
faq.a: No. Valeo is an automotive supplier listed on the Paris Stock Exchange that applies automotive heat-exchanger and thermal technology to data-center cooling; its data-center products cover rear-door heat exchangers, direct-to-chip liquid cooling and immersion units.

profiles.name: Synano
profiles.tagline: Synano is a Delft-based nanofluid manufacturer supplying NanoOils (alumina nanoparticles in dielectric base oils such as GTL and PAO-2) for single-phase immersion cooling of servers, GPUs and power electronics, plus water-, propylene-glycol- and ethylene-glycol-based NanoCoolants and NanoAdditives.

productLines.name: NanoOils
productLines.note: Dielectric immersion-cooling oils with alumina nanoparticles, stated to deliver up to 15% higher heat transfer than conventional dielectric oils, for submerging servers, GPUs, AI servers and power electronics in standard immersion tanks. Base oils include GTL, PAO-2 and ester additives; PAO2-NanoOil passed Submer immersion fluid validation.

productLines.name: NanoCoolants
productLines.note: Water-, propylene glycol- and ethylene glycol-based coolants with alumina nanoparticles; AG One is described as a biostatic water-based fluid with alumina nanoparticles. EG50 NanoCoolant delivered 7.4% better heat transfer in a GP Elite dyno test on a Porsche GT4 engine.

productLines.name: NanoAdditives
productLines.note: Nano-additive concentrates for oil-based coolants that let operators upgrade existing dielectric fluids with Synano nanoparticles; the company states its nanoparticles are metal or metal oxides with 100x higher thermal conductivity than liquids.

facts.text: Synano published a full white paper on GRC and Grundfos validation of its NanoOil for immersion cooling and opened its webshop so NanoCoolants can be ordered worldwide (September 2026).
Synano announced that its PAO2-Nano fluid passed Submer immersion fluid validation, published as a case study in August 2026.
Synano demonstrated NanoOil immersion cooling live at OCP Global Summit 2025 in October 2025, reporting strong interest from the direct liquid cooling and immersion cooling industry.

In July 2025 Synano announced independent validation of its nanofluids at APL GmbH and first shipments of nano-enhanced cooling fluids to industrial partners; in August 2025 it doubled its office and laboratory space.

faq.q: What does Synano sell for immersion cooling?
faq.a: NanoOils are dielectric oils with alumina nanoparticles for single-phase immersion cooling of servers, GPUs, AI servers and power electronics in standard immersion tanks, stated to give up to 15% higher heat transfer than conventional dielectric oils. NanoAdditives and water-, PG- and EG-based NanoCoolants complete the range.

faq.q: Have Synano fluids been validated by third parties?
faq.a: Yes. Synano reports validation with Submer (PAO2-Nano passed Submer immersion fluid validation), with GRC and Grundfos (white paper published September 2026), and independent testing at APL GmbH in July 2025; fluids are tested per REACH, ASTM and IEC standards.

faq.q: Who is Synano?
faq.a: A Dutch startup founded in 2017 by a team of thermal and nano-materials experts from TU Delft research, based in Delft, Netherlands, that stabilizes nanoparticles in low-viscosity fluids and reports consistent heat-transfer increases above 10%.

faq.q: Where can Synano fluids be bought?
faq.a: Since September 2026 the Synano webshop is live and NanoCoolants are available to order worldwide; the company also reports first shipments of nano-enhanced cooling fluids to industrial partners since July 2025.

profiles.name: TE Connectivity
profiles.tagline: TE Connectivity is a global connector and sensor manufacturer whose data-center liquid cooling portfolio spans pressure, temperature and ultrasonic liquid-level sensors for coolant loops, liquid-cooled power busbars and liquid-cooled high-speed I/O built around the Open Rack v3 ecosystem.

productLines.name: Liquid cooling sensors
productLines.note: High-precision pressure sensing that stabilizes pump performance, temperature sensors, and ultrasonic level sensors giving reliable readings even in aerated liquids, for CDUs (liquid-to-air and liquid-to-liquid), manifolds, cold plates, heat exchangers, pumps, filters, expansion tanks and piping in deionized water and water-glycol coolants such as PG25.

productLines.name: Liquid-cooled power busbar assembly
productLines.note: Power busbar with integrated liquid cooling, showcased at OCP EMEA Summit 2025, designed so rack power distribution can follow rising AI rack power requirements without increasing busbar footprint.

productLines.name: High-speed I/O liquid cooling and thermal bridge hybrid
productLines.note: Combination of TE patented thermal bridge components with a liquid cooling cold plate to address thermal challenges in high-speed I/O for AI, HPC and data center applications.

productLines.name: ORv3 rack power distribution
productLines.note: Power distribution compatible with Open Rack v3, including integrated busbar assemblies, custom power cable assemblies, RAPID LOCK cable assemblies, CROWN CLIP Jr busbar clips, ELCON Mini connectors and next-generation MULTI-BEAM Plus power connectors.

facts.text: In its March 13, 2026 release ahead of OFC 2026, TE Connectivity described a high-density optical backplane with front-panel connectivity that integrates liquid cooling, among optical, copper and thermal innovations for AI architectures

At OCP EMEA Summit 2025 (April 29-30, Dublin, booth B3), TE Connectivity showcased a liquid-cooled power busbar assembly for rising AI rack power, a high-speed I/O liquid cooling and thermal bridge hybrid combining patented thermal bridge components with a liquid cooling cold plate, and Open Rack v3 compatible power distribution.

profiles.ocp: TE Connectivity is listed on the OCP Marketplace for its busbar assembly with liquid cooling, with related links to the Open Rack V3 base specification; the listing page shows no acceptance status or date.

faq.q: Which sensors does TE offer for data center liquid cooling?
faq.a: Pressure sensors for high-precision sensing that stabilizes pump performance, temperature sensors, and ultrasonic liquid level sensors that deliver reliable readings even in aerated liquids, deployed across CDUs (liquid-to-air and liquid-to-liquid), manifolds, cold plates, heat exchangers, pumps, filters, expansion tanks and piping.

faq.q: In which cooling loops are the sensors used?
faq.a: TE positions its sensors across the secondary technology cooling system loop and the primary facility water system, in coolants including deionized water and water-glycol mixtures such as PG25.

faq.q: What is TE liquid-cooled power busbar?
faq.a: A power busbar assembly with integrated liquid cooling, showcased at OCP EMEA Summit 2025, intended to let rack power distribution keep up with rising AI rack power requirements without increasing the busbar footprint.

faq.q: Is TE involved with OCP?
faq.a: TE exhibited at OCP EMEA Summit 2025 in Dublin and is listed on the OCP Marketplace for its busbar assembly with liquid cooling, linked to the Open Rack V3 base specification; the marketplace listing carries no acceptance status or date.

profiles.name: Calyos
profiles.tagline: Calyos, based in Charleroi, Belgium, designs passive, pumpless two-phase cooling loops - heat pipes, loop heat pipes, micro-channel and pulsating heat pipes - for AI servers, switches and edge compute, moving heat to remote air exchangers without pumps.

productLines.name: Airgrade AI server GPU tray
productLines.note: Passive two-phase cooling tray for AI server GPUs, dissipated up to 12 kW without pumps; showcased at Data Centre World Asia in September 2026.

productLines.name: Pumpless loop heat pipes
productLines.note: Two-phase loop heat pipes carry heat from CPUs, GPUs and switch ASICs to remote air exchangers; demonstrated on a single 1,500 W switch ASIC and a 600 W CPU with >150 W hotspots in a 2U chassis at 300 CFM.

productLines.name: Two-phase cooling for 2CRSi edge AI server
productLines.note: Portable pumpless loop heat pipe cooling for the 2CRSi edge AI server, dissipating up to 12 kW; the collaboration was announced in June 2026.

facts.text: In November 2026 Calyos and Euro Heat Pipes launched the Two-Phase Valley, a joint European ecosystem for two-phase cooling; in September 2026 Calyos showcased its passive two-phase Airgrade solution for AI servers at Data Centre World Asia.

In April 2026 Calyos presented its air-cooled AI server concept ('AI GenAIRation') at the OCP EMEA Summit; in June 2026 it announced a collaboration with 2CRSi on two-phase cooling for edge AI servers.

In December 2025 Calyos was selected for NATO's DIANA 2026 cohort to optimize data centre cooling, and in November 2025 it presented a hybrid air/two-phase cooled server with Valeo at Data Center World Paris.

faq.q: Do Calyos cooling loops need pumps?
faq.a: No. Calyos builds passive, pumpless two-phase loops - heat pipes, loop heat pipes, micro-channel and pulsating heat pipes - that move heat by phase change and capillary action to remote air exchangers, with no moving parts in the loop.

faq.q: What heat loads has Calyos demonstrated for data center hardware?
faq.a: On its data center page Calyos cites its Airgrade AI server GPU tray and 2CRSi edge AI server cooling at up to 12 kW, a single 1,500 W switch ASIC, a 600 W CPU with >150 W hotspots in a 2U chassis at 300 CFM, and a 300 W FPGA in a 1U chassis.

faq.q: Where is Calyos based and how active is it in the data center ecosystem?
faq.a: Calyos is located in Charleroi, Belgium (Zoning De Jumet). Its 2025-2026 news lists appearances at the OCP Global Summit 2025 and OCP EMEA Summit 2026, Data Centre World Asia 2026, and selection for NATO's DIANA 2026 cohort on data centre cooling.

profiles.name: SECO/WARWICK
profiles.tagline: SECO/WARWICK, headquartered in Swiebodzin, Poland, is a publicly traded industrial furnace maker (traded since 2007). Its CAB and vacuum brazing lines - Active Only CAB, EV/CAB, Vector, VAB Line - braze the aluminium cooling plates and heat exchangers used in liquid cooling systems.

productLines.name: CAB furnaces (Controlled Atmosphere Brazing)
productLines.note: Fluxless CAB lines for aluminium assemblies, in use by SECO/WARWICK since 1984; the vacuum purge semi-continuous Active Only CAB furnace is applied to brazing battery cooling plates and automotive heat exchangers, per the company's 2019 brazing article.

productLines.name: EV/CAB, Semi-Continuous and Universal CAB Batch lines
productLines.note: CAB product series for high-volume aluminium brazing; in November 2026 a Chinese partner ordered a semi-continuous CAB line for demanding tube-and-bar heat exchangers.

productLines.name: Vector and VAB Line vacuum furnaces
productLines.note: Vacuum furnace lines (Vector, CaseMaster Evolution, UniCase Master, Pit-LPC, VAB Line) covering vacuum brazing and heat treatment, the fluxless joining route for aluminium and copper cooling components.

facts.text: In November 2026 a Chinese partner ordered a semi-continuous CAB brazing line from SECO/WARWICK for demanding tube-and-bar aluminium heat exchangers, per the company's news page.

SECO/WARWICK's March 2019 brazing article positions CAB furnaces, including the vacuum purge semi-continuous Active Only CAB delivered to a North American aftermarket maker, as the preferred joining technology for aluminium battery cooling plates in HEV/EV vehicles; the company notes CAB activity since 1984.

faq.q: How does SECO/WARWICK relate to liquid cooling hardware?
faq.a: SECO/WARWICK sells the brazing furnaces used to join aluminium cooling plates and heat exchangers - components of liquid cooling systems. Its published brazing guidance covers cooling plates for vehicles, and its CAB and vacuum lines are used for fluxless aluminium brazing.

faq.q: Which furnace series are offered?
faq.a: Controlled Atmosphere Brazing series include CAB Furnaces, EV/CAB, Semi-Continuous Brazing, Universal CAB Batch and Aftermarket lines; vacuum lines include Vector, CaseMaster Evolution, UniCase Master, Pit-LPC and VAB Line, plus custom-designed furnaces.

faq.q: Who owns SECO/WARWICK and where is it based?
faq.a: SECO/WARWICK is headquartered at Sobieskiego 8, 66-200 Swiebodzin, Poland, and is a publicly listed company traded since 2007, with customers in over 30 countries per its own pages.

profiles.name: SuperX
profiles.tagline: SuperX, a Singapore-based company and subsidiary of NASDAQ-listed SuperX AI Technology Limited, builds full-stack AI infrastructure: its CryoPod modular cooling enclosure integrates a liquid cooling CDU, circulation pump and dry air cooler in models rated 680-900 kW, alongside AI servers (XI6150, B300/B200) and 800VDC digital power.
profiles.ownership: Subsidiary of SuperX AI Technology Limited (NASDAQ: SUPX)

productLines.name: CryoPod 680 / 700 / 880 / 900
productLines.note: Modular dry-cooler enclosure integrating a liquid cooling CDU, primary circulation pump and pipework plus sprinkler system. Rated heat transfer 680/700/880/900 kW with 35 C liquid supply at 30 C ambient, flows 833-1,000 L/min, max 10 bar, 25% ethylene glycol or water coolant, DN100 connections, 400V 50/60Hz, 6,000-6,700 kg.

productLines.name: AI servers and AI rack systems
productLines.note: AI servers including the XI6150 and B300/B200 systems and an NVIDIA GB300-based AI rack; a first order of 128 NVIDIA B300 servers from Ezisight was announced in August 2026.

productLines.name: Digital power and modular data center products
productLines.note: Digital power products including Panama-800VDC, Aurora-800VDC, GreenPort and Energy Vault, a Powercore AI-factory offering and a Micro-Modular Data Center, complementing its cooling systems for AI sites.

facts.text: On 12 November 2026 SuperX made its U.S. exhibition debut at SC26, showcasing full-stack AI infrastructure solutions spanning AI servers, cooling and digital power.
On 28 August 2026 SuperX announced a first order of 128 NVIDIA B300 servers from Ezisight, its entry into the Australian market; a further B300 order from Woodman followed for Japan.

faq.q: What is the SuperX CryoPod?
faq.a: A modular cooling enclosure that integrates a liquid cooling CDU, primary circulation pump and pipeline, a sprinkler system and a dry air cooler in one unit, aimed at AI data centers. Four models (680, 700, 880, 900) are rated at 680-900 kW heat transfer capacity.

faq.q: What are the CryoPod's operating parameters?
faq.a: Rated liquid supply temperature is 35 C at 30 C ambient, max pressure 10 bar, flows 833 L/min (680/700 models) or 1,000 L/min (880/900), coolant of 25% ethylene glycol or water, DN100 connections, 400V 50/60Hz power, in a 6058x2438x5792 mm enclosure weighing 6,000-6,700 kg.

faq.q: Who owns SuperX and what else does it sell?
faq.a: SuperX AI Pte. Ltd. of Singapore is a subsidiary of SuperX AI Technology Limited, listed on NASDAQ as SUPX. Beyond cooling, it sells AI servers (XI6150, B300/B200, GB300 rack), 800VDC digital power and micro-modular data centers.

profiles.name: Shell
profiles.tagline: Shell plc produces liquid cooling fluids for data centres, including a propylene glycol-based PG25 direct liquid cooling fluid and a proprietary dielectric single-phase immersion cooling fluid made from natural gas via its gas-to-liquids (GTL) technology, complemented by the Shell MIDEL ester fluid range.

productLines.name: Shell DLC Fluid (PG25)
productLines.note: Propylene glycol-based PG25 coolant engineered for direct-to-chip liquid cooling, aimed at heat transfer performance, long-term corrosion protection and extended operational life; qualified as NVIDIA DSX Ready Coolant, per Shell.

productLines.name: Shell Immersion Cooling Fluid
productLines.note: Dielectric single-phase immersion fluid made from natural gas using Shell's gas-to-liquids (GTL) technology; certified by Intel for use with 4th and 5th Gen Intel Xeon processors in data centres worldwide.

productLines.name: Shell MIDEL ester fluids
productLines.note: Ester transformer-fluid range complementing the liquid cooling portfolio: MIDEL 7131 meets IEC 61099 and ASTM D8240 (K3 class) and MIDEL eN 1204/eN 1215 meet IEC 61039 and ASTM D6871 (K2 class); FM Approved and UL classified.

facts.text: Shell announced NVIDIA DSX Ready Coolant qualification for its direct liquid cooling (DLC) fluid, a PG25 propylene glycol coolant for direct-to-chip applications; per Shell, NVIDIA is the first to announce qualification of the fluid, just over a year after its launch (page updated 9 November 2026).

On April 20, 2026 Keppel and Shell announced an immersion liquid cooling testbed at an operational Keppel data centre in Singapore, using Shell’s gas-to-liquids-based immersion cooling fluid in a live server tank; it was to be operational by May 2026 for twelve months

faq.q: What liquid cooling fluids does Shell sell for data centres?
faq.a: Shell sells a propylene glycol-based PG25 direct liquid cooling fluid for direct-to-chip applications and a dielectric single-phase immersion cooling fluid made from natural gas via its GTL technology, with the Shell MIDEL ester range complementing the portfolio.

faq.q: What third-party validation do the fluids have?
faq.a: Per Shell, its DLC Fluid received NVIDIA DSX Ready Coolant qualification (NVIDIA being the first to announce qualification of the fluid), and its Immersion Cooling Fluids are certified by Intel for use with 4th and 5th Gen Intel Xeon processors in data centres worldwide.

faq.q: What performance figures does Shell publish for immersion cooling?
faq.a: Shell cites up to 48% energy footprint reduction, up to 40% CPU speed increase, up to 80% floor-space saving and up to 33% lower total cost of ownership for single-phase immersion, figures it bases on a Mordor Intelligence market report and Shell internal evaluations, noting results vary by site.

faq.q: Has Shell used immersion cooling itself?
faq.a: Shell reports that Shell IT deployed an immersion-cooled HPC cluster within its Houston data center with help from AMD and Penguin Solutions, and that Shell worked with Asperitas on an energy-efficient HPC cluster upgrade in Amsterdam.

profiles.name: Vaisala
profiles.tagline: Finnish measurement company supplying humidity, dew point and temperature transmitters and monitoring systems for data-center cooling, including the Origo platform launched in February 2026; its guidance for liquid-cooled halls is to keep coolant supply at least 2 degrees C above measured ambient dew point.
profiles.ownership: Series A and K shares; series A shares listed on Nasdaq Helsinki

productLines.name: Origo10 Series transmitters
productLines.note: Modular HVAC transmitter family with exchangeable probes measuring humidity, temperature, CO2 and dew point; the Origo platform was launched with a February 2, 2026 press release on cutting cooling waste in data centers and is listed among Vaisala's recommended data-center products.

productLines.name: Indigo Supervisor
productLines.note: Monitoring hub that connects up to 100 sensors to one touchscreen with one Modbus TCP connection; Vaisala announced it for data centers on September 29, 2026, saying the challenge is shifting from measurement coverage to operational scalability.

productLines.name: HUMICAP humidity and temperature instruments
productLines.note: Probe and transmitter family for data-center air conditions, including HMP110 and HMP113 HUMICAP probes, HMT120/130 transmitters, and wall- and duct-mounted HMW110, HMD60 and HMD110 units, all listed on Vaisala's data-center application page.

productLines.name: viewLinc Cloud Suite
productLines.note: Cloud-based continuous environmental monitoring platform offered for data centers, complemented by the Vaisala Care for Data Centers service combining calibration, probe pools and the MyVaisala portal.

facts.text: On September 29, 2026 Vaisala launched Indigo Supervisor for data centers, a monitoring system that manages up to 100 measurement points as a single system as environmental monitoring shifts from coverage to scalability.

On September 8, 2026 Vaisala launched Care services to help data centers maintain measurement accuracy at scale, covering measurements that support cooling performance in larger, AI-driven facilities.
On February 2, 2026 Vaisala launched the Origo modular transmitter platform with the press release 'What's the cost of a half-degree? Vaisala's new Origo slashes cooling waste in data centers'.

faq.q: What does Vaisala offer for liquid-cooled data centers?
faq.a: Measurement and monitoring rather than cooling hardware: Origo10 transmitters with exchangeable probes, Indigo Supervisor for up to 100 measurement points, HUMICAP probes and viewLinc monitoring. Vaisala's guidance for liquid-cooled halls is to keep coolant supply temperature at least 2 degrees C above the measured ambient dew point.

faq.q: Does Vaisala make coolant distribution units or cold plates?
faq.a: No. Its data-center offering consists of measurement instruments, monitoring software and services, used to control cooling and manage condensation risk around liquid cooling loops.

faq.q: When did Vaisala launch the Origo platform for data centers?
faq.a: February 2, 2026, with a press release on reducing cooling waste in data centers; Indigo Supervisor followed on September 29, 2026 and data-center Care services on September 8, 2026.

faq.q: Where is Vaisala listed?
faq.a: Vaisala has series A and K shares; its series A shares are listed on Nasdaq Helsinki.

profiles.name: USystems
profiles.tagline: UK maker of the ColdLogik line of rear door heat exchangers (CL20, CL21 and CL23, with the CL23 rated up to 200 kW per rack), matching coolant distribution units and in-row coolers; acquired by the Legrand group in July 2022 and now part of its data-centre offering.
profiles.ownership: Subsidiary of Legrand; acquired by the Legrand group on July 29, 2022

productLines.name: ColdLogik CL23 Active Rear Door Heat Exchanger
productLines.note: Active rear door heat exchanger rated at up to 200 kW per rack; the announcement of the Legrand acquisition described the ColdLogik rear door cooler range as 0.1 to 200 kW plus per rack, covering retrofit and new build; a FastTrack delivery version is offered.

productLines.name: ColdLogik CL20 and CL21 Rear Door Heat Exchangers
productLines.note: CL20 is the active model described as the original intelligent rear door heat exchanger; CL21 is the passive model offering high-performance cooling at zero operational cost. Both are available in FastTrack versions for faster delivery.

productLines.name: ColdLogik Coolant Distribution Unit
productLines.note: CDU that separates primary and secondary fluid circuits through a plate heat exchanger; stated to fit the footprint of a standard 42U rack, 800 mm wide by 1200 mm deep. Capacity and flow figures are not stated on the pages opened.

productLines.name: CL80 InRow Coolers
productLines.note: In-row cooler family listed in 300W and 600W variants, with a FastTrack version configurable at 42U extendable to 52U and 600 mm or 800 mm widths, shipped in 4 to 6 weeks.

facts.text: In August 2025 USystems published a case study describing a decade of ColdLogik intelligent cooling at Cambridge University, highlighting efficiency and adaptability of the rear door heat exchanger deployment.

On July 29, 2022 the Legrand group announced the acquisition of Bedford-based USystems Ltd, adding the ColdLogik rear door cooler technology with a cooling range of 0.1 to 200 kW plus per rack to its data centre solutions.

faq.q: What cooling capacity do ColdLogik rear door heat exchangers offer?
faq.a: The CL23 active rear door heat exchanger is rated at up to 200 kW per rack, and the range announced with the Legrand acquisition spans 0.1 to 200 kW plus per rack, covering both retrofit and new build deployments. A passive CL21 model cools with zero operational cost.

faq.q: Who owns USystems?
faq.a: USystems Ltd, headquartered in Bedford, United Kingdom, was acquired by the Legrand group; the acquisition was announced on July 29, 2022. The company's founding year is not stated on the pages opened.

faq.q: What does the ColdLogik CDU provide?
faq.a: The ColdLogik coolant distribution unit separates primary and secondary fluid circuits using a plate heat exchanger and fits the footprint of a standard 42U rack, 800 mm wide by 1200 mm deep; published capacity and flow figures were not found on the product pages.

faq.q: Is there a recent ColdLogik deployment reference?
faq.a: An August 2025 case study on the USystems knowledge hub describes ten years of ColdLogik intelligent cooling operation at Cambridge University.

profiles.name: Ansys
profiles.tagline: Simulation software vendor whose CFD and thermal tools (Icepak, Fluent, Thermal Desktop) predict airflow, heat transfer and cooling performance across servers, racks, containment and air/liquid cooling systems in data centers. Part of Synopsys since July 2025.

productLines.name: Ansys Icepak
productLines.note: CFD electronics-cooling software whose listed product specs include Liquid Cooling, multi-fluid and complex flow modeling, thermoelectric cooler modeling and full conjugate heat transfer analysis; the 2026 R1 release adds a system-level thermal management workflow the vendor says is 3-5x quicker to set up with 80% fewer clicks.

productLines.name: Ansys Fluent
productLines.note: Advanced-physics CFD solver used in the vendor's data-center workflow to analyze airflow, heat transfer and cooling performance across servers, racks and containment, including air/liquid cooling systems via conjugate heat transfer.

productLines.name: Ansys Thermal Desktop
productLines.note: Thermal analysis tool used in the data-center applications workflow for two-phase flow modeling, relevant to two-phase liquid cooling architectures.

productLines.name: Ansys Twin Builder
productLines.note: Digital-twin software for data centers: reduced-order models used to predict failures and monitor component-to-facility performance in real-time operations, alongside cooling infrastructure analysis.

facts.text: Ansys Icepak 2026 R1 shipped with a system-level thermal management workflow that the vendor says delivers 3-5x quicker setup and 80% fewer clicks.
Synopsys completed its acquisition of Ansys on July 17, 2025; Ansys stock ceased to be listed for trading on the NASDAQ stock market.

faq.q: What do Ansys tools simulate for data-center cooling?
faq.a: The data-center applications page describes predicting airflow, heat transfer and cooling performance across servers, racks, containment and air/liquid cooling systems via conjugate heat transfer analysis, using tools including Icepak, Fluent and Thermal Desktop.

faq.q: Does Ansys Icepak support liquid cooling analysis?
faq.a: Yes. Liquid Cooling is listed among Icepak's product specs, alongside multi-fluid and complex flow modeling, thermoelectric cooler modeling and full conjugate heat transfer analyses for laminar and turbulent flows.

faq.q: Who owns Ansys?
faq.a: Synopsys (Nasdaq: SNPS) completed its acquisition of Ansys on July 17, 2025, after which Ansys stock was no longer listed for trading on the NASDAQ stock market.

faq.q: What is recent in Icepak for cooling design?
faq.a: The Icepak 2026 R1 release introduced a system-level thermal management workflow that the vendor says provides 3-5x quicker setup and 80% fewer clicks.

profiles.name: Deep Green
profiles.tagline: Operates modular, high-density, waterless data centres for AI and HPC that donate waste heat to local communities: racks up to 150 kW, PUE 1.07 and 4 weeks to rack. A 400 kW site is live in Manchester, further UK sites are in development and a heat-reuse project is proposed in Lansing, Michigan.

productLines.name: Heat-donating modular data centres
productLines.note: Modular, high-density, waterless data centres for AI and HPC placed next to heat partners; the site reports rack densities up to 150 kW, PUE of 1.07, 4 weeks to rack and a pipeline of 26 MW+.

productLines.name: DG01 Manchester
productLines.note: Live 400 kW data centre at a leisure centre in Urmston, Manchester; recovered heat is donated to the community, which the site says cuts CO2 by 100-150 tonnes per year.

productLines.name: UK development pipeline
productLines.note: North London site in development at 4.9 MW and Bradford DG03 in development at 5.6 MW, as listed on the company site.

productLines.name: Lansing heat-reuse project (proposed)
productLines.note: Proposed downtown Lansing, Michigan data centre with a 16 MW Bloom fuel cell installation whose waste heat would feed the Lansing Board of Water and Light's steam-to-hot-water district energy conversion, replacing a 15.3 MMBtu/hr natural gas boiler.

facts.text: On 2 April 2026 Deep Green published a Lansing Board of Water and Light analysis of its proposed 16 MW fuel-cell data centre in downtown Lansing, whose waste heat would feed the utility's district energy conversion and replace a 15.3 MMBtu/hr gas boiler (BWL projects 94% lower NOx vs a gas boiler); a City Council vote was expected 6 April 2026.
Octopus Energy Generation invested in Deep Green, whose stated mission is to deploy 300 MW of decarbonised data centres across UK and Ireland, Europe and North America.
Deep Green's concept began by immersing Nvidia A100 GPUs in a tank connected to a swimming pool as a heat sink, recapturing part of roughly 50 kW of computing power as heat.

faq.q: What does Deep Green offer?
faq.a: Modular, high-density, waterless data centres for AI and HPC placed next to heat partners, donating recovered waste heat to local communities. The site reports racks up to 150 kW, PUE of 1.07 and 4 weeks to rack.

faq.q: Where does Deep Green operate?
faq.a: DG01 is live at a leisure centre in Urmston, Manchester (400 kW); North London (4.9 MW) and Bradford DG03 (5.6 MW) are in development; a 16 MW fuel-cell heat-reuse project is proposed in Lansing, Michigan.

faq.q: How did Deep Green start?
faq.a: Around 2020 the founders immersed Nvidia A100 GPUs in a tank connected to a swimming pool, recapturing part of roughly 50 kW of computing power as heat; in 2023 Octopus Energy Generation invested, with a stated mission of 300 MW of decarbonised data centres.

faq.q: Where is Deep Green based?
faq.a: The contact page lists 3 Waterhouse Square, Greater London, England EC1N 2SW.

profiles.name: Heata
profiles.tagline: Runs a distributed cloud on server units attached to vented domestic hot-water cylinders in UK homes, using energy twice - once for compute and once for hot water. The company claims up to 80% lower carbon than a typical data centre for its heat-reusing model.

productLines.name: heata unit
productLines.note: Edge compute device that attaches to a vented domestic hot-water cylinder; waste heat from computing heats the household's water, in the company's words using energy twice - once for compute and once for hot water.

productLines.name: heata distributed cloud
productLines.note: Cloud compute service running workloads on the home-based network, with service pages for Kubernetes, VM clusters, action runners, Anyscale/Ray and Kubeflow.

productLines.name: Free hot water hosting
productLines.note: Programme under which households host heata units and receive hot water heated by the waste heat from cloud workloads running on the units.

facts.text: On 5 February 2025 heata announced that British Gas partnered with it to launch a trial reusing waste heat from distributed data processing to save households money on their energy bills.
On 28 October 2024 heata announced a partnership with expanso to extend its heat-reusing green cloud beyond specialised jobs to traditional workloads.

faq.q: How does heata cool its servers?
faq.a: heata units attach to vented domestic hot-water cylinders in UK homes; the waste heat from computing heats the household's water. The company describes this as using energy twice, once for compute and once for hot water.

faq.q: What compute services does heata offer?
faq.a: A distributed cloud running on the home-based network, with service pages covering Kubernetes, VM clusters, action runners, Anyscale/Ray and Kubeflow, plus security information.

faq.q: What has heata announced recently?
faq.a: On 5 February 2025 British Gas partnered with heata to launch a trial reusing waste heat from distributed data processing to save households money; in October 2024 heata partnered with expanso to extend its green cloud to traditional workloads.

faq.q: What does heata claim about carbon?
faq.a: The company states its model delivers up to 80% lower carbon than a typical data centre by reusing compute waste heat for hot water.

profiles.name: Chunghwa System Integration
profiles.tagline: Wholly-owned Chunghwa Telecom subsidiary headquartered in Taipei. It integrated the liquid-cooled data center announced in Kaohsiung with Supermicro and ASE (cold plates, CDUs, manifolds, cooling towers) and positions itself as an AIDC service provider with hosting and energy management including water cooling and PUE reduction.

productLines.name: Liquid-cooled data center integration
productLines.note: Deployed and integrated Supermicro liquid-cooled AI servers for host ASE in Kaohsiung, with a rack-level solution covering cold plates, cooling distribution units (CDUs), cooling distribution manifolds (CDM) and cooling towers; the announcement cites at least 20% energy savings and PUE below 1.2.

productLines.name: AIDC hosting and managed services
productLines.note: Managed hosting and maintenance model for AI data centers, covering infrastructure planning, construction and long-term operations and maintenance, which the company describes as its AIDC service provider positioning.

productLines.name: AIDC energy management
productLines.note: Energy management and ESG services for AI data center facilities, including water cooling, energy recycling and lowering PUE.

facts.text: In a 24 June 2026 article on its site (reprinted from Taiwan's Commercial Times), Chunghwa System Integration described its AIDC hosting business, noting it built Taiwan's first data center using water-cooling heat dissipation technology and citing energy management for AIDC facilities covering water cooling, energy recycling and lowering PUE; it also stated an IPO plan aiming to list within three years.
