On 6 June 2024, Supermicro, ASE and Chunghwa System Integration jointly announced Taiwan's first next-generation liquid-cooled data center in Kaohsiung: ASE hosts Supermicro liquid-cooled AI servers in a rack-level solution with cold plates, CDUs, cooling distribution manifolds and cooling towers, with at least 20% energy savings and PUE below 1.2.

faq.q: What did Chunghwa System Integration build in Kaohsiung?
faq.a: Announced 6 June 2024 with Supermicro and ASE: Taiwan's first next-generation liquid-cooled data center, where ASE hosts Supermicro liquid-cooled AI servers with cold plates, CDUs, cooling distribution manifolds and cooling towers, targeting at least 20% energy savings and PUE below 1.2.

faq.q: What role does the company play in such projects?
faq.a: As a wholly-owned Chunghwa Telecom subsidiary it handled integration of servers, energy management and data center operations for the Kaohsiung deployment.

faq.q: What is its AI data center business today?
faq.a: It positions itself as an AIDC service provider offering managed hosting and maintenance - infrastructure planning, construction and long-term operations and maintenance - plus energy management covering water cooling, energy recycling and lowering PUE.

faq.q: Where is the company headquartered?
faq.a: In Taipei City (3F, No. 52, Section 2, Jinshan South Road, Da'an District), with additional offices in Taipei, Taichung and a 5G AIoT technical center in Kaohsiung.

profiles.name: GDT (General Datatech)
profiles.tagline: Dallas-based IT services integrator (General Datatech, LP, 900+ employees) that readies AI data center sites for neoclouds and hyperscalers - coordinating data center space, power, liquid cooling and cabling - and assesses traditional facilities for liquid-cooled GPU infrastructure retrofits.
profiles.ownership: General Datatech, LP; company site announces it is joining Softcat

productLines.name: AI-ready site preparation
productLines.note: For neoclouds, AI hyperscalers and data center providers: coordinates data center space, power, liquid cooling and cabling so facilities are ready when infrastructure arrives, with rapid cluster deployment from purchase order to live capacity in some cases in as little as 30 days and on-demand technician teams including weekends.

productLines.name: Data center AI-readiness assessment
productLines.note: Holistic facility assessment covering whether existing power and cooling capacity can support planned AI workloads, what physical changes higher-density infrastructure requires, and whether retrofitting for liquid-cooled GPU infrastructure makes sense versus modular data centers or cloud and neocloud options.

productLines.name: AI Factory Center of Excellence
productLines.note: Dallas facility launched 22 October 2026 where customers explore AI use cases and run proofs of concept on an integrated AI factory stack with NVIDIA, Cisco and NetApp technologies; the launch article does not specify cooling details.

productLines.name: Multi-site AI lifecycle and managed services
productLines.note: Lifecycle and managed services across multiple sites, alongside deployment automation, for AI infrastructure serving neocloud and hyperscaler customers.

facts.text: On 9 November 2026 GDT published guidance on adapting traditional data centers for AI, including why liquid cooling is not a simple upgrade: supporting liquid-cooled GPU infrastructure can require significant facility changes, liquid cooling standards are still evolving, and networking and storage equipment may still require air cooling alongside liquid-cooled NVIDIA GPU systems.

GDT launched an AI Factory Center of Excellence in Dallas on 22 October 2026, an environment where customers run AI proofs of concept on a full integrated AI factory stack using NVIDIA, Cisco and NetApp technologies.

faq.q: What does GDT do in liquid cooling?
faq.a: As part of AI-ready site preparation for neoclouds and hyperscalers it coordinates data center space, power, liquid cooling and cabling so facilities are ready when infrastructure arrives, and assesses whether existing facilities can support liquid-cooled GPU infrastructure.

faq.q: How fast does GDT deploy AI clusters?
faq.a: The company cites rapid cluster deployment from purchase order to live capacity in some cases in as little as 30 days, supported by on-demand technician teams including weekends.

faq.q: What does GDT say about liquid cooling retrofits?
faq.a: Its November 2026 guidance states liquid cooling is not a simple upgrade: most traditional data centers were built around air cooling, retrofits can be extensive, standards are still evolving, and mixed environments may need air cooling for networking and storage alongside liquid-cooled NVIDIA GPU systems.

faq.q: Where is GDT based and who owns it?
faq.a: Headquarters are the GDT Innovation Campus at 999 Metromedia Place, Dallas, Texas; the legal entity is General Datatech, LP, and the company site announces it is joining Softcat.

profiles.name: Qarnot
profiles.tagline: French cloud-HPC provider that distributes computing to sites that consume the waste heat, using patented direct liquid cooling to recover up to 95% of server heat and eliminate traditional cooling systems such as ventilation and air conditioning. Acquired by Scaleway to strengthen a European Cloud & AI platform.

productLines.name: Qarnot cloud HPC with heat reuse
productLines.note: Turnkey cloud platform for engineering simulation (CFD/CAE with tools such as Abaqus, Ansys Fluent and OpenFOAM) whose servers are housed in heating devices; the company states it reuses 95% of the heat generated by the servers and that simulations carry up to 80% less carbon thanks to its heat-reuse technology.

productLines.name: Heat-reuse data center deployments
productLines.note: Server heat is delivered to high-heat-consumption sites; deployments cited by the company include district heating in Brescia with utility A2A and wellness/aquatic centres. The heat-reuse approach is stated to eliminate the need for traditional cooling systems such as ventilation and air conditioning.

facts.text: Scaleway announced on July 10, 2026 that it acquires Qarnot to strengthen its European Cloud & AI platform with low-carbon HPC; the release credits Qarnot with patented direct liquid cooling that recovers up to 95% of server heat and cuts carbon emissions by up to 80%.

Existing heat-reuse deployments cited in the acquisition release include district heating in Brescia with A2A and wellness/aquatic centres; Qarnot states its model places servers at high-heat-consumption sites rather than in conventionally cooled data centers.

faq.q: How does Qarnot cool its servers?
faq.a: It uses patented direct liquid cooling to capture server heat and reuses 95% of it at high-heat-consumption sites, which the company says eliminates the need for traditional cooling systems such as ventilation and air conditioning.

faq.q: Who owns Qarnot?
faq.a: Scaleway announced the acquisition of Qarnot on July 10, 2026 to strengthen its European Cloud & AI platform with low-carbon HPC technology.

faq.q: What workloads run on Qarnot's platform?
faq.a: Ready-to-use cloud HPC for engineers, including CFD and CAE simulations with tools such as Abaqus, Ansys Fluent and OpenFOAM, with up to 80% lower carbon emissions claimed for simulations.

faq.q: Where does the recovered heat go?
faq.a: Deployments cited by the company include district heating in Brescia with utility A2A and wellness/aquatic centres that consume server heat directly.

profiles.name: SimScale
profiles.tagline: Cloud-based, AI-native engineering simulation provider (SimScale GmbH, Munich) whose data center cooling offering covers direct-to-chip liquid cooling, cold plate sizing and optimization, immersion tanks, manifolds, CDU design and hybrid air-liquid systems, run in a browser without local HPC.

productLines.name: Data center cooling simulation
productLines.note: Cloud CFD for high-density AI/HPC rooms: direct-to-chip liquid cooling, cold plate optimization, immersion tanks, manifolds, CDU design, heat exchanger performance and hybrid air-liquid systems, with ASHRAE TC 9.9, ASHRAE 90.4 and EN 50600 checks. Users include Submer (SmartPod), NDC-GARBE, Silent-Aire and One Stop Systems (400 W AI edge enclosure).

productLines.name: Engineering AI and Physics AI for thermal design
productLines.note: Engineering AI builds simulation models from BIM/CAD and meshes rack geometry; Physics AI predicts results across many CRAH layouts and supply temperatures in minutes. The cooling page cites 16 minutes to intervene after a cooling supply failure, plus 50% less development time and 95% lower cooling energy cost versus air cooling.

facts.text: Launched the Engineering AI Blueprint built with NVIDIA technologies (announced November 12, 2026), extending the AI-native simulation line that SimScale applies to data-center cooling design on its solutions pages.

Announced September 15, 2026 that SimScale Engineering AI moved physics simulation inside Onshape at the exact moment a design decision gets made; the same platform is the basis of its data-center cooling simulation offering, and a Nominal agentic design-and-test loop followed on November 19, 2026.

faq.q: What liquid cooling scenarios can SimScale simulate?
faq.a: Its data center cooling offering covers direct-to-chip liquid cooling, cold plate sizing and optimization, immersion tanks and manifolds, CDU design, heat exchanger performance and hybrid air-liquid systems for AI and HPC workloads.

faq.q: Which data center customers are named on its cooling page?
faq.a: Submer for immersion cooling (SmartPod), NDC-GARBE for cooling resilience and smoke/fire scenarios, Silent-Aire, and One Stop Systems for a 400 W AI edge enclosure study.

faq.q: When and where was SimScale founded?
faq.a: Founded in November 2012 by five engineers; headquartered in Munich, Germany, as SimScale GmbH, with 900,000+ engineers on the platform.

faq.q: Does the platform support standards compliance checks?
faq.a: Yes, ASHRAE TC 9.9, ASHRAE 90.4 and EN 50600 compliance checks are supported in the data center cooling workflows, run cloud-native in a browser without HPC or VPN.

profiles.name: Southwest Research Institute (SwRI)
profiles.tagline: Independent applied R&D institute that validates data center liquid-cooling equipment at scale, with a Large-Scale Heat Exchanger Test Facility rated up to 5 MW of heating and cooling and a medium-scale facility up to 1 MW heat load, and leads the Data Center Immersion Fluids (DCIF) consortium for immersion-cooling fluids and materials.
profiles.ownership: Independent R&D organization providing services to government and industry clients (per swri.org)

productLines.name: Data center cooling testing and validation
productLines.note: Thermal performance testing of heat exchangers and CDUs (first-of-kind early product validation), plus pumps, VFDs, in-row and rear-door heat exchangers, with P-Q and loss-of-utility-cooling transient tests. The Large-Scale Heat Exchanger Test Facility is rated up to 5 MW of heating and cooling; the medium-scale facility up to 1 MW heat load.

productLines.name: Liquid cooling R&D
productLines.note: Research areas include direct liquid cooling (single- and two-phase), immersion cooling, spray cooling, heat pipes and vapor chambers, waste heat recovery, and PUE/WUE reduction, using custom thermal test flow loops.

productLines.name: Data Center Immersion Fluids (DCIF) Consortium
productLines.note: Consortium helping the IT industry develop methods and standards to test and evaluate fluids and materials in immersion cooling: electrical properties (dielectric constant and strength), fluid aging, flash point, heat transfer figure of merit and material compatibility, under thermal, chemical, environmental and mechanical stressors. Open to new members.

facts.text: On November 17, 2025 SwRI announced expanded large-scale heat exchanger testing with heat loads of up to 5 MW, supporting the testing and validation of coolant distribution units, secondary side pumps and cooling fluid distribution for IT equipment

SwRI's 2025 annual report describes heat exchanger testing from 500 kilowatts up to 2.75 megawatts in its current configuration, with the potential to exceed 5 megawatts, to help the industry establish a performance baseline for data centers

faq.q: What liquid-cooling hardware can SwRI test?
faq.a: Heat exchangers and CDUs (first-of-kind early product validation), pumps and pump skids, VFDs including harmonics, in-row and rear-door heat exchangers, mechanical skids and PIC valves, including P-Q and loss-of-utility-cooling transient tests.

faq.q: How large are SwRI's cooling test facilities?
faq.a: The Large-Scale Heat Exchanger Test Facility is rated up to 5 MW of heating and cooling, and the medium-scale facility up to 1 MW heat load, with custom flow loops for thermal testing.

faq.q: What is the DCIF Consortium?
faq.a: An SwRI-led consortium developing methods and standards to test and evaluate fluids and materials for data center immersion cooling, covering electrical properties, fluid aging, flash point, heat transfer figure of merit and material compatibility; it is open to new members.

faq.q: Who does SwRI work for?
faq.a: It describes itself as an R&D problem solver providing independent, premier services to government and industry clients.

profiles.name: Nor-Tech
profiles.tagline: Minnesota HPC and AI integrator (authorized Supermicro systems integrator) that designs, integrates and validates liquid-cooled solutions, from single liquid-cooled servers to enterprise-scale AI clusters, drawing on roughly 30 years of integration experience.

productLines.name: Liquid-cooled server solutions
productLines.note: Design, integration and validation of liquid-cooled solutions from single liquid-cooled servers to enterprise-scale AI clusters, claiming improved cooling efficiency, lower energy use, greater rack density, longer hardware life and less HVAC dependence. A cited project headline covers a liquid-cooled solution for a large U.S. agency (no details published).

productLines.name: AI and HPC cluster integration
productLines.note: Ready-to-deploy and turnkey HPC clusters, custom GPU servers and AI infrastructure integration services for scalable performance, including turnkey password-cracking clusters built for a large U.S. organization.

productLines.name: AI thermal engineering and support
productLines.note: Support offerings covering GPU server overheating (AI thermal engineering) and emergency HPC cluster support for rapid AI and HPC recovery, published December 17, 2025.

facts.text: Announced AI infrastructure integration services for scalable performance (April 17, 2026), alongside ready-to-deploy HPC clusters (January 19, 2026) and custom GPU servers (January 29, 2026) in its integration portfolio, which includes liquid-cooled solutions.
Published its AI thermal engineering support offering for GPU server overheating and an emergency HPC cluster support service for rapid AI/HPC recovery, both dated December 17, 2025.

faq.q: What does Nor-Tech offer for liquid cooling?
faq.a: It designs, integrates and validates liquid-cooled solutions from single liquid-cooled servers to enterprise-scale AI clusters, as an authorized Supermicro systems integrator, claiming improved cooling efficiency, lower energy use, greater rack density and longer hardware life.

faq.q: Where is Nor-Tech located?
faq.a: At 901 Cliff Rd. E., Suite 101, Burnsville, Minnesota 55337, holding Minnesota State Contract #160318.

faq.q: How much integration experience does the company cite?
faq.a: Its liquid-cooled solutions page cites roughly 30 years of integration experience; the site does not state a founding year.

faq.q: What has it published recently?
faq.a: AI thermal engineering support for GPU server overheating and emergency HPC cluster recovery services (December 17, 2025), and in 2026 AI infrastructure integration services, ready-to-deploy HPC clusters and custom GPU servers.

profiles.name: PurgeRite
profiles.tagline: Houston-based specialist in liquid cooling fluid management whose mechanical flushing, purging and filtration services span the thermal chain from chillers to coolant distribution units. Vertiv completed its acquisition on December 4, 2025 to expand its liquid cooling services portfolio.

productLines.name: Mechanical flushing, purging and filtration services
productLines.note: Services for data centers and other mission-critical facilities covering mechanical flushing, purging and filtration, with expertise spanning from chillers to coolant distribution units (CDUs); clean fluid loops start with optimal flow at commissioning, per the acquisition announcement.

productLines.name: Liquid cooling thermal-chain services
productLines.note: Described at announcement as having engineering expertise and proprietary technologies for liquid cooling across the thermal chain, relationships with hyperscalers and Tier 1 colocation providers, and plans to expand its service center network across North America under Vertiv.

facts.text: Vertiv completed its acquisition of PurgeRite on December 4, 2025, adding mechanical flushing, purging and filtration services for data centers and mission-critical facilities to Vertiv's liquid cooling services portfolio; the acquisition intent had been announced on November 3, 2025.

At announcement, Vertiv described PurgeRite's engineering expertise and proprietary technologies for liquid cooling across the thermal chain, its relationships with hyperscalers and Tier 1 colocation providers, and plans to expand PurgeRite's service center network across North America.

faq.q: What does PurgeRite do?
faq.a: It provides mechanical flushing, purging and filtration services for data centers and other mission-critical facilities, with expertise spanning from chillers to coolant distribution units (CDUs), supporting clean fluid loops from commissioning onward.

faq.q: Who owns PurgeRite?
faq.a: Vertiv completed its acquisition of PurgeRite on December 4, 2025, having announced the intent on November 3, 2025, to expand its liquid cooling services portfolio.

faq.q: Where is PurgeRite based?
faq.a: Headquartered in Houston, Texas, with plans announced at acquisition to expand its service center network across North America.

faq.q: Who are its customers?
faq.a: The acquisition announcement cites relationships with hyperscalers and Tier 1 colocation providers.

profiles.name: Penguin Solutions
profiles.tagline: US HPC and AI infrastructure provider that designs and builds data centers using direct-to-chip liquid cooling, single-phase and two-phase immersion, rear-door heat exchangers and hybrid air/liquid designs. Its power-and-cooling expertise group works alongside its Full-Stack AI Factory platform business.

productLines.name: Data center power and cooling design services
productLines.note: Design services covering direct-to-chip cooling via cold plates, single-phase immersion in non-conductive fluids (oils, fluorocarbons, esters), two-phase immersion, rear-door heat exchangers and hybrid combinations. AI racks are cited at up to 50 kW or more per rack and 44 kW for an H100 rack with four nodes, versus 8.6-10 kW for a traditional rack.

productLines.name: Immersion-ready systems (AMD and Shell partnership)
productLines.note: Penguin Solutions partnered with AMD and Shell for immersion-ready systems deployed at Shell's Houston data center, which the company reports boosted performance and lowered emissions.

productLines.name: Full-Stack AI Factory Platform
productLines.note: Platform family (brands OriginAI, ClusterWareAI, ComputeAI, MemoryAI) presented on the company's data-center power and cooling expertise pages for AI factory deployments that pair high-density compute with its cooling design services.

facts.text: Announced (September 9, 2026) that its Full-Stack AI Factory Platform enables Lektra's AI data centers; the platform line is presented on the company's data-center power and cooling expertise page together with its direct-to-chip and immersion offerings.
Became an NVIDIA AI Factory Specialized Partner, announced June 23, 2026, extending the AI factory business that its data-center power and cooling design services support.

faq.q: What liquid cooling approaches does Penguin Solutions design for?
faq.a: Its data-center power and cooling expertise covers direct-to-chip cold plates, single-phase liquid immersion in non-conductive fluids, two-phase immersion, rear-door heat exchangers, high-efficiency air cooling and hybrid combinations.

faq.q: Where is Penguin Solutions based and how is it listed?
faq.a: The company site lists headquarters at 45800 Northport Loop W, Fremont, California, and schema markup on the site identifies Penguin Solutions, Inc. with ticker PENG.

faq.q: What rack densities does the company cite for liquid-cooled AI deployments?
faq.a: Its cooling page cites AI racks requiring up to 50 kW or more per rack, and 44 kW for a rack of four H100 nodes, against 8.6-10 kW for a traditional rack.

faq.q: What are its recent AI-infrastructure milestones?
faq.a: Announced September 9, 2026 that its Full-Stack AI Factory Platform enables Lektra's AI data centers, and on June 23, 2026 that it became an NVIDIA AI Factory Specialized Partner.

profiles.name: Cundall
profiles.tagline: Engineering consultancy offering data-centre design, due diligence and R&D; its current liquid-cooling work centers on retrofit pathways for existing air-cooled hyperscale sites, notably compressor-assisted coolant distribution units (CA-CDUs) and liquid-cooling-ready new builds.

productLines.name: Liquid-cooling retrofit R&D (CA-CDU study)
productLines.note: R&D engagement for a confidential hyperscale client evaluating compressor-assisted CDU technology in existing air-cooled data centres, with technical water supply typically around 30 C and return around 40 C, free cooling when ambient is at least 2 C below supply, and mechanical mode when ambient is less than 5 C below return temperature.

productLines.name: Technical due diligence of liquid-cooling technology
productLines.note: Due-diligence project for a venture capital investor reviewing a start-up's liquid-to-liquid and liquid-to-air cooling solutions for HPC, AI and data-centre relevance, covering performance data, technical literature and product information.

productLines.name: Data-centre engineering services
productLines.note: Site due diligence, design, construction administration, technical due diligence and R&D; the team, established in 2006, also evaluates liquid-cooling deployment pathways for existing air-cooled hyperscale data-centre environments.

facts.text: In a November 2026 blog, 'Powering intelligence: How AI is redefining data centre design', Cundall wrote that developers can reduce future retrofit risk by making facilities ready for liquid cooling from the outset, citing rack loads of 100 kW per rack.

In a July 2026 blog, Cundall concluded that compressor-assisted CDUs remove the dependency on chilled water by integrating a refrigeration circuit directly within the unit, making liquid-cooling retrofits feasible in air-cooled facilities without chilled water.

faq.q: What liquid-cooling retrofit research has Cundall published?
faq.a: A July 2026 blog on compressor-assisted CDUs argued they remove the dependency on chilled water by integrating a refrigeration circuit within the unit, enabling liquid-cooling retrofits in existing air-cooled data centres; a November 2026 blog recommends making new facilities liquid-cooling ready from the outset.

faq.q: Has Cundall done liquid-cooling work for hyperscale operators?
faq.a: Yes. It was engaged by a confidential hyperscale client to evaluate adding compressor-assisted CDU technology into existing air-cooled data centres, using technical water supply around 30 C and return around 40 C, with free cooling when ambient air is at least 2 C below supply temperature.

faq.q: Does Cundall evaluate liquid-cooling technologies for investors?
faq.a: Yes. Its technical due-diligence project for a venture capital firm reviewed a start-up's liquid-to-liquid and liquid-to-air cooling solutions, including performance data and technical literature, for HPC, AI and data-centre relevance.

profiles.name: UNICOM Engineering
profiles.tagline: OEM integration and deployment-services provider of purpose-built application platforms and appliances; in 2026 it announced liquid- and immersion-cooled platform collaborations with GRC, Fourier Cooling and Nexalus covering AI, HPC, edge and modular data-center infrastructure.

productLines.name: Immersion-cooled AI solutions with GRC
productLines.note: Turnkey single-phase immersion offerings combining UNICOM immersion-ready platforms with GRC immersion cooling, targeting AI, HPC, GPU-as-a-Service, high-density compute and industrial data centers, plus edge use cases with GRC's ICEraQ Nano, deployed at UNICOM's Plano, Texas lab after 4 years of joint testing.

productLines.name: Cooling-defined modular AI data centers with Fourier Cooling
productLines.note: Pairs Fourier prefabricated containerized modular data centers supporting direct-to-chip, immersion and hybrid fan-wall liquid cooling with UNICOM liquid-cooled Tier-1 platforms and lifecycle services; Fourier reports 600+ MW of deployed or in-progress liquid-cooled infrastructure and 30 MW of turnkey capacity in as little as six months.

productLines.name: Liquid-cooled OEM edge solutions with Nexalus
productLines.note: Announced partnership combining Nexalus cooling technology with UNICOM design, integration and global manufacturing for liquid-cooled edge solutions targeting data centers, edge and industrial environments, including AI, cloud and telecom workloads.

productLines.name: OEM integration and deployment services
productLines.note: OEM design, system integration, branding, logistics, compliance and global support for edge, AI and data-center solutions, with an 'Advanced thermal solutions for dense, efficient systems' liquid-cooling capability area described on the homepage.

facts.text: During Dell Technologies World 2026, Nexalus and UNICOM Engineering formalized a strategic partnership to deliver liquid-cooled OEM edge solutions combining Nexalus cooling technology with UNICOM design, integration and global manufacturing for AI, cloud and telecom workloads.

On April 28, 2026 UNICOM Engineering and Fourier Cooling announced a collaboration on cooling-defined modular AI data center infrastructure supporting direct-to-chip, immersion and hybrid fan-wall liquid cooling; Fourier reported more than 600 MW of deployed and in-progress liquid-cooled infrastructure and 30 MW of turnkey capacity in as little as six months.

On March 10, 2026 UNICOM Engineering and GRC announced expanded turnkey immersion-cooled AI solutions built on 4 years of joint testing, including deployment of GRC's ICEraQ Nano at UNICOM's Plano, Texas lab for AI, HPC, industrial and edge use cases.

faq.q: What liquid-cooling partnerships has UNICOM Engineering announced in 2026?
faq.a: Three: an expanded immersion-cooled AI collaboration with GRC announced March 10, 2026; a modular AI data-center collaboration with Fourier Cooling announced April 28, 2026; and a liquid-cooled OEM edge partnership with Nexalus formalized during Dell Technologies World 2026.

faq.q: What does the GRC collaboration include?
faq.a: Turnkey single-phase immersion solutions combining UNICOM immersion-ready platforms with GRC cooling for AI, HPC, GPU-as-a-Service, industrial and edge use cases, with GRC's ICEraQ Nano deployed at UNICOM's Plano, Texas lab after 4 years of joint testing.

faq.q: What cooling technologies does the Fourier Cooling collaboration support?
faq.a: Fourier supplies prefabricated containerized modular data centers supporting direct-to-chip, immersion and hybrid fan-wall liquid cooling; Fourier reports over 600 MW of deployed and in-progress liquid-cooled infrastructure and 30 MW of turnkey capacity deliverable in as little as six months.

profiles.name: CSA Group
profiles.tagline: Independent, not-for-profit membership association providing testing and certification; its data center compliance and evaluation services cover cooling equipment including chillers, cooling distribution units and cooling towers, evaluated at component level and combined into operational assemblies.

productLines.name: Data Center Compliance & Evaluation Services
productLines.note: Evaluates cooling equipment including chillers, cooling distribution units and cooling towers at component level and as operational assemblies; also covers power (UPS, BESS, switchgear, busway), IT infrastructure (servers, racks, PDUs), Field Evaluation, Canadian Special Inspections and pre-construction compliance reviews; CSA is an OSHA-recognized NRTL.

productLines.name: Standards development
productLines.note: CSA Group was established in 1919 as the Canadian Engineering Standards Association (CESA) and operates as a not-for-profit standards organization; per its August 2026 announcement, the Canadian Standards Association moves forward as a standalone not-for-profit organization after the sale of its testing, inspection and certification business.

facts.text: In August 2026 CSA Group announced the sale of its testing, inspection and certification business to Kiwa Group, with the Canadian Standards Association to move forward as a standalone not-for-profit organization focused on its public-benefit standards mandate; the data center evaluation services sit within the business being sold.

As of November 2026, CSA Group's data center services evaluate cooling equipment including chillers, cooling distribution units and cooling towers at both component level and combined into operational assemblies, alongside power, IT infrastructure and connectivity equipment.

faq.q: What cooling equipment does CSA Group evaluate for data centers?
faq.a: Its data center services evaluate chillers, cooling distribution units, cooling towers and related HVAC infrastructure at the component level and as operational assemblies, with CSA Group operating as an OSHA-recognized Nationally Recognized Testing Laboratory and an accredited Certification Body in Canada.

faq.q: Is CSA Group's testing business changing ownership?
faq.a: Yes. In August 2026 CSA Group announced the sale of its testing, inspection and certification business to Kiwa Group, with the Canadian Standards Association continuing as a standalone not-for-profit organization focused on standards.

faq.q: What is CSA Group and when was it founded?
faq.a: An independent, not-for-profit membership association established in 1919 as the Canadian Engineering Standards Association (CESA), described on its FAQ as a solutions-based standards organization.

profiles.name: Fortum
profiles.tagline: Fortum is an energy company operating the district heating network of the Finnish capital region. Waste heat from Microsoft's data centres in Espoo and Kirkkonummi will be recovered into the network, and in May 2026 Fortum started heat production at heat pump plants sized so the data centres can cover about 40% of the area's heat demand.
profiles.ownership: Listed on Nasdaq Helsinki; the Fortum Group was formed in 1998 in the merger of the IVO and Neste groups

productLines.name: Data centre waste-heat recovery, Helsinki region
productLines.note: Heat pump plants at Hepokorpi (Espoo) and Kolabacken (Kirkkonummi) with 72 water-to-water heat pumps producing up to 180 MW of district heat, 40 air-to-water heat pumps, 200 MW of electric boiler capacity and 20,000 m3 (800 MWh) heat storage; expected to cover about 40% of the area's roughly 2 TWh annual district heat demand of 250,000 users.

productLines.name: District heating from recovered heat and heat pumps
productLines.note: Waste heat and heat pumps, including wastewater treatment and smaller data centres, cover almost a quarter of network heat today; with the Microsoft data centres this rises to about 65%. Fortum reports about 85% non-fossil heat sources in 2025.

productLines.name: Data centre energy solutions
productLines.note: Fortum offers energy solutions for data centres in the Helsinki region, including connection of waste heat to its district heating network; site requirements it lists are proximity to the network, a sufficiently large plot, fossil-free electricity supply and data connectivity.

facts.text: On 6 May 2026 Fortum announced it had started heat production at two large data-centre sites: heat pump plants at Hepokorpi (Espoo) and Kolabacken (Kirkkonummi) with 72 water-to-water heat pumps producing up to 180 MW of district heat, 40 air-to-water heat pumps, 200 MW of electric boilers and 20,000 m3 (800 MWh) heat storage. Waste-heat recovery from Microsoft's data centres begins step by step as construction phases complete.

Fortum's collaboration with Microsoft, announced in 2022, routes waste heat from two new data centres in Espoo and Kirkkonummi into the district heating network; the data centres are expected to supply roughly 40% of the area's district heat, and about 75% of the centres' waste heat will be used annually. The work has EU NextGenerationEU funding and investment support from Finland's Ministry of Economic Affairs and Employment.

faq.q: What did Fortum start in May 2026?
faq.a: On 6 May 2026 Fortum announced it had started heat production at its heat pump plants at Hepokorpi in Espoo and Kolabacken in Kirkkonummi: 72 water-to-water heat pumps producing up to 180 MW of district heat, 40 air-to-water heat pumps, 200 MW of electric boilers and 20,000 m3 (800 MWh) of heat storage. Recovery of waste heat from Microsoft's data centres begins step by step.

faq.q: How much district heat can come from the data centres?
faq.a: Fortum expects data-centre waste heat to cover roughly 40% of district heat demand in the Espoo-Kirkkonummi area, about 2 TWh per year for 250,000 users, and that about 75% of the data centres' waste heat will be used annually.

faq.q: Which data centres supply Fortum's network?
faq.a: Microsoft's two data centres under construction at Hepokorpi in Espoo and Kolabacken in Kirkkonummi, Finland, will supply waste heat to Fortum's district heating network in the capital region.

faq.q: Is the project publicly supported?
faq.a: Yes. Fortum's page states the waste-heat work has EU NextGenerationEU funding plus investment support from Finland's Ministry of Economic Affairs and Employment.

profiles.name: Dalkia
profiles.tagline: Dalkia is an EDF Group energy-services company that designs, builds and operates heating and cooling networks in France and provides energy services for data centres, recovering by-product heat from data centres such as the Meteo France supercomputer site in Toulouse.
profiles.ownership: Subsidiary of the EDF Group, as stated on dalkia.com

productLines.name: Green Data Center services
productLines.note: Design, operation and optimization of data centres: ventilation and air conditioning, energy management, audits, predictive maintenance and control via digital twins on the Dalkia Analytics (Metron) platform, including server re-layout and waste-heat recovery; Dalkia states it operates 80 data centres in France.

productLines.name: District heating and cooling networks
productLines.note: Dalkia designs, builds and operates heating and cooling networks for local authorities, about 330 networks with 2,900 km of pipes, using recovered heat from data centres and industrial processes.

productLines.name: TED network, Toulouse
productLines.note: Heating and cooling network operated by Dalkia (about 75 km of piping, more than 150 buildings, equivalent of 34,000 dwellings) that captures heat from the Espace Clement Ader data centre hosting Meteo France supercomputers to supply heating and chilled water to the Toulouse Aerospace zone.

facts.text: It was reported in July 2025 that waste heat from Meteo France supercomputers at the Espace Clement Ader data centre in Toulouse will heat 27 large buildings, equivalent to about 1,800 homes, via the district heating network operated by Dalkia.

The Toulouse Energie Durable (TED) heating and cooling network operated by Dalkia entered service in autumn 2019; about 75 km of piping serves more than 150 buildings, equivalent of 34,000 dwellings, including heat recovered from the Meteo France supercomputer data centre and chilled water supply for the Toulouse Aerospace zone.

faq.q: What does Dalkia do with data-centre waste heat?
faq.a: Dalkia operates heating and cooling networks that recover by-product heat from data centres and industry. In Toulouse, its TED network captures heat from the Espace Clement Ader data centre (13,000 m2, hosting Meteo France supercomputers) to heat buildings and to supply chilled water for air conditioning in the Toulouse Aerospace zone.

faq.q: How large is Dalkia's network and data-centre business?
faq.a: Dalkia reports operating about 330 heating and cooling networks with some 2,900 km of pipes, and states that it operates and optimizes 80 data centres in France.

faq.q: Who owns Dalkia?
faq.a: Dalkia is a subsidiary of the EDF Group, as stated on its corporate website.

faq.q: What was announced for Toulouse in 2025?
faq.a: In July 2025 it was reported that waste heat from Meteo France's Toulouse supercomputers would heat 27 large buildings, equivalent to about 1,800 homes, on the district heating network operated by Dalkia.

profiles.name: Helen
profiles.tagline: Helen is an energy company owned by the City of Helsinki that recovers data-centre waste heat with heat pumps into its district heating network and supplies cooling in return. It has used data-centre waste heat since 2010, and in 2026 signed to connect a new data centre expected to deliver over 500,000 MWh of heat per year.
profiles.ownership: Owned by the City of Helsinki, per helen.fi corporate governance page

productLines.name: Heat recovery service for data centres
productLines.note: Helen recovers waste heat with heat pumps and feeds it into Helsinki's district heating network. Options: Helen invests in and runs the heat pump system, which also cools the data centre; the data centre builds its own system and Helen buys surplus heat at about 85 degrees C; or connection to district cooling. One data centre can heat 20,000 apartments.

productLines.name: Data-centre heat projects
productLines.note: At Telia's Helsinki Data Center, up to 90% of waste heat is recovered, heating about 14,000 two-room apartments, with the figure expected to rise to 28,000. In 2026 Helen agreed with OnZero Finland Oy to connect a new data centre expected to supply more than 500,000 MWh of heat annually, about 70,000 flats, from 2027.

productLines.name: District cooling
productLines.note: Helen offers district cooling connections for data centres located within its cooling network, with free cooling as a backup thanks to Finland's cool climate, alongside heat recovery.

facts.text: On 31 August 2026 Helen announced an agreement with OnZero Finland Oy to connect waste heat from a new data centre into Helsinki's district heating network. Heat recovery is scheduled to begin in 2027 and, when fully operational, is expected to deliver more than 500,000 MWh of heat annually, enough to heat roughly 70,000 flats.

Helen has used waste heat from data centres in its district heating network since 2010, as stated in its 2026 announcement of the OnZero Finland Oy agreement. At Telia's Helsinki Data Center, up to 90% of waste heat is recovered, heating about 14,000 two-room apartments, a figure expected to rise to 28,000.

faq.q: What did Helen announce in August 2026?
faq.a: On 31 August 2026 Helen announced an agreement with OnZero Finland Oy to connect waste heat from a new data centre into Helsinki's district heating network. Recovery begins in 2027 and is expected to deliver more than 500,000 MWh of heat per year when fully operational, enough for roughly 70,000 flats.

faq.q: How does Helen's heat-recovery service work for data centres?
faq.a: Three ways: Helen invests in and operates the heat pump system, which also cools the data centre, and takes the waste heat; the data centre builds its own system and Helen buys surplus heat at an input temperature of about 85 degrees C; or the data centre connects to Helen's district cooling network.

faq.q: How long has Helen recovered data-centre heat?
faq.a: Helen states it has used data-centre waste heat in its district heating network since 2010. At Telia's Helsinki Data Center, up to 90% of waste heat is recovered, heating about 14,000 two-room apartments, expected to rise to 28,000.

faq.q: Who owns Helen and when was it founded?
faq.a: Helen Ltd is owned by the City of Helsinki. Its history page records that the electricity company of the City of Helsinki was established in 1909, when Helsinki's small electricity companies were transferred to city ownership.

profiles.name: Eurovent
profiles.tagline: Eurovent is the European HVACR industry association, founded in 1956 and based in Brussels, representing over 100 companies directly. It published its Data Centre Cooling Guidebook in November 2026, and Eurovent Certita Certification operates the ITCU certification covering IT cooling units including rear-door coolers.
profiles.ownership: Member-funded European industry association for HVACR manufacturers; its stated scope includes data centre cooling technologies

productLines.name: Data Centre Cooling Guidebook
productLines.note: Guidebook published in November 2026. Eurovent describes it as explaining, in clear and technology-neutral terms, what data centre cooling is, how it works and why it matters, building a shared technical vocabulary for informed policy-making and aligning performance requirements with environmental goals without compromising reliability.

productLines.name: ITCU certification programme
productLines.note: Operated by Eurovent Certita Certification: third-party certification of IT cooling units, covering CRAC, CRAH, rear-door coolers (active or passive) and hybrid units. facts.text: In November 2026 Eurovent published its Data Centre Cooling Guidebook, a technology-neutral explanation of what data centre cooling is, how it works and why it matters, with chapters on liquid cooling, waste heat recovery, product certification, standards and EU legislation.

As checked in November 2026, the ITCU programme operated by Eurovent Certita Certification certifies CRAC, CRAH, rear-door cooler and hybrid IT cooling units for data centres, with independent verification of cooling capacity, energy efficiency, airflow and acoustics, annual factory audits and surveillance testing; its directory lists 746 certified products.

faq.q: What is Eurovent?
faq.a: Eurovent describes itself as the voice of the European HVACR industry, representing over 100 companies directly and more than 1,000 indirectly through 18 national associations. It was founded in 1956 and is based at Rue de la Loi 62, 1040 Brussels, Belgium.

faq.q: What has Eurovent published on data-centre cooling?
faq.a: The Eurovent Guidebook on Data Centre Cooling (2026), published 19 November 2026. Eurovent says it explains in technology-neutral terms what data centre cooling is, how it works and why it matters, and builds a shared technical vocabulary for informed policy-making.

faq.q: Is data-centre cooling equipment certified under Eurovent?
faq.a: Eurovent Certita Certification operates the ITCU programme covering CRAC, CRAH, rear-door cooler and hybrid units for data centres. It independently verifies declared cooling capacity, energy efficiency (EER, SEPRsens), airflow and acoustics, with annual factory audits and surveillance testing; the directory lists 746 certified products.

profiles.name: DLB Associates
profiles.tagline: DLB Associates is a US data-centre engineering firm founded in 1980 and based in Neptune, New Jersey, offering design engineering and commissioning for hyperscale, neo-cloud and colocation facilities, with a published liquid-cooling series on cold plates and CDUs. profiles.ownership: 65% majority stake held by Accenture; announced 16 December 2025, closed 22 January 2026

productLines.name: Data centre engineering and commissioning

productLines.name: Liquid-cooling engineering publications

facts.text: On 22 January 2026 Accenture completed the acquisition of a 65% majority stake in DLB Associates and its affiliate companies, first announced on 16 December 2025; DLB joined Accenture's Industry X infrastructure and capital projects practice.

In May 2026 DLB published TCS Coolant Integrity and System Readiness Best Practices, adding to its liquid-cooling series, which in 2025 included Coolant Distribution Units Part 1: Design (June), Liquid Cooling Cold Plates Part 1 (September), Server Cold Plates Part 2 (November) and Liquid Cold Plates Part 3 (December).

In December 2024 DLB's publications page records a new ASHRAE TC 9.9 technical bulletin, Liquid Cooling: Resiliency Guidance for Cold Plate Deployments, part of its long-running liquid-cooling technical output that began with Liquid-Cooling Trends in Data Centers in July 2019.

faq.q: Who owns DLB Associates?
faq.a: Accenture acquired a 65% majority stake in DLB Associates and its affiliate companies; the deal was announced on 16 December 2025 and closed on 22 January 2026, with DLB joining Accenture's Industry X infrastructure and capital projects practice.

faq.q: What services does DLB provide?
faq.a: Engineering and consulting for data centres and mission-critical facilities since 1980: site selection, due diligence, design engineering, commissioning, construction quality management and energy optimization, serving hyperscalers, neo-clouds and colocation providers.

faq.q: What liquid-cooling work has DLB published?
faq.a: A technical series on its publications page: Coolant Distribution Units Part 1: Design (June 2025), Liquid Cooling Cold Plates Part 1 (September 2025), Server Cold Plates Part 2 (November 2025), Liquid Cold Plates Part 3 (December 2025) and TCS Coolant Integrity and System Readiness Best Practices (May 2026), plus an ASHRAE TC 9.9 bulletin on resiliency guidance for cold plate deployments (December 2024).

faq.q: Where is DLB based and how large is it?

profiles.name: Exascale Labs

Its factory-built Modular Data Centers pre-integrate power, cooling and networking for AI workloads, and its infrastructure solutions span modular data centers, HVDC power, high-density cooling and data center interconnectivity.
profiles.ownership: Exascale Labs Holdings Inc., listed on Nasdaq (XLAB)

productLines.name: Modular Data Center (MDC)
productLines.note: A factory-built container that pre-integrates power, cooling and networking for high rack densities. productLines.name: AI infrastructure solutions
productLines.note: A software-defined GPU compute platform with Token Factory, GPU-as-a-service, GPU cluster management and optimization, and infrastructure spanning modular data centers, HVDC power, high-density cooling and data center interconnectivity, supporting training, fine-tuning and high-concurrency inference.

productLines.name: 800 VDC validation platform with Compal (announced)

facts.text: On 14 September 2026 Exascale Labs Holdings (Nasdaq: XLAB) announced a non-binding letter of intent with Compal Electronics to jointly develop a U.S.-based native 800 VDC validation platform using solid-state transformers, combining Compal GPU servers and liquid cooling systems with Exascale's Modular Data Center and power architecture.

On 19 May 2026 Exascale Labs and Compal announced an integrated AI infrastructure solution to be showcased at COMPUTEX Taipei 2026 (2-5 June): Compal AI servers with direct liquid cooling for high-power GPUs, the Exascale factory-built Modular Data Center pre-integrating power, cooling and networking, and an 800 V DC HVDC power architecture with solid-state transformers.

faq.q: What is the Exascale Modular Data Center?
faq.a: A factory-built container that pre-integrates power, cooling and networking, aimed at high rack densities for AI workloads. faq.q: What was agreed with Compal in September 2026?

Compal would provide the site, GPU servers and liquid cooling systems; Exascale the modular data center, SST power architecture and software, leading deployment, commissioning and testing. faq.q: Where is Exascale Labs headquartered?
faq.a: San Francisco, California, according to its press releases of May and September 2026.

profiles.name: EkkoSense
profiles.tagline: EkkoSense is a UK-headquartered software company founded in 2013 whose EkkoSoft Critical platform provides real-time monitoring and AI-driven optimization for data centres, including temperatures and flow rates across direct-to-chip, rear-door heat exchanger and hybrid liquid-cooled infrastructure.
profiles.hq: United Kingdom (head office city not published on its site)
profiles.ownership: Private company backed by PE investors, per ekkosense.com

productLines.name: EkkoSoft Critical - Liquid Cooling Optimization
productLines.note: Real-time monitoring of temperatures, flow rates and thermal behaviour across direct-to-chip, rear-door heat exchanger and hybrid liquid cooling deployments. Correlates liquid-cooling data with air-cooling, power and IT-load metrics in a single view, with governance controls, alerting and safety thresholds and a unified 3D operational view.

productLines.name: EkkoScore
productLines.note: A performance index for liquid cooling environments, helping teams understand how effectively thermal energy is being removed relative to IT load and operational constraints.

productLines.name: EkkoSoft Critical platform and EkkoSim
productLines.note: The wider platform includes a Data Center Digital Twin, Cooling Advisor, capacity planning, power monitoring, ESG reporting, sensors and 3DCIM under EkkoSoft Critical, plus the EkkoSim simulation offering. EkkoSense states it holds ISO 27001 and ISO 9001 accreditations and runs offices in North America, the UK, Europe and Australia.

facts.text: In February 2026 EkkoSense published its Data Center Liquid Cooling Optimization capability for EkkoSoft Critical: real-time monitoring of temperatures, flow rates and thermal behaviour across direct-to-chip, rear-door heat exchanger and hybrid liquid cooling deployments, with governance controls, alerting, defined safety thresholds and the EkkoScore performance index for liquid cooling environments.

EkkoSense was founded in 2013 with a mission to help organizations resolve the thermal risks their data centres face from inefficient cooling strategies, as stated on the company's about page; it now sells the EkkoSoft Critical real-time platform and EkkoSim simulation software.

faq.q: What does EkkoSoft Critical do for liquid-cooled data centres?
faq.a: It monitors temperatures, flow rates and thermal behaviour in real time across direct-to-chip, rear-door heat exchanger and hybrid liquid cooling deployments, and correlates liquid-cooling data with traditional air-cooling, power and IT-load metrics to give a single operational view across mixed cooling strategies.

faq.q: What is EkkoScore?
faq.a: EkkoScore is a performance index for liquid cooling environments. It helps teams understand how effectively thermal energy is being removed relative to IT load and operational constraints.

faq.q: How does EkkoSense help manage liquid-cooling risk?
faq.a: Governance controls, alerting and defined safety thresholds help operators manage the complexity of liquid cooling without introducing operational risk, supported by 3D visualization and analytics across liquid, air and hybrid cooling environments for ultra high-density AI workloads.

faq.q: When was EkkoSense founded and where does it operate?
faq.a: EkkoSense was founded in 2013 and lists a UK headquarters on its website, with offices in North America, the UK, Europe and Australia. The company states it is backed by PE investors and holds ISO 27001 and ISO 9001 accreditations.

profiles.name: Ramboll
profiles.tagline: Engineering consultancy whose data-centre practice advises owners on adopting liquid cooling and heat reuse, from immersion feasibility and hybrid cooling design to district-heating integration, backed by 15+ GW of designed and tested data-centre capacity.
profiles.ownership: Owned by the Ramboll Foundation (established 1971), described as its main owner and majority shareholder

productLines.name: Liquid cooling and heat-reuse advisory
productLines.note: Consulting that helps data-centre owners incorporate liquid cooling and heat reuse alongside site selection, energy supply, MEP engineering design, masterplanning and permitting; 15+ GW of data-centre space designed and tested and 1,000+ studies completed.

productLines.name: Hybrid and immersion cooling design guidance
productLines.note: Design guidance covering full immersion cooling supporting 100 kW per rack or more, cold-plate systems that typically capture around 80% of server heat, and secondary rear-door heat exchanger or air-side systems for the residual heat.

productLines.name: Heat reclaim and district-heating integration
productLines.note: Design of high-temperature heat rejection from immersion cooling so heat can be reclaimed into district heating, including water-to-water heat pumps to raise water temperature for heat-reuse applications.

productLines.name: Liquid-ready cooling infrastructure design
productLines.note: Chilled-water systems installed with taps for water-cooled equipment so data halls can migrate gradually to liquid cooling, plus hall designs without raised floors, where containment trenches bring cooling water to immersion tanks and racks with leak detection.

facts.text: On 23 September 2025 Ramboll published guidance for data-centre operators on cooling strategy and water use as part of NYCW 2025, covering maximising cycles of concentration and alternative water sources such as rainwater.

Ramboll's 13 December 2023 insight described advising on a small-scale Nordic data-centre conversion to full immersion cooling with heat reclaim into district heating, and noted cold plates typically capture around 80% of server heat, leaving residual heat for secondary systems.

faq.q: What does Ramboll do in data-centre liquid cooling?
faq.a: It is an engineering consultancy that helps data-centre owners incorporate liquid cooling and heat reuse within site selection, energy supply, MEP design and permitting. Its data-centre practice lists 15+ GW of capacity designed and tested and 1,000+ studies completed.

faq.q: Has Ramboll worked on immersion cooling projects?
faq.a: A December 2023 Ramboll insight describes work with a company that converted a Nordic data centre to full immersion cooling on a small scale, using the high heat-rejection temperatures for heat reclaim into a district-heating system.

faq.q: Does Ramboll recommend full liquid cooling for every site?
faq.a: No. Ramboll notes cold plates typically capture around 80% of server heat, so secondary rear-door heat exchangers or air-side systems are still needed, and many owners will choose a hybrid liquid and air environment.

faq.q: How does Ramboll prepare facilities for future liquid cooling?
faq.a: It designs chilled-water systems with taps for water-cooled equipment so data halls can migrate gradually, and no-raised-floor designs with containment trenches that bring cooling water to immersion tanks and racks while enabling leak detection.

profiles.name: Salute

productLines.name: Direct-to-Chip (DTC) liquid cooling operations service

productLines.name: Immersion cooling services

productLines.name: Air-to-liquid transition support
productLines.note: Full Service support for air-to-liquid transitions and new liquid-cooling deployments, with in-house CFD expertise, direct-to-chip assessments from planning to execution and a 24/7 helpdesk; Salute cites DLC at 70-90 kW per rack with heat rejection above 70 degrees C versus under 40 degrees C for air systems.

facts.text: Announced at NVIDIA GTC in Washington DC: a full-service Direct-to-Chip (DTC) liquid cooling operations service for AI/HPC data centers, which Salute describes as an industry first. Salute's current cooling services catalogue (site copyright 2026) lists direct liquid cooling and immersion cooling operations, with cited rack density limits of 15-20 kW for air cooling, 40-50 kW for rear-door air cooling, 70-90 kW for DLC and beyond 150 kW for full immersion.

faq.q: What liquid-cooling services does Salute provide?
faq.a: It operates direct-to-chip liquid cooling for AI/HPC data centers, covering design and operational assessment, commissioning support, chemistry management, leak detection, safety protocols, training and staffing, plus immersion cooling operations and full-service support for air-to-liquid transitions.

faq.q: What rack densities does Salute cite for each cooling method?
faq.a: Its services page cites peak limits of 15-20 kW per rack for air cooling, 40-50 kW for rear-door air cooling, 70-90 kW for direct liquid cooling, and more than 150 kW per rack for full immersion, with DLC heat rejection above 70 degrees C versus under 40 degrees C for air systems.

faq.q: What did Salute announce at NVIDIA GTC Washington DC?
faq.a: A full-service Direct-to-Chip (DTC) liquid cooling operations service for AI/HPC data centers, described by Salute as an industry first, expected to support roughly 250 MW of data center capacity in the coming months and an estimated 3,100 MW of additional capacity by end of 2027.

faq.q: Does Salute help existing air-cooled sites move to liquid?

profiles.name: HITT Contracting
profiles.tagline: US general contractor headquartered in Falls Church, Virginia, whose data center work includes liquid-cooled construction: closed-loop cold-plate systems moving heat through CDUs to facility water loops, supporting rack densities HITT quotes at up to 160 kW per rack versus 10 kW for air cooling.

productLines.name: Liquid-cooled data center construction
productLines.note: Construction of data centers using closed-loop liquid cooling: technical water circulates through cold plates on chips, transferring heat via coolant distribution units (CDUs) to a facility water loop and chilled water plant; HITT cites support for up to 160 kW per rack compared to 10 kW per rack with air cooling.

productLines.name: Liquid cooling retrofits and non-traditional sites
productLines.note: HITT positions liquid cooling as enabling retrofits of older buildings and deployment in non-traditional locations such as edge sites, historic buildings and office basements, where air-cooling infrastructure would be impractical.

productLines.name: AI and HPC data center building
productLines.note: General contracting for denser, more efficient data centers supporting AI and high-performance computing, with liquid cooling cited as delivering lower energy use, quieter and more compact technical spaces.

facts.text: On 27 August 2025 HITT published its article on liquid cooling in data center construction, describing closed-loop cold-plate systems carrying heat through CDUs to facility water loops and chilled water plants, and citing support for up to 160 kW per rack versus 10 kW per rack with air cooling.

On 10 June 2026 HITT announced it had broken ground on the Microsoft Alviso datacenter campus in San Jose, California, where HITT is general contractor for the second phase of development: 48 MW of critical capacity, with completion scheduled for 2028.

faq.q: What liquid cooling approach does HITT build?
faq.a: Closed-loop systems in which technical water circulates through cold plates on chips, transfers heat via coolant distribution units (CDUs) to a facility water loop and the chilled water plant. HITT cites support for up to 160 kW per rack compared to 10 kW per rack with air cooling.

faq.q: Can HITT retrofit existing buildings with liquid cooling?
faq.a: Yes. HITT says liquid cooling enables retrofits of older buildings and use of non-traditional locations such as edge sites, historic buildings and office basements, and its project teams include retrofit specialists.

faq.q: When was HITT founded and where is it headquartered?

faq.q: Why does HITT argue for liquid cooling in data centers?
faq.a: Its August 2025 article states liquids conduct heat far more efficiently than air, enabling denser and more efficient data centers with lower energy use, quieter and more compact spaces for AI and high-performance computing.

productLines.name: Immersion liquid cooling demonstration systems

productLines.name: Data center and cloud solutions

faq.a: Sweco is headquartered at Gjorwellsgatan 22, Stockholm, Sweden, and has about 23,000 architects, engineers and other experts. Its shares are listed on Nasdaq Stockholm.

profiles.name: ToffeeX
profiles.tagline: Physics-based generative design software for thermo-fluid engineering, spun out of Imperial College London and based in London. It grows GPU/CPU cold plate, manifold and heat-exchanger geometries from governing physics and chip power/heat maps rather than training data, with manufacturing constraints built in.
profiles.ownership: Private company and Imperial College London spinout; its 2020 seed round was led by IQ Capital

productLines.name: Generative cold plate and manifold design
productLines.note: Designs GPU/CPU cold plates, direct-to-chip cooling, rack cooling and distribution manifolds for AI workloads; fins and channels are generated from the chip's power/heat map and coolant limits with flow and heat solved at every step. A customer pilot reported 12%+ better cooling than a skived-fin GPU cold plate.

productLines.name: Simulated performance benchmarking
productLines.note: Published simulated comparisons versus skived fins include one-third the pressure drop for the same 61 C peak (1.0 m/s vs 0.3 m/s) and roughly 10% lower pressure drop versus 80 um skived fins with improved heat transfer.

facts.text: ToffeeX announced a partnership with Excel3D (23 January 2026) to advance physics-driven generative design in India, extending the reach of its software for thermo-fluid component design.
ToffeeX announced a strategic partnership with CAD-IT Korea (14 January 2025) to accelerate adoption of its physics-driven generative design software in South Korea.

faq.q: What does ToffeeX design for liquid cooling?
faq.a: Its software generates GPU/CPU cold plates, direct-to-chip cooling, rack cooling and distribution manifolds, growing fins and channels from the chip's power and heat maps with coolant limits, flow and heat solved at every step.

faq.q: How is ToffeeX's approach different?
faq.a: It is physics-driven generative design: geometries come from governing physics with manufacturing constraints built in, not from training data. The company is a spinout of Imperial College London based in London.

faq.q: What performance results has ToffeeX published?
faq.a: A customer pilot reported 12%+ better cooling versus a skived-fin GPU cold plate; simulated comparisons include one-third the pressure drop for the same 61 C peak versus 100 um skived fins.

profiles.name: Sunbird Software
profiles.tagline: Vendor of the dcTrack data center infrastructure management (DCIM) software. For liquid-cooled facilities dcTrack offers CDU modeling and telemetry, manifold modeling and liquid port tracking, alongside monitoring the company says covers over 10 billion data points a day.
profiles.ownership: Owner not stated on sunbirddcim.com; an independent company since Legrand's 2015 purchase of Raritan's hardware businesses

productLines.name: dcTrack DCIM with liquid cooling tracking
productLines.note: CDU modeling and telemetry with manifold modeling and liquid port tracking for liquid-cooled racks, within a DCIM suite the company says monitors over 10 billion data points a day across power and environmental sensors.

productLines.name: Liquid cooling knowledge base and glossary
productLines.note: Educational content covering direct-to-chip, immersion and rear-door liquid cooling, CDU/manifold operation, coolant challenges (leaks, retrofit, disposal) and reference glossary definitions for liquid cooling infrastructure.

facts.text: Sunbird released dcTrack 9.3.5 on 6 July 2026, a release whose feature list includes tracking and modeling of liquid cooling infrastructure in the DCIM platform.

Sunbird published its liquid cooling 101 guide (12 January 2024) covering direct-to-chip, immersion and rear-door liquid cooling, components such as coolants, heat exchangers and pumps, and challenges including leaks, retrofit complexity and coolant disposal.

faq.q: How does Sunbird's DCIM support liquid cooling?
faq.a: dcTrack provides CDU modeling and telemetry, manifold modeling and liquid port tracking, and the company says its monitoring handles over 10 billion data points a day from power and environmental sensors.

faq.q: What was added in dcTrack 9.3.5?
faq.a: Released 6 July 2026, dcTrack 9.3.5 includes tracking and modeling of liquid cooling infrastructure among its features.

faq.q: Where is Sunbird Software located?
faq.a: The company's About page lists its address as 30 Knightsbridge Road, Suite 620, Piscataway, NJ 08854, USA.

profiles.name: Southland Industries
profiles.tagline: US MEP engineering and construction firm founded in 1949 with over 40 GW of data center capacity constructed, spanning advanced liquid cooling strategies for AI facilities: proprietary liquid-cooled rack designs for two 6 MW data vaults in Hillsboro, Oregon and a 24 MW waterless-cooled facility in Irving, Texas.
profiles.ownership: No parent stated; its history page records a 2019 shift to a C corporation to expand employee ownership

productLines.name: Data center MEPF engineering with liquid cooling
productLines.note: Scalable MEPF design including airflow modeling, heat load analysis and advanced liquid cooling strategies, with direct-to-chip liquid cooling cited for AI facilities; the firm lists over 40 GW of capacity constructed.

productLines.name: Proprietary liquid-cooled racks and modular pipe racks
productLines.note: Proprietary liquid-cooled rack designs supporting two 6-megawatt data vaults for a confidential client in Hillsboro, Oregon, using modular secondary pipe rack assemblies engineered for repeatable fabrication, with production spread across five shops nationwide.

productLines.name: Prefabrication, modular construction and energy optimization
productLines.note: BIM/VDC-driven fabrication, prefabrication and modular construction, plus power, cooling and water optimization modeling for both air-cooled and liquid-cooled data centers.

facts.text: Southland reported (31 July 2026) that as design-build partner for a confidential client in Hillsboro, Oregon it engineered and delivered proprietary liquid-cooled rack designs supporting two 6-megawatt data vaults, with modular secondary pipe rack assemblies produced across five shops nationwide.

Southland completed work in January 2025 on the 24 MW Edged data center in Irving, Texas, whose ThermalWorks waterless cooling system supports densities up to 200 kW per rack with plug-and-play liquid cooling.

faq.q: What liquid cooling systems has Southland delivered?
faq.a: In Hillsboro, Oregon it delivered proprietary liquid-cooled rack designs supporting two 6-megawatt data vaults, and it completed work on the 24 MW Edged Irving, Texas facility whose ThermalWorks waterless cooling supports up to 200 kW per rack with plug-and-play liquid cooling.

faq.q: What services does Southland provide for liquid-cooled data centers?
faq.a: MEPF design with airflow modeling, heat load analysis and advanced liquid cooling strategies including direct-to-chip for AI facilities, plus prefabrication, modular construction, and power, cooling and water optimization modeling for air- and liquid-cooled sites.

faq.q: How much data center capacity has Southland built?
faq.a: The firm states it has constructed over 40 GW of capacity, and it was founded in 1949, celebrating 75 years in 2024.

profiles.name: World Wide Technology
profiles.tagline: St. Louis-based technology solutions integrator founded in 1990 with more than 14,000 employees. WWT tests liquid cooling in its Advanced Technology Center labs - experiments with two-phase direct-to-chip cooling cut CPU temperatures from 90 C to 70 C versus air cooling - and advises clients on AI-era water efficiency.

productLines.name: Advanced Technology Center liquid cooling validation
productLines.note: Tests cooling and other solutions in its ATC lab ecosystem; published experiments with two-phase direct-to-chip liquid cooling (ZutaCore cited as an example) in which CPU temperatures dropped from 90 C to 70 C compared with air cooling, addressing devices exceeding 500 W TDP.

productLines.name: Sustainable IT and data center consulting
productLines.note: Sustainable IT Briefing service assessing current state, mapping systems and identifying workloads and optimization areas, alongside published research on water-efficient cooling choices for AI data centers.

productLines.name: AI water-efficiency research
productLines.note: October 2025 research on data center water use covering direct-to-chip cold plates, single- and dual-phase immersion and closed-coupled cooling as levers to reduce water consumption in AI infrastructure.

facts.text: WWT published research (21 October 2025) on the water challenge of AI infrastructure, covering direct-to-chip, immersion and closed-coupled cooling as water-reduction levers and noting data center water use in Virginia's Data Center Alley rose nearly 66% from 2019 to 2023.

WWT Research (22 September 2023) documented Advanced Technology Center experiments with two-phase direct-to-chip liquid cooling - citing ZutaCore's liquid-to-vapor approach - in which CPU temperatures dropped from 90 C to 70 C compared with air cooling.

faq.q: What liquid cooling work does WWT perform?
faq.a: WWT tests liquid cooling in its Advanced Technology Center labs; its experiments with two-phase direct-to-chip cooling, citing ZutaCore as an example, dropped CPU temperatures from 90 C to 70 C compared with air cooling.

faq.q: Does WWT advise on data center water use?
faq.a: Yes. Its October 2025 research covers direct-to-chip, immersion and closed-coupled cooling as water-reduction options, and notes Data Center Alley water use rose nearly 66% from 2019 to 2023.

faq.q: How large is WWT and where is it based?
faq.a: WWT is headquartered in St. Louis and reports more than 14,000 employees and more than 35 years of experience.

profiles.name: Valicor
profiles.tagline: US environmental services company (founded 1982, headquartered in Monroe, Ohio, owned by Pritzker Private Capital) that collects, transports, treats and disposes of the liquid waste liquid-cooled data centers generate: commissioning flushwater, glycol fluids, hydrotest water and chemical cleaning wastewater.

productLines.name: Data center commissioning flushwater services
productLines.note: Bulk tanker transport and wastewater treatment for mechanical, chilled-water and closed-loop flushwater containing sediment, pipe scale, rust, oils and suspended solids, with phased or scheduled hauling aligned to commissioning timelines.

productLines.name: Glycol and chiller loop waste management
productLines.note: Handles propylene and ethylene glycol wastewater, dilute flushwater, concentrated drain-downs, off-spec cooling fluid and rinse water containing glycol or inhibitors, plus ongoing post-commissioning service such as glycol replacement and blowdown.

productLines.name: Hydrotest and chemical cleaning wastewater
productLines.note: Evaluation, transport and treatment of hydrotest/pressure-test water when onsite discharge is not suitable, and profiling of chemical cleaning streams containing detergents, corrosion inhibitors, passivation chemicals, biocides and metals.

productLines.name: Emergency and high-volume wastewater response
productLines.note: Nationwide data center support including vacuum trucks, high-volume hauling, multi-truck projects, overflow and stormwater response, and after-hours service, backed by a fleet of 250+ trucks across 30+ locations in 16 states.

facts.text: As documented on its 2025-26 data center services pages, Valicor operates a nationwide liquid-waste program for liquid-cooled data centers spanning cooling water, glycol and chiller loop waste, commissioning flushwater, hydrotest water, chemical cleaning wastewater and cooling tower blowdown.
On 24 March 2026 Valicor announced the acquisition of the Pittsburgh-area wastewater treatment and industrial oil operations of Petromax LTD, expanding its network to 32 facilities across 16 states.

faq.q: What does Valicor do for liquid-cooled data centers?
faq.a: It collects, transports, treats and disposes of commissioning flushwater, propylene and ethylene glycol fluids, hydrotest water and chemical cleaning wastewater, with hauling phased to commissioning schedules plus ongoing glycol replacement and blowdown service.

faq.q: How large is Valicor's operation?
faq.a: The company states it has 30+ locations in 16 states, a 250+ truck fleet, and recycles 300+ million gallons of wastewater per year.

faq.q: Who owns Valicor and when was it founded?
faq.a: Valicor was founded in 1982 and acquired by Pritzker Private Capital in 2019; its corporate offices are in Monroe, Ohio, USA.

profiles.name: Stockholm Exergi
profiles.tagline: Stockholm district heating utility that buys waste heat from data centers: through Open District Heating and Stockholm Data Parks, data halls are cooled with heat pumps so excess heat feeds the roughly 3,000 km district heating network - currently heating 11,000 apartments with recovered excess heat.
profiles.ownership: Stockholm Exergi Holding AB is owned 50/50 by Stockholms Stadshus AB (City of Stockholm) and Ankhiale Bidco AB

productLines.name: Open District Heating
productLines.note: Heat-recovery marketplace in which Stockholm Exergi buys excess heat from data centers, supermarkets and industry; data halls are cooled with one or more heat pumps so the heat can be fed into the district heating network instead of being rejected via cooling towers. The utility reports currently heating 11,000 apartments with excess heat.

productLines.name: Stockholm Data Parks
productLines.note: Program launched in January 2017 together with the City of Stockholm, Stokab and Ellevio to attract large-scale data centers whose recovered heat supplies the network; supports the goal of 100% renewable or recovered district heating energy by 2030.

facts.text: Stockholm Data Parks was launched in January 2017 by Stockholm Exergi together with the City of Stockholm, Stokab and Ellevio to attract large-scale data centers and recover their heat into the district heating network.

In a 7 April 2026 post, Digital Realty stated that its Stockholm data center campus has been connected to the Open District Heating network since 2015, that a heat-pump investment in its STO6 data center improves the yield of reusing excess heat, and that more than 30 data centers are collaborating in the scheme.

faq.q: How does Stockholm Exergi use data center heat?
faq.a: Through Open District Heating, data halls are cooled with one or more heat pumps so excess heat feeds the district heating network; the utility reports currently heating 11,000 apartments with recovered excess heat.

faq.q: What is Stockholm Data Parks?
faq.a: A program launched in January 2017 with the City of Stockholm, Stokab and Ellevio to attract large-scale data centers whose recovered heat supplies Stockholm's district heating.

faq.q: Who owns Stockholm Exergi?
faq.a: The company states it is owned by the City of Stockholm and Ankhiale, and provides heat to over 800,000 Stockholmers across roughly 3,000 km of district heating pipes.

profiles.name: Sudlows
profiles.tagline: UK data centre design and build firm founded in 2014 and headquartered in Manchester, with over 100 data centre projects across 20 countries; delivery partner for NTT's first production liquid immersion and direct contact liquid cooling deployment in India. Kent plc acquired Sudlows Consulting in February 2025.
profiles.ownership: Kent plc acquired Sudlows Consulting on 25 February 2025 and presents its heritage under the Kent Data Centres brand

productLines.name: Data centre design and build
productLines.note: Data centre audit, design and build, testing and commissioning, and maintenance; Kent lists full in-house MEP and CSA design, 3D modelling, BIM and CFD, and Tier design expertise for its data centre business.

productLines.name: Liquid cooling deployment engineering
productLines.note: Design and engineering partner (alongside Dell and client PhonePe) for NTT's conversion of a conventionally cooled facility at Navi Mumbai to liquid immersion cooling (LIC) and direct contact liquid cooling (DCLC).

productLines.name: Sustainability and commissioning services
productLines.note: Commissioning authority and management, performance analytics and lifecycle benchmarking; listed sustainability capabilities include water-free operation and LEED Silver and Gold certified projects.

facts.text: Kent plc announced on 25 February 2025 that it had completed the acquisition of Sudlows Consulting, entering the data centre engineering market; its release describes the firm as established in 2014 with over 100 data centre projects across 20 countries.

NTT announced (25 January 2023) the first production deployment of liquid immersion cooling and direct contact liquid cooling in India at its Navi Mumbai data center, a 4.8 MW facility on the Mahape campus planned to reach up to 150 MW of IT load, with Sudlows among the delivery partners alongside Dell and client PhonePe; the technologies are up to 30% more energy efficient than conventional cooling.

faq.q: What is Sudlows' liquid cooling track record?
faq.a: Sudlows was a design and engineering partner for NTT's Navi Mumbai deployment of liquid immersion cooling and direct contact liquid cooling, announced 25 January 2023 as the first production deployment of these technologies in India and up to 30% more energy efficient than conventional cooling.

faq.q: Who owns Sudlows today?
faq.a: Kent plc completed its acquisition of Sudlows Consulting on 25 February 2025 and presents the consultancy's heritage under its Kent Data Centres brand; the release describes the firm as established in 2014 with over 100 data centre projects across 20 countries.

faq.q: What services does the company provide?
faq.a: Data centre audit, design and build, testing and commissioning, and maintenance, with full in-house MEP and CSA design, 3D modelling, BIM and CFD, Tier design expertise, and commissioning management and performance analytics.

faq.q: Where is the company headquartered?
faq.a: The head office is Ducie Works, 107 Hulme Hall Lane, Manchester, M40 8HH, United Kingdom.
